{{short description|American actress and singer}} {{Use mdy dates|date=May 2019}} {{Infobox person | name = AJ Michalka | image = AJ Michalka - portrait 2019.jpg | caption = Michalka at WonderCon in 2019 | birth_name = Amanda Joy Michalka | birth_date = April 10, 1991 | birth_place = [[Torrance, California]], U.S. | works = {{hlist|[[Aly & AJ discography|Discography]]|[[List of songs recorded by Aly & AJ|songs]]}} | occupation = {{flatlist| * Actress * musician * singer * songwriter }} | years_active = 2002–present | relatives = [[Aly Michalka]] (sister) | module = {{Infobox musical artist | embed = yes | genre = {{flatlist| * [[Pop music|Pop]] * [[pop rock]] * [[indie pop]] * [[synth-pop]] }} | label = {{flatlist| * [[Hollywood Records|Hollywood]] * [[AWAL]] }} | current_member_of = [[Aly & AJ]] }} }} '''Amanda Joy''' "'''AJ'''" '''Michalka''' ({{IPAc-en|m|iː|ˈ|ʃ|ɑː|k|ə}} {{respell|mee|SHAH|kə}};{{cite magazine |last=Semigran |first=Aly |date=August 14, 2009 |title=Aly Michalka, actor and musician |url=http://ew.com/article/2009/08/14/aly-michalka-actor-and-musician/ |magazine=Entertainment Weekly |access-date=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170406021040/http://ew.com/article/2009/08/14/aly-michalka-actor-and-musician/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 6, 2017}} born April 10, 1991)https://www.astro-seek.com/birth-chart/aj-michalka-horoscope is an American actress, musician and singer-songwriter who is one half of the musical duo [[Aly & AJ]] (briefly 78violet), alongside her older sister [[Aly Michalka]]. In addition to her music career, Michalka has appeared in films such as ''[[The Lovely Bones (film)|The Lovely Bones]]'' (2009), ''[[Secretariat (film)|Secretariat]]'' (2010), ''[[Super 8 (2011 film)|Super 8]]'' (2011), ''[[Grace Unplugged]]'' (2013), ''[[Weepah Way for Now]]'' (2015), and ''[[Support the Girls]]'' (2018). Michalka also starred in the [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] sitcom ''[[The Goldbergs (2013 TV series)|The Goldbergs]]'' (2013–2023) and its spin-off series ''[[Schooled (TV series)|Schooled]]'' (2019–2020), and she voiced a lead role as [[Catra]] in the [[Netflix]] animated adventure series ''[[She-Ra and the Princesses of Power]]'' (2018–2020).{{cite web|url=http://ew.com/tv/2018/05/18/she-ra-netflix-cast-photo-reveal/|title=She-Ra gets a makeover! A first look at the new Netflix series and meet the cast|publisher=Entertainment Weekly|access-date=May 18, 2018|archive-date=September 8, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190908180958/https://ew.com/tv/2018/05/18/she-ra-netflix-cast-photo-reveal/|url-status=dead}} ==Early life== Michalka was born in [[Torrance, California]] and is the younger sister of actress and musician [[Aly Michalka]]. Her father, Mark, owns a contracting company, and her mother, Carrie, is a musician and performed with the [[Christian rock]] band "JC Band". Her parents are divorced. As a little girl, she briefly lived in [[Seattle]] and [[Milwaukee]].{{cite news |url= http://www.accessmylibrary.com/coms2/summary_0286-15872042_ITM |title=Article: Pop sisters: Better known for their acting, Aly and AJ leap onto music... | AccessMyLibrary – Promoting library advocacy |publisher=AccessMyLibrary |date=July 7, 2006 |access-date= May 11, 2010 | first=Scooby | last=Axson}}{{Cite news|title=Tweenage Riot |publisher=Blender Magazine |date=May 23, 2006 |url=http://www.blender.com/guide/68270/tweenage-riot.html |access-date=September 24, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100628134130/http://www.blender.com/guide/68270/tweenage-riot.html |archive-date=June 28, 2010 }} Both she and her sister attended Mack Elementary. She has played the piano since she was six and started playing the guitar in her early life. She started acting when she was five, mostly in church play productions. She was raised as a [[Christians|Christian]] and homeschooled for part of her childhood.{{cite web |url=http://www.christianitytoday.com/music/interviews/2005/alyandaj-1105.html |title=78 Violet, 11/05 – Interviews – Christian Music Today |publisher=Christianitytoday.com |access-date=May 11, 2010 |archive-date=September 11, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090911162250/http://www.christianitytoday.com/music/interviews/2005/alyandaj-1105.html |url-status=dead }}{{cite web|url=http://www.blender.com/guide/articles.aspx?id=1937 |title=Tweenage Riot Article on Blender |publisher=Blender.com |date=May 23, 2006 |access-date=November 10, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081218214041/http://www.blender.com/guide/articles.aspx?id=1937 |archive-date=December 18, 2008 }}[http://www.christianitytoday.com/tc/2007/001/12.52.html Grounded in Faith – Today's Christian] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070615204540/http://www.christianitytoday.com/tc/2007/001/12.52.html |date=June 15, 2007 }} Michalka was in a number of [[musical theatre|musical productions]] at her school in [[Milwaukee]] as a young woman. She plays a variety of [[musical instrument|instruments]] such as [[Steel-string acoustic guitar|acoustic guitar]], electric guitar, and piano. ==Career== [[File:Amanda Joy (AJ) Michalka - September 2007.jpg|right|thumb|Michalka performing in 2007]] Michalka started work in entertainment in the 2000s, when she was a model for [[Trade literature|catalogs]]. In 2006, she made her [[Disney Channel]] debut in the [[Disney Channel Original Movie]] ''[[Cow Belles]]'', as "Courtney Callum", along with sister Aly, as "Taylor Callum". She has also appeared on shows such as ''[[Oliver Beene]]'', ''[[Six Feet Under (TV series)|Six Feet Under]]'', ''[[The Guardian (TV series)|The Guardian]]'', and ''[[General Hospital]]''.{{cite journal |url=http://www.christianitytoday.com/music/interviews/2005/alyandaj-1105.html |title=Away from the Rush |journal=[[Christianity Today]] |date=November 14, 2005 |access-date=May 11, 2010 |first=Andy |last=Argyrakis |archive-date=September 11, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090911162250/http://www.christianitytoday.com/music/interviews/2005/alyandaj-1105.html |url-status=dead }} She and her sister appeared in the MTV film ''[[Super Sweet 16: The Movie]].'' In 2009, she was featured in the [[Peter Jackson]] film ''[[The Lovely Bones (film)|The Lovely Bones]]'', released widely on January 15, 2010.{{cite magazine |url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/1046856/aly-aj-writing-new-songs-plot-films |title=Aly & AJ Writing New Songs, Plot Films |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |date=January 10, 2008 |access-date=February 17, 2019 |publisher=Brightspot |first=Gary |last=Graff}} From 2009 to 2013, Michalka and her sister performed as the musical duo [[78violet]]. They decided to change their band name back to "Aly and AJ" in 2015. She was cast as a [[recurring character]] on [[The CW]] series ''[[Hellcats]]''{{cite web |first=Maria |last=Valiente |url=http://www.wetpaint.com/hellcats/articles/hellcats-star-aly-michalka-reveals-ajs-characters-name |title=Hellcats Star Aly Michalka Reveals AJ's Character's Name! |work=[[Wetpaint.com]] |date=January 20, 2011 |access-date=March 28, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120318115813/http://www.wetpaint.com/hellcats/articles/hellcats-star-aly-michalka-reveals-ajs-characters-name |archive-date=March 18, 2012 |url-status=live }} starring [[Ashley Tisdale]] and her sister Aly Michalka. The series ran for one season and was cancelled in May 2011. Michalka appeared in the 2011 film ''[[Super 8 (2011 film)|Super 8]]'', directed by [[J. J. Abrams]]. Her first big-screen starring role was as the title character in 2013's ''[[Grace Unplugged]]''. Since 2013, Michalka has had a recurring role on the ABC sitcom ''[[The Goldbergs (2013 TV series)|The Goldbergs]]'' as Lainey Lewis, the best friend of main character Erica Goldberg and one-time girlfriend of Erica's brother, Barry. In May 2015, it was announced that she was promoted to series regular for the show's upcoming third season.{{cite journal |url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/goldbergs-aj-michalka-series-regular-796555|title='The Goldbergs' Promotes AJ Michalka to Series Regular |date=May 18, 2015 |journal=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |access-date=June 7, 2015 |first=Lesley |last=Goldberg }} She also played the Lainey character in a lead role on the spinoff series ''[[Schooled (TV series)|Schooled]]'', which ran for two seasons. In July 2014, she and her sister filmed an untitled drama in [[Laurel Canyon]], California. The film was directed and written by Aly's husband, Stephen Ringer. Michalka was one of the producers of the film, with her sister and Ringer, and participated in the casting process. In May 2015, it was announced that the film, ''[[Weepah Way for Now]]'', would premiere at the [[Los Angeles Film Festival]] on June 16, 2015. The film was released on DVD, iTunes, and other streaming platforms in June 2016.{{cite journal |url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/2015-los-angeles-film-festival-793617 |title=Los Angeles Film Festival Unveils Lineup |date=May 5, 2015 |journal=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |access-date=June 7, 2015 |first=Gregg |last=Kilday}} Starting in 2015, Michalka voiced the character [[Stevonnie]] in ''[[Steven Universe]]'', a fusion of the protagonist Steven and his best friend Connie. In 2024, Michalka competed in [[The Masked Singer (American TV series) season 12|season twelve]] of ''[[The Masked Singer (American TV series)|The Masked Singer]]'' as "Strawberry Shortcake", with [[Hayley Orrantia]] (who competed in [[The Masked Singer (American TV series) season 7|season seven]] as "Ringmaster") serving as her Mask Ambassador. She was eliminated in the semi-finals and finished in third place. Michalka also made references to her nephew and Aly & AJ's upcoming album.{{cite web |last=Schneider |first=Michael |date=December 11, 2024 |title=''The Masked Singer'' Reveals Identity of Strawberry Shortcake: Here Is the Celebrity Under the Costume |url=https://variety.com/2024/tv/news/the-masked-singer-season-12-episode-11-recap-aj-michalka-strawberry-shortcake-1236246491/ |access-date=December 12, 2024 |website=Variety}} In December 2025, it was announced that Michalka was cast in season 4 of ''[[The White Lotus]]''.{{Cite web|title=AJ Michalka and Alexander Ludwig Cast in White Lotus Season 4|url=https://www.eonline.com/news/1426331/aj-michalka-alexander-ludwig-cast-in-white-lotus-season-4|website=E! Online|date=2025-12-19|access-date=2026-01-22}} ==Personal life== In 2006, Michalka dated actor and musician [[Joe Jonas]].{{cite news |last1=Siwak|first1=Miranda |title=AJ Michalka Recalls 'Sloppy' 1st Kisses With 15-Year-Old Joe Jonas: We Were 'Inexperienced' |url=https://www.usmagazine.com/celebrity-news/news/aj-michalka-recalls-sloppy-1st-kiss-with-joe-jonas/|access-date=January 24, 2024 |work=U.S. Weekly |date=November 16, 2023}} She has confirmed that her duo's song "Flattery" was written about him.{{cite news |last1=Hautman|first1=Nicholas |title=Aly & AJ Shoot Down Theory That 'Potential Breakup Song' Is About Joe Jonas — But Confirm 'Flattery' Is!|url=https://www.usmagazine.com/entertainment/news/aly-aj-flattery-is-about-joe-jonas-not-potential-breakup-song/ |access-date=January 24, 2024 |work=U.S. Weekly |date=April 9, 2020}} Since August 2017, Michalka has been in a relationship with actor [[Josh Pence]].{{Cite Instagram|postid=CEKvoalHNki|user=iamaj|title=first date blur (3 years ago this month) thankful for this sweet man. Hardcore Wonder{{citation needed|date=September 2024}} |height = 4 ft 5 inplease do not change height or weight WWE {{cite journal|title=Tale of the Tape|journal=WWE Magazine|issue=16|page=85|date=October 2007}}{{cite web|url=http://www.wwe.com/superstars/smackdown/hornswoggle/|title=Hornswoggle|access-date=April 27, 2010|publisher=[[WWE]]|archive-date=February 26, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070226064411/http://www.wwe.com/superstars/smackdown/hornswoggle/|url-status=live}} |weight = 142 lb |billed = [[Dublin]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] |trainer = [[Ken Anderson (wrestler)|Ken Anderson]]{{cite web|url=https://www.cagematch.net/?id=2&nr=3586&gimmick=Hornswoggle|title=Wrestlers Database - Swoggle|work=CAGEMATCH}} |debut = 2004 |retired = |module={{infobox social media personality | child = yes | youtube_handle = @dylanpostl | youtube_display_name = Dylan Postl | youtube_years_active = 2006–present | youtube_genre = [[Professional wrestling]] | youtube_subscribers = 10.3 thousand | youtube_views = 688 thousand | stats_update = December, 2025 }} }} '''Dylan Mark Postl''' (born May 29, 1986) is an American [[professional wrestler]] and [[YouTuber]] best known under the [[ring name]] '''Hornswoggle'''. He is signed to [[WWE]] under a legends contract, having previously performed for the company as an in-ring competitor. Hornswoggle currently performs on the [[independent circuit]], sometimes under the tweaked name '''Swoggle'''. He is also known for his tenure in [[Impact Wrestling]]. Postl debuted in WWE in 2006, allied with [[Dave Finlay|Finlay]]. He won the [[WWE Cruiserweight Championship (1991–2007)|Cruiserweight Championship]] and was the final champion in its first stint. He was then revealed, in [[kayfabe]], to be [[Vince McMahon]]'s [[Legitimacy (family law)|bastard son]], and was exposed as the [[Anonymous Raw General Manager]] who had controlled the [[WWE Raw|Raw]] brand from June 21, 2010, to July 18, 2011. He left WWE in 2016, and competed in [[Impact Wrestling]] from 2016 to 2019. == Professional wrestling career == === Early career (2004–2006) === Postl started his career in the Fox Valley Wrestling Alliance (FVWA), under the ring name Hardcore Wonder.{{Cite web |last=Kelly |first=Ross |date=2019-09-11 |title=Hornswoggle Opens Up About Personal Details Discussed In His New Autobiography, His Future |url=https://www.wrestlinginc.com/news/2019/09/swoggle-opens-up-about-personal-details-he-discuses-in-his-659502/ |access-date=2025-06-19 |website=Wrestling Inc. |language=en-US}} In 2005, Postl appeared with [[National Wrestling Alliance]] territory NWA Wisconsin as '''"The World's Sexiest Midget" Shortstack''', where he won the NWA Wisconsin X Division Championship. He also won the SSW Tag Team Championship with Devin Diamond, from The Pretty Hott Thangs (Ryan Kross and Josh Maxim) on May 19, 2006, in Oak Creek, Wisconsin. He relinquished the title after signing a contract with [[WWE|World Wrestling Entertainment]]. === World Wrestling Entertainment/WWE (2006–2016) === ====Finlay's leprechaun and Cruiserweight Champion (2006–2007) ==== On May 26, 2006, Postl made his televised debut in [[Bakersfield, California]] on ''[[WWE SmackDown|SmackDown!]]'' as the character '''Little Bastard''', the [[leprechaun]] partner of Northern Irish wrestler [[Dave Finlay|Finlay]].{{cite web|url=http://www.onlineworldofwrestling.com/profiles/midgets/hornswoggle.html|title=Hornswoggle Profile|access-date=February 29, 2008|publisher=Online World of Wrestling|archive-date=September 7, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110907064226/http://www.onlineworldofwrestling.com/profiles/midgets/hornswoggle.html|url-status=live}} After Finlay's victory over [[Paul Burchill]], an extremely hyper, dirty, mysterious little man (Postl) in a leprechaun costume scurried out from under the ring and jumped on Burchill, laughing maniacally. Finlay pulled him off, only to slam him back down onto Burchill again and again.{{cite web|url=http://www.wwe.com/shows/smackdown/archive/05262006/mainarticle|title=Kiss Him Goodbye|author=Louie Dee|date=May 26, 2006|publisher=[[World Wrestling Entertainment]]|access-date=May 26, 2006|archive-date=December 16, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131216074743/http://www.wwe.com/shows/smackdown/archive/05262006/mainarticle|url-status=dead}} For the next few weeks, Postl continued to appear from under the ring after matches and attack Finlay's opponents. He soon became more and more aggressive and started attacking Finlay's opponents during matches, much to Finlay's dismay. At one point, he attacked Finlay, biting him when Finlay tried to stop him from attacking [[Brent Albright|Gunner Scott]].{{cite web|url=http://www.onlineworldofwrestling.com/results/smackdown/060623.html|title=WWE Friday Night SmackDown! – June 23, 2006 results|publisher=Online World of Wrestling|access-date=September 4, 2007}} Little Bastard helped Finlay win the [[WWE United States Championship]] on the July 14 episode of ''SmackDown!'' when he tossed him a [[Shillelagh (club)|shillelagh]] to knock out the champion [[Bobby Lashley]] and pick up the win.{{cite web|url=http://www.wwe.com/shows/smackdown/archive/07142006/mainarticle|title=Rey's Revenge|author=Brett Hoffman|date=July 14, 2006|publisher=[[World Wrestling Entertainment]]|access-date=July 14, 2006|archive-date=November 3, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103061513/http://www.wwe.com/shows/smackdown/archive/07142006/mainarticle|url-status=live}} On February 23, 2007, the character's name was changed to '''Hornswoggle''' on WWE's website and all references to the name "Little Bastard" were removed. The meaning of “hornswoggle” is to swindle, cheat, hoodwink, or hoax.{{cite web|url=http://dictionary.reference.com/browse/Hornswoggle|title=Meaning of Hornswoggle|publisher=Dictionary.com|access-date=September 4, 2007}} On the March 2 episode of ''SmackDown!'', Hornswoggle attacked [[John Layfield|John "Bradshaw" Layfield]] (JBL) and [[Michael Cole (wrestling)|Michael Cole]]. Afterward, Finlay intimidated Cole, warning him to refer to Little Bastard as "Hornswoggle."{{cite web|url=http://www.onlineworldofwrestling.com/results/smackdown/070302.html|title=WWE Friday Night SmackDown! – March 2, 2007 results|publisher=Online World of Wrestling|access-date=September 4, 2007}} On the March 30 episode of ''SmackDown!'', Hornswoggle helped Finlay beat [[Ken Anderson (wrestler)|Mr. Kennedy]] by performing a [[professional wrestling aerial techniques#senton bomb|senton bomb]] off a stepladder onto Kennedy, essentially copying Kennedy's move, the Kenton Bomb. ''SmackDown!'' announcers Michael Cole and JBL immediately referred to the move as the "Lepreton Bomb".{{cite web|url=http://www.wwe.com/shows/smackdown/archive/03292007/mainarticle|title=Next stop: Detroit|author=Lennie DiFino|publisher=[[World Wrestling Entertainment]]|date=March 30, 2007}} During the [[Money in the Bank ladder match]] at [[WrestleMania 23]] on April 1, Kennedy hit Hornswoggle with a Green Bay Plunge off of a ladder when Hornswoggle tried to interfere on the behalf on Finlay.{{cite web|url=http://www.wwe.com/shows/wrestlemania/23/matches/391618421|title=Mr. Kennedy wins the Money in the Bank Ladder Match|publisher=[[WWE]]|access-date=June 26, 2013}} On the April 6 episode of ''SmackDown!'', Finlay attacked Kennedy after his match and challenged him to a [[professional wrestling match types#Handicap match|handicap match]] with Hornswoggle as Finlay's partner.{{cite web|url=http://www.wwe.com/shows/smackdown/archive/04062007/mainarticle|title=Deadman rising|author=Lennie DiFino|publisher=[[World Wrestling Entertainment]]|date=April 6, 2007|access-date=April 9, 2011|archive-date=May 23, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140523032958/http://www.wwe.com/shows/smackdown/archive/04062007/mainarticle|url-status=live}} Before the match, Kennedy apologized for hurting Hornswoggle. Finlay accepted his apology and formed a team with Kennedy.{{cite web|url=http://www.wwe.com/shows/smackdown/archive/04132007/mainarticle|title=Polar opposites|author=Lennie DiFino|publisher=[[World Wrestling Entertainment]]|date=April 13, 2007|access-date=April 9, 2011|archive-date=November 3, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103053937/http://www.wwe.com/shows/smackdown/archive/04132007/mainarticle|url-status=live}} Hornswoggle won the [[WWE Cruiserweight Championship (1991–2007)|WWE Cruiserweight Championship]] after he pinned [[Jamie Noble]] in a [[Professional wrestling match types#Gauntlet match|Cruiserweight Open]] at [[The Great American Bash (2007)|The Great American Bash]] on July 22. The other participants and commentators were unaware that he was a participant in the match until the [[Referee (professional wrestling)|referee]] counted the [[Pin (professional wrestling)|pin]] and awarded him the belt.{{cite web|url=http://www.wwe.com/shows/thebash/2007/matches/42789824/|title=Hornswoggle wins a Cruiserweight Open (new champion)|date=July 22, 2007|access-date=June 10, 2012|publisher=[[World Wrestling Entertainment]]}} Hornswoggle then began a storyline [[Feud (professional wrestling)|feud]] with Noble over the belt. The next week on ''SmackDown!'', Hornswoggle retained the title when he defeated Noble by [[professional wrestling#Countout|countout]].{{cite web|url=http://www.wwe.com/shows/smackdown/archive/07272007/articles/cruisertitle|title=Irish eyes smile on Hornswoggle again|author=Louie Dee|publisher=[[World Wrestling Entertainment]]|access-date=July 27, 2007|archive-date=October 12, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071012132936/http://www.wwe.com/shows/smackdown/archive/07272007/articles/cruisertitle|url-status=live}} He attacked Noble in the following weeks by shoving a pie in his face,{{cite web|url=http://www.wwe.com/shows/smackdown/archive/08032007/mainarticle|title=Handing notice|author=Alissa Fuhrman|publisher=[[World Wrestling Entertainment]]|date=August 3, 2007|access-date=April 9, 2011|archive-date=December 31, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131231094440/http://www.wwe.com/shows/smackdown/archive/08032007/mainarticle|url-status=live}} spraying him with a [[fire extinguisher]], pushing him into [[Kane (wrestler)|Kane]] and causing him to get [[chokeslam]]med, and locking him in a large box.{{cite web|url=http://www.wwe.com/shows/smackdown/archive/08172007/mainarticle|title=Hand-slotted reprisal|author=Alissa Fuhrman|publisher=[[World Wrestling Entertainment]]|date=August 17, 2007}} ==== Vince McMahon's illegitimate son (2007–2008) ==== [[File:Finlay and his son.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Finlay and Hornswoggle]] On the September 10 episode of ''[[WWE Raw|Raw]]'', the storyline involving [[Vince McMahon|Mr. McMahon's]] [[Legitimacy (family law)|illegitimate son]] culminated with the reveal that Hornswoggle was the illegitimate son. Hornswoggle's feud with Noble ended on the September 28 episode of ''SmackDown!'' when [[List of authority figures in professional wrestling#General managers 2|Acting General Manager]] [[Vickie Guerrero]] forced Hornswoggle to surrender the Cruiserweight Championship (which was later retired), citing that his status as Mr. McMahon's son and his diminutive stature would eventually jeopardize his well-being.{{cite web|url=http://www.wwe.com/shows/smackdown/archive/09272007/mainarticle|title=All things big and small|date=September 28, 2007|publisher=[[World Wrestling Entertainment]]|access-date=April 9, 2011|archive-date=November 13, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121113093618/http://www.wwe.com/shows/smackdown/archive/09272007/mainarticle|url-status=live}} Mr. McMahon began giving Hornswoggle matches against competitors that were much larger than him to show his son "tough love." Hornswoggle was placed into a match against [[The Great Khali]] at [[Survivor Series (2007)|Survivor Series]] on November 18. At Survivor Series, Khali defeated Hornswoggle by [[Professional wrestling#Disqualification|disqualification]] when Finlay attacked Khali on Hornswoggle's behalf, turning both Hornswoggle and Finlay [[Babyface (professional wrestling)|face]].{{cite web|url=http://www.wwe.com/shows/survivorseries/history/2007/matches/433496412/|title=Friends in low places?|access-date=November 19, 2007|publisher=[[World Wrestling Entertainment]]}} This was the first time that Finlay appeared together with Hornswoggle since the beginning of the Hornswoggle and Mr. McMahon storyline. At [[Armageddon (2007)|Armageddon]] on December 16, Finlay defeated Khali with the help of Hornswoggle.{{cite web|url=http://www.wwe.com/shows/armageddon/history/2007/matches/5546604/|date=December 16, 2007|title=Protective endeavors|author=Lennie DiFino|publisher=[[World Wrestling Entertainment]]}} On the February 18, 2008 episode of ''Raw'', Hornswoggle had a scheduled [[professional wrestling match types#Steel Cage match|steel cage match]] against his father, Mr. McMahon.{{cite web|url=http://www.wwe.com/shows/raw/archive/02182008/mainarticle|title=Outrage in a Cage|date=February 18, 2008|author=Greg Adkins|access-date=February 29, 2008|publisher=[[World Wrestling Entertainment]]|archive-date=March 30, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140330120036/http://www.wwe.com/shows/raw/archive/02182008/mainarticle|url-status=live}} During this match, Hornswoggle was whipped with a leather belt by Mr. McMahon. Finlay tried to get involved, but was attacked and handcuffed to the ring ropes by JBL. Mr. McMahon left the ring and allowed JBL to beat up Hornswoggle while an enraged Finlay watched. failed to win. ==== Association with D-Generation X (2009–2010) ==== {{Main|D-Generation X}} On April 15, 2009, Hornswoggle was drafted to the Raw brand, without Finlay, as part of the [[2009 WWE draft#Supplemental Draft|2009 Supplemental Draft]].{{cite web|url=http://www.wwe.com/shows/raw/2009draft/2009supplementaldraftresults/|title=2009 WWE Supplemental Draft results|date=April 15, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161225191133/http://www.wwe.com/shows/raw/2009draft/2009supplementaldraftresults/|url-status=live}} Hornswoggle then entered into a feud with [[Chavo Guerrero Jr.|Chavo Guerrero]], in which they competed in a series of comedy [[gimmick (professional wrestling)|gimmick]] matches each week determined by the weekly Guest Host for ''Raw'' (Texas Bullrope Match, Blindfold Match, Falls Count Anywhere, etc.). The program began on the July 7 episode of ''[[WWE Superstars|Superstars]]'' and continued on to ''Raw''. Hornswoggle won every match in this feud. Hornswoggle's next storyline began the October 26 episode of ''Raw'', when after several weeks of wearing [[D-Generation X]] (DX) clothing, Hornswoggle received legal notification that he was no longer allowed to wear it. Later on in the night, he got his revenge by helping the ''Raw'' guest hosts, [[Kyle Busch]] and [[Joey Logano]], put DX against each other and [[John Cena]] for the [[WWE Championship]] at [[Survivor Series (2009)|Survivor Series]] on November 22. On the December 21 episode of ''Raw'', Hornswoggle tried pressing charges against DX for assault on him, but later dropped them when DX agreed to make him DX's official mascot. On the January 18, 2010, episode of ''Raw'' backstage, Hornswoggle and Triple H confronted [[Big Show]], The Miz and [[Jon Heder]]. Triple H made the match a six-man tag team match: DX and Hornswoggle against Big Show, The Miz and Heder which ended after Hornswoggle pinned Heder. ==== Brand switches and Anonymous Raw General Manager (2010–2011) ==== [[File:Hornswoogle WrestleMania Axxess 2015 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Hornswoggle in 2015]] As part of the [[2010 WWE draft#supplemental draft|2010 WWE Supplemental Draft]] on WWE.com, Hornswoggle was drafted back to the SmackDown brand. On October 8 episode of ''SmackDown'', Hornswoggle was named the official mascot for the SmackDown team at [[Bragging Rights (2010)|Bragging Rights]]. On the July 9, 2012, episode of ''Raw'', Hornswoggle was revealed as the [[Anonymous Raw General Manager]], who previously ran the brand from June 2010 to July 2011. On the season premiere of ''[[WWE NXT|NXT Redemption]]'', Hornswoggle was revealed as the pro for [[Titus O'Neil]].[http://www.wwe.com/shows/raw/archive/02142011/mainarticle The Rock has come back]. WWE.com (February 14, 2011). Retrieved on February 15, 2013.[http://www.wwe.com/shows/raw/photos/17009778/17010428/ Valentine's Day Kiss Cam] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110629055942/http://www.wwe.com/shows/raw/photos/17009778/17010428/ |date=June 29, 2011 }}. WWE.com (February 11, 2013). Retrieved on February 15, 2013. After their tag team victory over [[Darren Young]] and Chavo Guerrero, Young attacked O'Neil. They later had a match against each other which Hornswoggle won. Hornswoggle was later confronted by O'Neil's previous NXT mentor, [[Zack Ryder]]. Ryder lured Titus out of the ring by pretending to attack Hornswoggle, but he quickly re-entered the ring and ambushed Titus as he climbed back in, cementing the victory. Weeks later, Hornswoggle was sent gifts from a secret admirer, assuming it to be [[Maryse Ouellet|Maryse]]. He responded by giving her gifts, only to be shot down. On July 26, [[AJ Lee]] revealed herself as the admirer by kissing him. AJ then accompanied Hornswoggle on both ''NXT'' and ''SmackDown''. Sometime later, Hornswoggle became jealous of O'Neil hugging AJ and eventually sent her a letter ending their relationship, as he no longer wanted to be on ''NXT'' and preferred to stay on ''SmackDown''. ==== Various alliances final storylines and departure (2011–2016) ==== On November 29, 2011, holiday edition of ''SmackDown'', Hornswoggle won a battle royal, by lastly eliminating [[Sheamus]], to receive a wish from Santa Claus ([[Mick Foley]]). With help from Sheamus, Hornswoggle wished for the ability to verbally communicate. With this ability, Hornswoggle became the special guest ring announcer for the [[David Otunga]] and Sheamus match on the following week's ''SmackDown''. On January 6, 2012, episode of ''SmackDown'' he defeated [[Heath Slater]] in an Over-the-Top Rope Challenge. Later that month, Hornswoggle formed an alliance with [[Justin Gabriel]], feuding with the former Intercontinental Champion [[Cody Rhodes]] and Heath Slater, he also accompanied Gabriel to the ring at the [[Elimination Chamber (2012)|Elimination Chamber]] pay-per-view in a losing effort against [[WWE United States Championship|United States Champion]] [[Jack Swagger]]. On March 23 episode of ''SmackDown'', Hornswoggle was added to [[Theodore Long]]'s [[WrestleMania XXVIII]] team as its personal mascot.{{cite web |url=http://www.wwe.com/shows/smackdown/2012-03-23/results/page-5|title=Zack def Swagger |date=March 23, 2012 |publisher= WWE|access-date=March 18, 2012}} [[File:Funkasaurus and the Funkettes.jpg|thumb|right|Hornswoggle dancing in front of [[Naomi (wrestler)|Naomi]], [[Brodus Clay]] and [[Cameron (wrestler)|Cameron]]]] He made a return on October 12, 2012, when he was found with a [[Randy Orton]] doll. [[Ricardo Rodriguez (wrestler)|Ricardo Rodriguez]] wrecked it and continued looking for the real Orton. After a period of inactivity, he returned to ''Raw'' in November, associating himself with [[The Great Khali]] and [[Natalya Neidhart|Natalya]]. He was injured ([[kayfabe|storyline]]) by [[Big E (wrestler)|Big E Langston]] on January 11, 2013, episode of ''SmackDown'', after Khali and Natalya lost to [[Dolph Ziggler]] and [[AJ Lee]]. He returned on March 17 episode of ''Raw'', to celebrate [[St. Patrick's Day]], only to be interrupted by [[Wade Barrett|Bad News Barrett]]. On the April 15, 2014, episode of ''[[WWE Main Event|Main Event]]'', Hornswoggle turned [[Heel (professional wrestling)|heel]] after revealing himself as the mascot for [[3 Man Band|3MB]] (Heath Slater, [[Drew McIntyre]] and [[Jinder Mahal]]). In the following months, he faced [[Mascarita Dorada|El Torito]] numerous times, losing a [[Tables, Ladders, and Chairs match|WeeLC match]] at [[Extreme Rules (2014)|Extreme Rules]] (Postl says this was the best match of his career{{cite web|url=http://411mania.com/wrestling/hornswoggle-says-el-torito-match-is-best-thing-hes-ever-done/|title=Hornswoggle Says El Torito Match is Best Thing He's Ever Done - 411MANIA|website=411mania.com}}) and a [[lucha libre#Luchas de Apuestas|hair match]] at [[Payback (2014)|Payback]], resulting in his head being shaved. On June 12, 2014, McIntyre and Mahal were released by WWE, and ending 3MB. In July on ''Superstars'', Hornswoggle accompanied Slater for his match with [[Adam Rose (wrestler)|Adam Rose]], and was kidnapped by the Rosebuds, who transformed him into a mini-Rose. On August 19 episode of ''Main Event'', Hornswoggle turned face once again when he joined his former rivals, [[Primo and Epico|Los Matadores]] (including El Torito), as their second valet. He donned a cow suit and was referred to as '''La Vaquita''' (meaning "the little cow"), to complement El Torito, who was dressed as a tiny bull. Los Matadores went on to be defeated by Heath Slater and Titus O'Neil.{{cite web|url=http://www.wwe.com/shows/wwemainevent/2014-08-19|title=WWE Main Event: Aug. 19, 2014}} That same week, on ''Superstars'', his name was tweaked to '''La Vaca''' (meaning "the cow"), when he teamed with El Torito to defeat Slater and O'Neil. On September 29 episode of ''Raw'', Hornswoggle reverted back to a heel and became Slater and O'Neil's (Slater-Gator) mascot, '''the Mini-Gator'''. After the breakup of Slater-Gator, Hornswoggle took time off from WWE television to undergo arthroscopic shoulder decompression surgery in March 2015. On September 28, 2015, WWE announced Hornswoggle's thirty-day suspension for violating the company's Wellness policy.{{cite web|last=Meltzer|first=Dave|title=WWE: Hornswaggle suspended|url=http://www.f4wonline.com/wwe-news/wwe-hornswaggle-suspended-198651|work=[[Wrestling Observer Newsletter]]|access-date=September 28, 2015|date=September 28, 2015}} In his 2019 autobiography, Postl claimed he had been suspended because he had been unable to produce a urine sample for a mandatory drug test within a required three-hour window, rather than for testing positive for banned substances.{{cite book |last=Postl |first=Dylan |date=2019 |title=Life Is Short and So Am I: My Life Inside, Outside, and Under the Wrestling Ring |publisher=ECW Press |isbn=9781770414846}} The book contained a photo of what Postl contends was a test report for a [[hair analysis]] drug test performed on the day his suspension was announced that found no evidence of drug use. After not having made any appearances in WWE since then, Hornswoggle was released from WWE on May 6, 2016.{{cite web|url=http://www.wwe.com/article/damien-sandow-king-barrett-other-superstars-released|title=Damien Sandow, King Barrett, Santino Marella, Hornswoggle, Alex Riley and other Superstars released|date=May 6, 2016|access-date=May 14, 2016|publisher=WWE|archive-date=May 12, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170512215257/http://www.wwe.com/article/damien-sandow-king-barrett-other-superstars-released|url-status=live}} ====Other appearances (2018–2020)==== On April 27, 2018, Postl returned in the [[WWE Greatest Royal Rumble|Greatest Royal Rumble]] event, eliminating [[Dash Wilder]], before being eliminated himself by [[Tony Nese]].{{Cite web |last=Woodward |first=Hamish |date=January 27, 2023 |title=What Happened To Hornswoggle? Why Was The WWE Legend Fired In 2015? - Atletifo |url=https://atletifo.com/wrestling/what-happened-to-hornswoggle/ |access-date=January 28, 2023 |language=en-GB}} On January 27, 2019, Postl made an appearance at [[Royal Rumble (2019)|Royal Rumble]], chasing [[Zelina Vega]] during the Women's Rumble match. WWE contacted him to appear at Backlash 2020 in a pre-taped match between The Street Profits and Viking Raiders. Despite taping his part, his segment wasn't aired.{{cite news |title=WWE descartó recientemente unos planes para Swoogle |url=https://solowrestling.mundodeportivo.com/new/95322-wwe-descarto-recientemente-unos-planes-para-swoogle |access-date=January 11, 2021 |work=solowrestling.mundodeportivo.com |date=January 11, 2021 |language=es}} ===Independent circuit (2016–present)=== [[File:Hornswoggle 2016.jpg|thumb|After Postl's tenure in WWE, he worked in the independent circuit.]] Following his release from WWE, Postl returned to his hometown promotion ACW.{{cite web|url=https://mobile.twitter.com/ACW_Wisconsin/status/730825668959698944|title=Twitter|website=mobile.twitter.com}} Postl also signed to appear at a show co-promoted by [[Global Force Wrestling (2014–2017)|Global Force Wrestling]] and WrestlePro under the ring name Swoggle and debuted for the promotion on June 11, facing [[Curt Hawkins|Brian Myers]].{{Cite web|url=http://411mania.com/wrestling/zeb-colter-set-to-work-gfwwrestlepro-show/|title=411MANIA|website=Zeb Colter Set to Work GFW/WrestlePro Show|access-date=December 18, 2019|archive-date=June 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160604101033/http://411mania.com/wrestling/zeb-colter-set-to-work-gfwwrestlepro-show/|url-status=live}} Swoggle won after Myers knocked down the referee and while the ref was down, Grim from ''Grim's Toy Show'' interfered against Myers with a full nelson slam. Swoggle did a tadpole splash on the incapacitated Myers and won by pinfall. On July 6, [[Chikara (professional wrestling)|Chikara]] announced that Postl would be debuting for the promotion on July 23 under the ring name The Big Deal.{{cite web|url=http://www.pwtorch.com/site/2016/07/06/hornswoggle-to-chikara/|title=Hornswoggle to Chikara|date=July 6, 2016|access-date=July 7, 2016|work=Pro Wrestling Torch|archive-date=July 10, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160710132444/http://www.pwtorch.com/site/2016/07/06/hornswoggle-to-chikara/|url-status=live}} On March 30 at [[WrestleCon]], Postl, under the Swoggle ring name, defeated [[Grado (wrestler)|Grado]]. ===Total Nonstop Action Wrestling / Impact Wrestling (2016–2020)=== On the December 15, 2016, episode of ''[[Impact! (TV series)|Impact Wrestling]]'', titled [[Total Nonstop Deletion]], Swoggle made an appearance as the partner of [[Rockstar Spud]] in the Tag Team Apocalypto match. After turning on Spud in the Tag Team Apocalypto, Swoggle would square off with [[Bobby Lashley|Lashley]] and knocked himself out when he attempted a spear on Lashley. He would then appear on January 5, 2017, episode of ''Impact Wrestling'', where he would defeat Rockstar Spud, causing Spud to quit. On January 19, episode of ''Impact Wrestling'', he would then team up with [[Robbie E]] in a losing effort against [[Damien Sandow|Aron Rex]] and Spud. On April 27 episode of ''Impact Wrestling'', Swoggle was paying Rockstar Spud some attention and ruffled Spud's hair in what was intended to be an amusing gimmick with the fans - however Spud took exception to this and as he was chasing Swoggle, the situation concluded with Swoggle running up the entrance ramp, after losing his trousers (pants). Later that same show, Swoggle would viciously attack Spud using a hammer, causing unknown leg injuries. On June 1, Spud returned to ''Impact'', entering through the crowd and attacking Swoggle with a hammer, like Swoggle had done to him. On November 13, 2017, his profile was officially removed from Impact Wrestling's website confirming his departure from the company. Swoggle returned to Impact Wrestling at [[Bound for Glory (2019)|Bound for Glory 2019]] where Swoggle competed in the [[Gauntlet for the Gold|Bound for Gold gauntlet match]] which was won by [[Eddie Edwards (wrestler)|Eddie Edwards]].{{Cite web|title=Call Your Shot Gauntlet|url=https://impactwrestling.com/call-your-shot-gauntlet/|work=Impact Wrestling|date=September 30, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191021061828/https://impactwrestling.com/call-your-shot-gauntlet/ |archive-date=October 21, 2019 |access-date=December 1, 2019}}{{cite news |last1=Beaston |first1=Erik |title=Impact Bound for Glory 2019: Winners, Grades, Reaction and Highlights |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2858582-impact-bound-for-glory-2019-winners-grades-reaction-and-highlights |access-date=December 1, 2019 |work=Bleacher Report |language=en |archive-date=June 8, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210608075401/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2858582-impact-bound-for-glory-2019-winners-grades-reaction-and-highlights |url-status=live }} On October 24, 2020, Swoggle made another surprise return to Impact Wrestling at [[Bound for Glory (2020)|Bound for Glory 2020]], where he competed in the Call Your Shot Gauntlet Battle Royal, which was won by Rhyno. On the October 27 episode of ''Impact'', Swoggle helped [[Tommy Dreamer]] in defeating [[Brian Myers (wrestler)|Brian Myers]] in a [[hardcore match]] by hitting Myers with a low blow. Later, it was announced that Myers would face Swoggle in a match at [[Turning Point (2020 wrestling)|Turning Point]]. At the event he lost against Myers. On November 24, 2020, Swoggle appeared as a parody of wrestler [[AJ Styles]], and defeated [[Ethan Page]] with the help of [[Karl Anderson]].{{cite news |last1=Toro |first1=Carlos |title=The Wee-nomenal One AJ Swoggle Appears On IMPACT Wrestling, Pins Ethan Page {{!}} Fightful Wrestling |url=https://www.fightful.com/wrestling/wee-nomenal-one-aj-swoggle-appears-impact-wrestling-pins-ethan-page |access-date=November 25, 2020 |work=www.fightful.com |date=November 24, 2020 |language=en |archive-date=November 25, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201125031954/https://www.fightful.com/wrestling/wee-nomenal-one-aj-swoggle-appears-impact-wrestling-pins-ethan-page |url-status=live }} ===Ring of Honor (2019)=== Swoggle competed November 3 at ROH Unauthorized, disguised as "Mini Delirious", the tag partner of [[Delirious (wrestler)|Delirious]]. He unmasked after they lost to [[Jeff Cobb|El Jefe Cobbo]] and [[Marty Scurll|El Villainisto]], based on the match's stipulation. This was broadcast on TV on December 16. ===All Elite Wrestling (2020)=== Swoggle made a cameo on the November 18, 2020, episode of ''[[AEW Dynamite]]'' during [[The Inner Circle (professional wrestling)|The Inner Circle]]'s trip to Las Vegas.{{cite news|url=https://www.wrestlinginc.com/news/2020/11/former-wwe-star-hornswoggle-makes-cameo-appearance-on-inner-677094/|title=Former WWE Star Hornswoggle Makes Cameo Appearance On AEW Dynamite|first=Joshua|last=Gagnon|publisher=Wrestling Inc.|date=November 19, 2020|access-date=November 19, 2020}} ==Boxing== Postl made his boxing debut on April 24, 2021, at Rough n Rowdy’s event. He was defeated by Jeremy Smith.{{Cite web|url=https://solowrestling.mundodeportivo.com/new/97834-swoggle-pierde-en-su-combate-de-debut-en-el-boxeo|title = Swoggle pierde en su combate oficial de debut en el boxeo|date = April 24, 2021}} ==Autobiography== On May 1, 2018, it was announced that Postl was working on an autobiography with Ross Owen Williams, the writer of [[Hardcore Holly|Bob Holly]] and [[Al Snow]]'s autobiographies, and Ian Douglass, the writer of [[Dan Severn]] and [[Bugsy McGraw]]'s autobiographies. It was advertised that the book would "delve into the physical and emotional challenges of being a little person in both a big person's world and, often, a large person's industry, as well as charting Dylan's emotional path to parenthood, and varied relationships within his own family." The book ''Life Is Short And So Am I'' was officially released by [[ECW Press]] on September 10, 2019, and it included forewords by Postl's close friends [[Kofi Kingston]] and [[Curt Hawkins]].{{cite web|url=https://www.fightful.com/wrestling/hornswoggle-biography-being-released-2019?amp|title=Hornswoggle Biography Being Released In 2019|work=Fightful|access-date=May 1, 2018|archive-date=April 18, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220418234750/https://www.fightful.com/wrestling/hornswoggle-biography-being-released-2019?amp|url-status=live}} WWE executive [[Stephanie McMahon]] posted her support for the book on Twitter on the day of its release.{{Cite web| url=https://www.ewrestlingnews.com/news/stephanie-mcmahon-promotes-hornswoggles-new-book-and-more| title=Stephanie McMahon Promotes Hornswoggle's New Book, and More| date=September 10, 2019| access-date=September 26, 2019| archive-date=April 12, 2022| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220412192152/https://www.ewrestlingnews.com/news/stephanie-mcmahon-promotes-hornswoggles-new-book-and-more| url-status=live}} The book also received a public endorsement from [[Dolph Ziggler]].{{Cite web|url = https://www.ewrestlingnews.com/news/lacey-evans-continues-to-hate-on-canada-ziggler-praises-hornswoggles-book|title = Lacey Evans Continues to Hate on Canada, Ziggler Praises Hornswoggle's Book|date = September 23, 2019|access-date = September 26, 2019|archive-date = January 18, 2021|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210118034736/https://www.ewrestlingnews.com/news/lacey-evans-continues-to-hate-on-canada-ziggler-praises-hornswoggles-book|url-status = live}} == Film == Postl starred in the film ''[[Leprechaun: Origins]]'', a reboot of the [[Leprechaun (franchise)|Leprechaun film series]]. '''Jordan Todosey''' ({{IPAc-en|'|t|Q|d|@|s|i}} {{respell|TOD|ə|see}}, born February 8, 1995{{Citation needed|date=July 2026}}) is a Canadian actress. She is known for her role as [[Adam Torres (Degrassi: The Next Generation)|Adam Torres]],<ref name=":1" /> the first [[transgender]] character on the long-running TV series ''[[Degrassi: The Next Generation]]'', and as Lizzie McDonald on ''[[Life with Derek]]''. More recently,{{When|date=July 2026}} Todosey has released music under the alias 'odditie'.<ref>{{Cite web |title=odditie |url=https://open.spotify.com/artist/4WAWhK5ppH2ZGmRNV558JU |access-date=2024-10-06 |website=Spotify |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Todosey was born and raised in [[Toronto|Toronto, Ontario]], Canada and began working as a child actor at a young age, making appearances in series such as ''[[Instant Star]]'' (2004–2008), ''[[Life with Derek]]'' (2005–2009) and ''[[Flashpoint (TV series)|Flashpoint]]'' (2008–2012)''.''{{Citation needed|date=July 2026}}

== Career ==
=== ''Degrassi'' ===
Todosey is perhaps best known for playing a transgender character, Adam Torres, in the [[Degrassi (franchise)|''Degrassi'' franchise]], becoming the first actor to portray a transgender character in the show's 30-year history. Her portrayal of matters involving [[Violence against transgender people|transphobic violence]], [[coming out]], and [[gender transition]]ing received praise by audiences and [[LGBT|LGBT+]] organizations.<ref name=":1">{{Cite magazine |last=Busis |first=Hillary |date=October 25, 2012 |title='Degrassi': We interview creator Linda Schuyler before ep 300 airs |url=http://www.ew.com/article/2012/10/25/degrassi-300th-episode-linda-schuyler |access-date=2016-06-25 |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2010-07-15 |title='Degrassi' tackles transgender storyline |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/degrassi-tackles-transgender-storyline-1.532722 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121021142316/http://www.ctvnews.ca/degrassi-tackles-transgender-storyline-1.532722 |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 21, 2012 |access-date=2024-03-09 |website=CTVNews |language=en}}</ref>

For her performance, Todosey won a [[Gemini Award]] in 2011, for Best Performance in a Children's or Youth Program or Series,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.geminiawards.ca/gemini26/press/GEMINI-Nominees-LIST-News-Release-Aug-3-2011.PDF |title=26th Gemini Awards Nominee List |date=3 August 2011 |publisher=Gemini Awards |access-date=17 August 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111006184115/http://www.geminiawards.ca/gemini26/press/GEMINI-Nominees-LIST-News-Release-Aug-3-2011.PDF |archive-date=6 October 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=":2">{{cite web |url=http://www.geminiawards.ca/gemini26/press/gemini-news-release-aug-31.pdf |title=2011 Gemini Awards Presented in Drama, Children's or Youth, Comedy and Variety Categories |date=31 August 2011 |publisher=Gemini Awards |access-date=1 September 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111203052552/http://www.geminiawards.ca/gemini26/press/gemini-news-release-aug-31.pdf |archive-date=3 December 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and the two-part episode "[[My Body Is a Cage]]" has also been widely recognized, including winning a [[Peabody Award]] in 2011, citing that Todosey "beautifully portrayed" a transgender character.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thestar.com/entertainment/2011/03/31/degrassi_episode_wins_peabody_award.html|title='Degrassi' episode wins Peabody Award {{!}} Toronto Star|website=thestar.com|date=31 March 2011 |access-date=2016-06-25}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.peabodyawards.com/award-profile/degrassi-my-body-is-a-cage|title=Degrassi: My Body Is A Cage|access-date=2016-06-25}}</ref>

[[Chaz Bono]], who is transgender, appeared on the show in support of Todosey's role. He invited her to meet with his group for trans teens to discuss her portrayal and to help her understanding the role. Bono stated that Todosey's character was "spot on" in the experiences of transgender people in high school and had helped one of his group members discover their own trans identity.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chaz Bono and Jordan Todosey Talk "Degrassi"'s Trans Storyline |url=https://www.logotv.com/news/tkaoq4/chaz-bono-and-jordan-todosey-talk-degrassis-trans-storyline |access-date=2024-03-09 [[Linda Schuyler]], one of the show's creators, defended the choice to kill the character, saying in a statement that Todosey's storyline "will affect even more lives in an authentic way…"<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://hollywoodlife.com/2013/08/16/degrassi-adam-dies-car-accident-season-13-episode-7-recap-video/|title='Degrassi' Shocker: Adam's Fate Revealed In Emotional Episode|last=Swift|first=Andy|date=2013-08-16|website=Hollywood Life|access-date=2016-06-25}}</ref> The executives argued that Adam's death, a result of [[texting while driving]], was an important storyline to present to audiences.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Allen |first=Joseph |date=2018-01-24 |title=17 Dark Secrets Behind Degrassi You Had No Idea About |url=https://screenrant.com/degrassi-secrets-trivia-facts/ |access-date=2024-03-09 |website=ScreenRant |language=en}}</ref>

It was also revealed that Todosey's contract had ended with the show and the actress had chosen not to renew it, leading to the death storyline.<ref name=":3" />

=== Other work ===
Todosey played Lizzie McDonald in the series ''[[Life with Derek]]'' from 2005 to 2009 and the spin-off movie ''[[Vacation with Derek]]''. She received a Best Young Ensemble Performance in a TV Series - Comedy or Drama at the [[Young Artist Award]]s for the show.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Jordan Todosey - Awards |url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1671839/awards/ |access-date=2024-03-08 |website=IMDb |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2006, Todosey portrayed Amelia in the short film Santa Baby. Her performance earned her a Best Female Performance win at the [[Yorkton Film Festival]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Yorkton Film Festival (2006) |url=http://www.imdb.com/event/ev0000715/2006/1/ |access-date=2024-03-08 |website=IMDb}}</ref>

She also appeared in one episode of ''[[Flashpoint (TV series)|Flashpoint]]''; in ''[[The Pacifier]]'' as a Firefly ([[Girl Scouts of the USA|Girl Scout]]); and in ''[[The Prize Winner of Defiance, Ohio]]'' as Tuff Ryan at 9 years old. She also voiced the main character, Willa, on the animated TV series ''[[Willa's Wild Life]]''.

In 2015, she co-starred with [[Henry Rollins]] and [[Boo Boo Stewart]] in the thriller ''[[He Never Died]]''. She appeared as Tracey in ''[[Between (TV series)|Between]].'' In 2016, she appeared in ''[[Murdoch Mysteries]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://bloody-disgusting.com/images/3335053/henry-rollins-plays-bingo-new-never-died-still-exclusive/ |title=Rollins joined on screen to He Never Died by the Twilight franchise star Boo Boo Stewart (X-Men: Days of Future Past), Kate Greenhouse (The Dark Hours), Jordan Todosey ("Degrassi: The Next Generation"), and Steven Ogg |date=31 August 2011 |publisher=Gemini Awards |access-date=1 September 2011}}</ref>

{{Short description|American actor (born 1992)}} {{about||the American college football coach|Adam Hicks (American football)}} {{Use mdy dates|date=December 2020}} {{Infobox person | name = Adam Hicks | image = Adam Hicks.jpg | image_size = | caption = Hicks in 2011 | birth_name = Adam Paul Nielson Hicks | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|mf=yes|1992|11|28}} | birth_place = [[Las Vegas]], Nevada, U.S. | occupation = {{hlist|Actor|rapper}} | net_worth = | years_active = 1999–present }} '''Adam Paul Nielson Hicks''' (born November 28, 1992){{cite web |url=http://www.disneyxdmedianet.com/web/showpage/showpage.aspx?program_id=3118750&type=hicks |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120226022635/http://www.disneyxdmedianet.com/web/showpage/showpage.aspx?program_id=3118750&type=hicks |archive-date=February 26, 2012 |title=Disney XD Medianet}} is an American actor, musician and rapper. '''Lucas Favalli''' (born 16 July 1985) is an Italian Argentine [[football (soccer)|football]] midfielder.

==Career==

===Early career===
Favalli started his career at [[Torneo Argentino A|3rd division (Interior)]] side [[Club Atlético Racing de Córdoba|Racing de Córdoba]]. He later joined [[Talleres de Córdoba]] in the [[Primera Division Argentina]] in 2002.

===Greece===
In 2006 Favalli was spotted by scouts from [[Apollon Kalamarias F.C.|Apollon Kalamarias]], and was signed by the club during the summer 2006 transfer window.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Guardian.co.uk|title=Statistics|url=http://guardian.touch-line.com/StatsCentre.asp?CTID=31&CPID=135&TEID=1505&PLID=200453&pStr=Player|accessdate=2008-12-09|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120615055408/http://guardian.touch-line.com/StatsCentre.asp?CTID=31&CPID=135&TEID=1505&PLID=200453&pStr=Player|archivedate=2012-06-15}}</ref>

From 2006 till 2013 he played for various Greek clubs both in the Greek [[Super League]] and the [[Football League (Greece)|Football League]]. His last club was [[Panetolikos F.C.|Panetolikos]] of the Football League where he signed a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=www.novasports.gr|title=Πάει Παναιτωλικό ο Φαβάλι|url=http://www.novasports.gr/podosfairo/ellada/super-league/article/135670/paei-panaitoliko-o-favali/|accessdate=8 August 2012}}</ref>

===Return to Argentina===
On 21 June 2013, after seven years in Greece, Favalli signed a one-year contract with Argentinian [[Primera B Nacional]] club [[Instituto Atlético Central Córdoba|Instituto de Córdoba]] for an undisclosed fee. In his first season, he completed 36 games and scored 9 goals.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=www.soyquemero.com.ar|title=Conociendo a Lucas Favalli |url=http://www.soyquemero.com.ar/noticias/futbol/conociendo-a-lucas-favalli.html|accessdate=7 July 2014}}</ref> As a result of his excellent performance, he signed with [[CA Huracán|Huracán]], helping the club to promote to the Argentinian [[Argentine Primera División|Primera Division]] after the play-offs.

===Return to Greece===
On 26 August 2015, Favalli signed a two-year contract with his former club [[Levadiakos F.C.|Levadiakos]] for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=www.levadiakosfc.gr|title=Η ΠΑΕ ΛΕΒΑΔΕΙΑΚΟΣ ανακοινώνει την έναρξη της συνεργασίας της με τον ποδοσφαιριστή Lucas Favalli|url=http://www.levadiakosfc.gr/?p=17756|accessdate=26 August 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|publisher=www.gazzetta.gr|title=Επίσημο και του Φαβάλι στον Λεβαδειακό|url=http://www.gazzetta.gr/football/article/792235/episimo-kai-toy-favali-ston-levadeiako|accessdate=26 August 2015}}</ref> On 21 January 2016, he signed a six months' contract with [[Super League]] rivals [[AEL Kalloni F.C.|AEL Kalloni]] on loan from Levadiakos.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=www.sdna.gr|title=Καλλονή: ανακοινώθηκε ο Φαβάλι και μπήκε στην αποστολή|url=http://www.sdna.gr/podosfairo/superleague/article/160025/kalloni-anakoinothike-o-favali|accessdate=22 January 2016}}</ref> Two days later, he scored on his debut, a 2–0 home win against [[Panthrakikos F.C.|Panthrakikos]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=www.sdna.gr|title=Kalloni win relegation battle against Panthrakikos |url=http://www.sdna.gr/news-english/article/160270/kalloni-win-relegation-battle-against-panthrakikos-vids|accessdate=23 January 2016}}</ref>

'''Roy Frank''' "'''RJ'''" '''Mitte III''' ({{IPAc-en|'|m|ɪ|t|i|}} {{respell|MIT|ee}}; August 21, 1992{{Spaced en dash space}}October 12, 2026) was an American actor and [[disability rights activist]]. Born in [[Jackson, Mississippi]], Mitte was diagnosed with [[cerebral palsy]] when he was three years old. He moved to Los Angeles in 2006 and worked with a personal [[talent manager]] to find acting opportunities where his disability could educate viewers. After playing minor roles in [[sitcom]]s, he was cast in his [[breakthrough role]] as [[Walter White Jr.]] on the [[AMC (TV channel)|AMC]] neo-Western crime drama television series ''[[Breaking Bad]]'' (2008–2013).

Mitte starred in the [[Freeform (TV channel)|ABC Family]] teen and family drama television series ''[[Switched at Birth (TV series)|Switched at Birth]]'' (2014) and the [[Netflix]] live-action/adult animated mixed media superhero television series ''[[The Guardians of Justice]]'' (2022). He appeared in ''[[Who's Driving Doug]]'' (2016), the thriller-drama ''[[Time Share (2018 film)|Time Share]]'' (2018), the independent comedy ''[[Standing Up for Sunny]]'' (2019), the thriller ''[[the Oak Room (film)|The Oak Room]]'' (2020), and the coming-of-age drama ''[[Triumph (2021 film)|Triumph]]'' (2021), the lattermost of which he executive produced.

Mitte advocated for the recognition of cerebral palsy and other disabilities. He was a [[Screen Actors Guild]] spokesman for actors with disabilities, a celebrity ambassador for [[United Cerebral Palsy]], and the president of the [[nonprofit organization]] the Mitte Foundation.<ref name="BBC Death">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cmn045en7d88o/ |title=''Breaking Bad'' actor RJ Mitte dies aged 34 |publisher=[[BBC News]] |location=[[Los Angeles]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261012210537/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cmn045en7d88o/ |archive-date=October 12, 2026 |date=October 13, 2026 |access-date=October 13, 2026 |author=Saad, Nardine}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.kbtx.com/2026/10/12/breaking-bad-actor-disability-rights-activist-rj-mitte-dies-34/ |title=''Breaking Bad'' actor, disability rights activist RJ Mitte dies at 34 |publisher=[[KBTX-TV]] |orig-date=October 12, 2026 |date=October 12, 2026 |access-date=October 13, 2026 |author=Beard, Brandy}}</ref> He received the SAG-AFTRA [[Harold Russell]] Award in 2013. Mitte died by suicide on October 12, 2026.

==Early and personal life==
Roy Frank Mitte III was born on August 21, 1992, in Jackson, Mississippi.<ref name="Vice Living">{{Cite web |date=June 9, 2020 |title=RJ Mitte of 'Breaking Bad' on Living with Cerebral Palsy |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Cc-cbcJVw00 |website=YouTube |access-date=April 10, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250425132109/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Cc-cbcJVw00&t=0 |archive-date=April 25, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://madison.com/birthday-rj-mitte/image_068cebe8-8444-11e7-a527-c371fb35595e.html | title=Birthday: RJ Mitte | date=August 18, 2017 | access-date=June 21, 2023 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230623114919/https://madison.com/birthday-rj-mitte/image_068cebe8-8444-11e7-a527-c371fb35595e.html | archive-date=June 23, 2023 | url-status=live }}</ref> He was delivered by emergency [[caesarean section]] and was not breathing at birth, which resulted in permanent [[Brain injury|brain damage]] ([[Cerebral hypoxia|hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy]]).<ref>{{cite web |title=R.J. Mitte: 'I have devoted my life to my mom and my sister' |url=https://www.smh.com.au/entertainment/celebrity/r-j-mitte-i-have-devoted-my-life-to-my-mom-and-my-sister-20190822-p52jty.html |website=www.smh.com.au |date=August 24, 2019 |access-date=November 3, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251209200752/https://www.smh.com.au/entertainment/celebrity/r-j-mitte-i-have-devoted-my-life-to-my-mom-and-my-sister-20190822-p52jty.html |archive-date=December 9, 2025 |url-status=live }}</ref> He was adopted a few weeks later by Roy Frank Mitte Jr. and Dyna Mitte, who separated when he was two months old.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last=Tumin |first=Remy |date=October 12, 2026 |title=RJ Mitte, Who Played Walter White's Son on 'Breaking Bad,' Dies at 34 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/12/arts/television/rj-mitte-dead.html |access-date=October 13, 2026 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> He was diagnosed with [[cerebral palsy]] at the age of three, and doctors put his legs in casts for six months in an attempt to straighten his feet.<ref name="Vice Living"/>

He was raised by his mother following his parents' separation, splitting time between [[Lafayette, Louisiana]], and [[Austin, Texas]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Epstein |first=Elena |date=April 6, 2015 |title=BREAKING BAD'S RJ MITTE ON GROWING UP WITH CP |url=https://www.laparent.com/special-needs-RJ-Mitte |access-date=October 12, 2026 |website=LA Parent |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260410083634/https://www.laparent.com/special-needs-RJ-Mitte |archive-date=April 10, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":2" /> After his mother became paralyzed following a car accident,<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 13, 2026 |title=What was RJ Mitte's net worth? Breaking Bad star once revealed how his manager stole his money |url=https://www.aol.com/articles/rj-mitte-net-worth-breaking-082557000.html |access-date=October 13, 2026 |website=[[AOL.com]] |language=en}}</ref> Mitte assumed financial responsibility for his family at the age of 13, which by then also included his sister, Lacianne Carriere, who had been born when he was 11. As of 2015, he remained financially responsible for both his mother and sister.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ferguson |first=Donna |date=February 17, 2016 |title=RJ Mitte: 'Breaking Bad didn't even make me a millionaire' |language=en-GB |work=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]] |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/money/fame-fortune/rj-mitte-breaking-bad-didnt-even-make-me-a-millionaire/ |access-date=April 3, 2022 |issn=0307-1235 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150601231432/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/finance/personalfinance/fameandfortune/11591741/Steve-Backshall-My-starting-pay-with-the-BBC-was-bonkers.html |archive-date=June 1, 2015 |url-status=live}}</ref> Mitte's first language was [[Spanish language|Spanish]], owing to the fact that his mother hired a monolingual babysitter to watch him while she worked.<ref>{{cite web |title=RJ Mitte's First Language Was Spanish {{!}} Breaking Bad Commentary Ep410 - Salud |url=https://www.youtube.com/shorts/oe2aeH49U8E |website=YouTube |date=January 31, 2026}}</ref>

Mitte was fitted with [[Orthotics|leg braces]] and used [[crutch]]es throughout most of his childhood. His body became stronger over time through sports and exercise, and he no longer needed walking devices by his teenage years.<ref name="CST">{{cite web|url=https://www.suntimes.com/lifestyles/23075431-423/breaking-bads-rj-mitte-talks-about-living-with-cerebral-palsy.html|title='Breaking Bad's' R.J. Mitte talks about living with cerebral palsy|first=Natasha |last=Wasinkski|date=October 10, 2013|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|access-date=January 4, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140105060504/https://www.suntimes.com/lifestyles/23075431-423/breaking-bads-rj-mitte-talks-about-living-with-cerebral-palsy.html|archive-date=January 5, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2006, he relocated to [[Los Angeles]], California, with his family after his younger sister received a job offer in a movie production.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Calabro|first1=Tina|title='Breaking Bad' actor RJ Mitte finds 'perfect role' prepared him to become an activist|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/tv-radio/2010/03/17/Breaking-Bad-actor-RJ-Mitte-finds-perfect-role-prepared-him-to-become-an-activist/stories/201003170257|access-date=October 20, 2015|work=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]|date=March 17, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151007205329/http://www.post-gazette.com/tv-radio/2010/03/17/Breaking-Bad-actor-RJ-Mitte-finds-perfect-role-prepared-him-to-become-an-activist/stories/201003170257|archive-date=October 7, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Turnquist|first1=Kristi|title='Breaking Bad' costar RJ Mitte on ability, disabilities, and filming in Portland|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/movies/2010/10/breaking_bad_costar_rj_mitte_o.html|access-date=October 20, 2015|work=[[The Oregonian]]|date=October 21, 2010}}</ref> Mitte was in a relationship with girlfriend Kennedy Suarez from 2018, having been long-term friends beforehand. He announced their engagement in October 2025.<ref>{{cite web|last=Robinette|first=Ashlyn|url=https://people.com/breaking-bad-star-rj-mitte-is-engaged-to-kennedy-suarez-exclusive-11830890|title=Breaking Bad Star RJ Mitte Is Engaged! All the Details of His Proposal to Kennedy Suarez (Exclusive)|date=October 16, 2025|access-date=October 16, 2025|website=[[People (magazine)|People]]|language=En-US}}</ref>

==Career==
[[File:Aaron Paul, Dean Norris, Anna Gunn, RJ Mitte and Betsy Brandt, May 2009 (14) (RJ Mitte).jpg|thumb|upright|Mitte at the 68th Annual [[Peabody Awards]] in 2009]]

After receiving several roles as an extra, including in the [[The Walt Disney Company|Disney]] teen sitcom ''[[Hannah Montana]]'',<ref name="HuffPost">{{Cite web |url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/2013/09/18/rj-mitte-miley-cyrus_n_3947385.html |title=RJ Mitte, Miley Cyrus Appeared On ''Hannah Montana'' Together |last=Clements |first=Erin |date=September 18, 2013 |website=[[The Huffington Post]] |access-date=September 12, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170722115347/http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2013/09/18/rj-mitte-miley-cyrus_n_3947385.html |archive-date=July 22, 2017 |url-status=live}}</ref> Mitte became interested in films and decided to take acting lessons. Shortly after, he was offered the role of [[Walter White Jr.]], a character who also has cerebral palsy, in the AMC series ''[[Breaking Bad]]''.<ref name="gazette">{{cite news |author=Tina Calabro |date=March 17, 2010 |title='Breaking Bad' actor RJ Mitte finds 'perfect role' prepared him to become an activist |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/pg/10076/1043265-67.stm#ixzz0yfZw7wEF |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100322204457/http://www.post-gazette.com/pg/10076/1043265-67.stm#ixzz0yfZw7wEF |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 22, 2010 |access-date=September 5, 2010 |work=[[The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]}}</ref> Series creator [[Vince Gilligan]] modeled the character on a friend who had cerebral palsy and used crutches;<ref name="BBC Death"/> the character used crutches to walk, though Mitte did not require them in real life by that time.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2008-mar-02-ca-mitte2-story.html |title=For once, his disability was an advantage |last=Gajewski |first=Josh |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=March 2, 2008 |accessdate=October 13, 2026 }}</ref> ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]''{{'}}s Daniel D'Addario called Mitte's performance "a breakthrough for disability representation". Mitte felt the role "set really high standards [...] that I can never meet".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2026/tv/columns/rj-mitte-walter-white-jr-breaking-bad-1236909529/ |title=''Breaking Bad'' Star RJ Mitte's Heartbreaking Performance as Walter White Jr. Was a Breakthrough for Disability Representation |last=D'Addario |first=Daniel |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=October 12, 2026 |accessdate=October 13, 2026 }}</ref>

At the 2013 Media Access Awards, Mitte received the SAG-AFTRA [[Harold Russell]] Award for his portrayal of Walter White Jr. on the series and also presented the eponymous RJ Mitte Diversity Award to deaf actor [[Ryan Lane]].<ref name="2013MAA">{{cite web |date=November 1, 2013 |title=2013 Media Access Awards |url=https://www.wga.org/content/default.aspx?id=5341 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140103072313/http://www.wga.org/content/default.aspx?id=5341 |archive-date=January 3, 2014 |publisher=[[Writers Guild of America]] }}</ref> The [[Screen Actors Guild]] named Mitte as the spokesman for actors with disabilities and he was the representative of Inclusion in the Arts and Media of Performers with Disabilities, which employs artists with disabilities.<ref>{{cite news |last=Wolfe |first=Kathi |url=http://www.itodaynews.com/2012-issues/april2012/Mitte.htm |title=For Mitte, 'Bad' Rep is Good |work=Independence Today |date=April 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303192518/http://www.itodaynews.com/2012-issues/april2012/Mitte.htm |archive-date=March 3, 2016 |access-date=February 19, 2013 |url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2011, Mitte starred in the short horror film ''Stump''.<ref name="WSU Stump"/> That same year, he worked as [[executive producer]] of the documentary ''Vanished: The Tara Calico Story'', about the [[disappearance of Tara Calico]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.indiegogo.com/TaraCalico |title=Vanished: The Tara Calico Story |website=Indiegogo |access-date=March 10, 2013 |archive-date=September 21, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921175059/http://www.indiegogo.com/projects/vanished-the-tara-calico-story |url-status=dead }}</ref> Around and after ''Breaking Bad''{{'}}s conclusion in 2013, Mitte appeared in the films ''[[House of Last Things]]'' (2013),<ref name="Influx House"/> ''[[Dixieland (film)|Dixieland]]'' (2015),<ref name="THR Dixieland"/> and as the lead character in ''[[Who's Driving Doug]]'' (2016).<ref name="THR Doug"/> He had a guest appearance on ''[[Vegas (2012 TV series)|Vegas]]'' in 2012,<ref name="THR Vegas"/> and a recurring role in ''[[Switched at Birth (TV series)|Switched at Birth]]'' in 2014.<ref name="Digital Spy Switched"/> He participated in the second series of ''[[Celebrity Island with Bear Grylls]]'' in 2017,<ref name="Radio Times Grylls"/> departing in the second episode due to the camp's disorganization.<ref name="Digital Spy Grylls"/>

[[File:Aaron Paul, Bryan Cranston, Anna Gunn, RJ Mitte & Dean Norris (42699855465).jpg|thumb|left|The cast of ''[[Breaking Bad]]'' at [[San Diego Comic-Con]] in 2018. {{abbr|L–R|Left to right}}: [[Aaron Paul]], [[Bryan Cranston]], [[Anna Gunn]], Mitte, and [[Dean Norris]].]]

Mitte modeled for a spring 2014 [[Gap Inc.|Gap]] ad campaign.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/gap-spring-campaign-2014_n_4810110|title=Gap Goes Back To Basics For Spring|first1=Chanel|date=February 18, 2014|website=[[HuffPost]]|last1=Parks|access-date=October 12, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251208123811/https://www.huffpost.com/entry/gap-spring-campaign-2014_n_4810110|archive-date=December 8, 2025|url-status=live}}</ref> He appeared on the cover of the February/March 2015 issue of ''Neurology Now'', published by the [[American Academy of Neurology]]. The issue included a short biography and his views on cerebral palsy, [[bullying]], and his acting career.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.brainhealth.com/voices/celebrity-profiles/rj-mitte-busting-cerebral-palsy-stereotypes/ |last=Childers |first=Linda |date=February 2015 |title=Breaking Good: After the role of a of Neurology]] |s2cid=147052248 |location=Minneapolis, Minnesota }}{{Cbignore}}</ref> He was also named a celebrity ambassador for [[United Cerebral Palsy]] in 2015.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celebrity Ambassadors |url=https://ucp.org/about/celebrity-ambassadors/ |access-date=June 18, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150609225117/http://ucp.org/about/celebrity-ambassadors/ |archive-date=June 9, 2015 |url-status=live}}</ref> In June 2015, he modeled on a [[fashion show]] catwalk for [[Vivienne Westwood]].<ref>{{cite magazine | last=Locker | first=Melissa | title=Breaking access-date=July 13, 2025}}</ref> In November 2015, Mitte was announced to be a presenter as part of British [[Channel 4]]'s coverage of the [[2016 Summer Paralympics|2016 Rio Summer Paralympics]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 17, 2015 |title=Breaking Bad actor RJ Mitte joins Channel 4's Paralympics presenters |access-date=January 21, 2021 |website=Channel 4}}</ref> In 2016, he appeared in the music video for "If I Get High" by English rock band [[Nothing but Thieves]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Nothing But Thieves hire 'Breaking Bad's RJ Mitte for emotional 'If I Get High' video |url=https://nbhap.com/blog/nothing-but-thieves-if-i-get-high |website=nbhap.com |date=February 10, 2016 |access-date=April 17, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250425131757/https://nbhap.com/blog/nothing-but-thieves-if-i-get-high |archive-date=April 25, 2025 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Mitte was cast in several science fiction and thriller films, including ''[[The Recall]]'' (2017),<ref name="Slant Recall"/> ''[[Time Share (2018 film)|Time Share]]'' (2018),<ref name="THR Time Share"/> and ''[[River Runs Red (film)|River Runs Red]]'' (2018),<ref name="THR River">{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/river-runs-red-trailer-taye-diggs-george-lopez-revenge-thriller-1146857/ |title=Taye Diggs, George Lopez Revenge Thriller ''River Runs Red'' Acquired by Cinedigm (Exclusive) |last=Lewis |first=Hilary |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=September 25, 2018 |accessdate=October 13, 2026 }}</ref> and he was the lead in the comedy film ''[[Standing Up for Sunny]]'' (2019), portraying a man with cerebral palsy.<ref name="SMH Sunny"/> On television, he appeared in an episode of ''[[This Close]]'' in 2018,<ref name="Paste Close"/> in two episodes of ''[[Now Apocalypse]]'' in 2019,<ref name="Deadline Apocalypse"/> and as a lead role in ''[[The Guardians of Justice]]'' in 2022.<ref name="BGR Guardians"/> Mitte played the lead characters in ''[[The Oak Room (film)|The Oak Room]]'' (2020),<ref name="Guardian Oak Room"/> ''The Unseen'' (2023),<ref name="Deadline Unseen"/> and ''[[Triumph (2021 film)|Triumph]]'' (2021), and executive-produced the latter,<ref name="Independent Triumph"/> before his role in ''[[Westhampton (film)|Westhampton]]'' (2025).<ref name="Variety Westhampton"/>

In a November 2025 interview with the ''Iced Coffee Hour'' podcast, Mitte stated that he had experienced financial difficulties after hiring a [[business manager]] who he alleged stole money intended for [[Tax|tax payments]] and provided him with [[Tax evasion|falsified tax filings]]. According to Mitte, the manager also defrauded 14 other actors, primarily elderly individuals and people with disabilities. He said that the resulting tax liabilities and interest took ten years to settle, stating: "I've paid more in taxes than I got from ''Breaking Bad''{{-"}}.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Davies |first=Matt |title=RJ Mitte 'barely saw Breaking Bad money' as financial manager left him in years of debt |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/3am/celebrity-news/rj-mitte-barely-saw-breaking-37766633 |date=October 13, 2026 |access-date=October 13, 2026 |website=[[Daily Mirror]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 13, 2026 |title=RJ Mitte's financial ordeal resurfaces following his death: 'I've paid more in taxes than I got from Breaking Bad' |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2634616/rj-mittes-financial-ordeal-resurfaces-following-his-death |access-date=October 13, 2026 |website=[[The Express Tribune]] |language=en}}</ref> 

He appeared as a lead in [[Josh Webber]]'s ''Love Me Dead'', which premiered in Germany in 2024; following changes and reshoots, it is scheduled to be released in 2026 or 2027 as ''Cassi''.<ref name="Deadline Cassi" /> Some of Mitte's final roles included ''Talking to Strangers'' and ''One Eye Open'' (both 2026), both of which he was promoting days before his death.<ref name="Variety Death" /><ref name="People Open" />
