'''Margaret Osborn''' (born 25 August 1988), known professionally as '''Alice Glass''', is a Canadian singer and songwriter. She is the co-founder and former frontwoman of the electronic band [[Crystal Castles]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Mcnett |first=Jared |title=Five songs to listen to now that Crystal Castles appear to be done |url=https://www.voxmagazine.com/music/five-songs-to-listen-to-now-that-crystal-castles-appear-to-be-done/article_19c253db-1630-5372-aa7c-b1c22cbdfa72.html |work=[[Vox (magazine)|Vox]] |date=8 October 2014}}</ref> In 2014, she embarked on a solo career.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Brandes|first1=Bertie|title=Crystal Castles' Leading Lady Alice Glass is Embracing Her Own Darkness|url=https://i-d.vice.com/en_gb/article/crystal-castles-leading-lady-alice-glass-is-embracing-her-own-darkness|work=[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]]|date=17 February 2015|access-date=29 April 2015|archive-date=28 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151128193750/http://i-d.vice.com/en_gb/article/crystal-castles-leading-lady-alice-glass-is-embracing-her-own-darkness|url-status=dead}}</ref> She released her [[Alice Glass (EP)|eponymous debut EP]] in 2017. Her solo debut album, ''[[Prey//IV]],'' was released in February 2022.

==Life and career==
===1988–2014: early life and Crystal Castles===
Alice Glass was born Margaret Osborn on 25 August 1988 in [[Toronto]], [[Ontario]].<ref>*{{cite web |last=Nelson |first=Michael |date=17 April 2015 |title=Is This Crystal Castles' New Singer? |url=https://www.stereogum.com/1795125/is-this-crystal-castles-new-singer/news |access-date=17 April 2015 |work=[[Stereogum]]}}
*[https://www.instagram.com/p/BYRokpeF1xZ/]
*{{cite web |title=Alice Glass |url=http://www.askmen.com/celebs/women/singer/alice-glass |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923222029/http://www.askmen.com/celebs/women/singer/alice-glass/ |archive-date=23 September 2015 |access-date=13 September 2015 |work=[[AskMen]]}}</ref> She was raised [[Catholic]], attending [[Catholic school|parochial school]] up until junior high.<ref>{{cite web |last=Dombal |first=Ryan |title=Interviews: Crystal Castles |url=http://pitchfork.com/features/interviews/8988-crystal-castles |work=Pitchfork |date=8 November 2012 |access-date=10 November 2015 |archive-date=8 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151108154610/http://pitchfork.com/features/interviews/8988-crystal-castles/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> At age 15, she ran away from home to live in a squat community of punks under the name [[Vicki Vale]] after the comic book character of the same name and started an [[All-female band|all-girl]] [[experimental rock|experimental punk]] band called Fetus Fatale.<ref name="Plan">{{cite web |last=Gillen| first=Kieron |title=Crystal Castles Interview |work=[[Plan B (magazine)|Plan B]] |url=http://www.planbmag.com/content/view/492/42 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080103053445/http://www.planbmag.com/content/view/492/42 |archive-date=3 January 2008 |url-status=usurped|access-date=11 June 2010}}</ref> In December 2003, she and [[Ethan Kath]] began working together on the project that would become [[Crystal Castles]].<ref name="the roots of cc"/> She picked the stage name Alice Glass based on a [[pin-back button|pin]] with the name Alice that she shoplifted and [[Love_and_Rockets_(comics)#Characters|Hopey Glass]], a character in ''[[Love and Rockets (comics)|Love and Rockets]]''.<ref>{{cite web |last=Mckenzie |first=Lesley |url=https://mag.agolde.com/2016/07/18/alice-glass |title=Alice Glass - Eighty-Nine |work=Agolde |date=18 July 2016 |access-date=15 June 2018 |archive-date=15 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180615191648/https://mag.agolde.com/2016/07/18/alice-glass |url-status=dead }}</ref>

[[File:Alice Glass C.jpg|thumb|Glass performing in 2008]]

Crystal Castles' first official release was their 2006 single "[[Alice Practice]]".<ref>{{citation |author=SoftandFading |title=Crystal Castles interview MTV Backstage Pass (Full) c. 2008|date=9 April 2015 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UAtsuWBY--A  |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/UAtsuWBY--A |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|access-date=17 April 2017}}{{cbignore}}</ref> The song got the band their first record deal with Merok Records in London.<ref name="the roots of cc">{{cite news |url=http://www.nme.com/blogs/nme-blogs/the-roots-of-crystal-castles-771776 |title=The Roots Of... Crystal Castles |date=14 March 2013 |work=[[NME]] |access-date=17 April 2017}}</ref> The same year, Crystal Castles played their first live show at Clinton's Tavern in Toronto.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://crystalcastles.com/board/index.php?topic=2134.0 |title=When and where was Crystal Castles first live performance? |website=crystalcastles.com |access-date=17 April 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170418162109/http://crystalcastles.com/board/index.php?topic=2134.0 |archive-date=18 April 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref> "Alice Practice" was eventually featured on their [[Crystal Castles (2008 album)|eponymous debut album]] released in 2008. Glass topped [[NME's Cool List|''NME''{{'}}s Cool List]] that year and responded to it by criticizing the idea of the cool list itself.<ref>{{cite web |title=Crystal Castles' Alice Glass reacts to topping 2008 Cool List |url=http://www.nme.com/news/crystal-castles/40824 |work=[[NME]] |date=4 November 2008 |access-date=21 August 2011}}</ref> The duo followed their debut album with two more critically acclaimed albums, ''[[Crystal Castles II|II]]'' (2010) and ''[[III (Crystal Castles album)|III]]'' (2012), completing a trilogy. Glass co-wrote every Crystal Castles song she contributed vocals to.<ref>{{citation |author=Dominic Amphetamine |title=Crystal Castles Interview Headlining NME Tour Alice Glass Ethan Kath |date=19 November 2016 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GK8GlvPd1VE |access-date=17 April 2017}}{{cbignore}}{{Dead YouTube link|date=February 2022}}</ref> 

In October 2014, Glass announced her departure from Crystal Castles due to her own professional and personal reasons. In the announcement, she noted that working within the band compromised her efforts towards "sincerity, honesty, and empathy for others".<ref>{{cite web |title=Crystal Castles announce their split on Twitter |url=http://www.dazeddigital.com/music/article/22102/1/crystal-castles-announce-their-split-on-twitter |website=Dazed |date=8 October 2014 |access-date=10 November 2015}}</ref> She later had a number of public disagreements with her former bandmate, including accusing him of assault and sexual misconduct.<ref>{{cite web|title=Alice Glass Responds To Ethan Kath's "Manipulative" Statements About Crystal Castles |url=http://www.stereogum.com/1795321/alice-glass-responds-to-ethan-kaths-manipulative-statements-about-crystal-castles/wheres-the-beef |work=Stereogum|date=17 April 2015 |access-date=10 November 2015}}</ref>

===2015–2017: solo singles and lawsuit===
In July 2015, Glass released her debut single as a solo artist, "[[Stillbirth (song)|Stillbirth]]".<ref name="Stillbirth">{{cite web|url=https://itunes.apple.com/us/album/stillbirth-single/id1019240410|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160314232051/https://itunes.apple.com/us/album/stillbirth-single/id1019240410|url-status=dead|archive-date=14 March 2016|title=STILLBIRTH - Single by Alice Glass on Apple Music|work=[[iTunes]]|access-date=10 August 2017|date=15 July 2015}}</ref> The release was largely an effort to increase awareness of [[Domestic violence|domestic]] and [[sexual abuse]]. Glass worked with anti-sexual assault organization [[Rape, Abuse & Incest National Network|RAINN]] to donate all proceeds from the song's revenue to aid abuse victims.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alice Glass releases first solo single, opens up about "abusive relationship" |url=https://www.factmag.com/2015/07/17/alice-glass-stillbirth-single-opens-up-about-abusive-relationship/ |work=[[Fact (UK magazine)|Fact]] |date=17 July 2015 |access-date=10 September 2020}}</ref>

In August 2017, Glass released "[[Without Love (Alice Glass song)|Without Love]]", which served as the lead single to [[Alice Glass (EP)|her eponymous debut EP]] which was released the following week.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kaye |first1=Ben |title=Alice Glass surprise releases her self-titled debut solo EP: Stream |url=https://consequence.net/2017/08/alice-glass-surprise-releases-her-self-titled-debut-solo-ep-stream/ |website=Consequence Sound |publisher=Consequence Sound |access-date=16 August 2026 |language=English |date=August 17, 2017}}</ref>

That same year, Alice Glass was added as the [[opening act]] for [[Marilyn Manson (band)|Marilyn Manson]] on the [[Heaven Upside Down Tour]] to support the [[Heaven Upside Down|album of the same name]]<ref name="NME">{{cite web |url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/alice-glass-new-video-marilyn-manson-tour-2123452 |title=Alice Glass shares video for 'Without Love', announces tour with Marilyn Manson |work=[[NME]] |last=Maine |first=Samantha |date=10 August 2017 |access-date=10 September 2020}}</ref>. However, the tour was wrought with safety issues. On September 29, during an [[encore]] performance of "[[The Beautiful People (song)|The Beautiful People]]" at the [[Stage AE]] in [[Pittsburgh]], Manson broke his ankle after jumping from the stage to sing with fans who were standing near the barricade. After the vocalist crawled back on-stage, the band abruptly abandoned the song. However, they resumed when Manson invited Glass on stage to take over vocals.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://loudwire.com/marilyn-manson-pittsburgh-show-i-just-broke-my-ankle/ |title=Marilyn Manson at Pittsburgh Show: 'I Just Broke My Ankle' |author=DiVita, Joe  |work=[[Loudwire]] |publisher=[[Townsquare Media]] |date=September 30, 2017 |access-date=October 8, 2017}}</ref>

The following night, at the [[Hammerstein Ballroom]] in New York City during a performance of "[[Sweet_Dreams_(Are_Made_of_This)#Marilyn_Manson_version|Sweet Dreams]]"<ref>{{cite magazine |url=http://ew.com/music/2017/09/30/marilyn-manson-injured-by-falling-stage-prop/ |title=Marilyn Manson injured by falling stage prop |author=Rosen, Christopher |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |date=September 30, 2017 |access-date=October 8, 2017}}</ref>, a large 750 kg – approximately 1650[[Pound (mass)|lbs]] – [[stage prop]] consisting of two oversized pistols attached via metal [[scaffolding]] fell on Manson<ref name="marilyn_manson_struck">{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2017/oct/01/marilyn-manson-struck-by-falling-stage-scenery-during-new-york-concert |title=Marilyn Manson struck by falling stage scenery during New York concert |author=Marsh, Sarah |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=October 1, 2017 |access-date=October 8, 2017}}</ref>, breaking his [[fibula]] in two places<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/marilyn-manson-on-stage-injury-the-pain-was-excruciating-w508726 |title=Marilyn Manson on 'Terrifying' Stage Injury: 'The Pain Was Excruciating' |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |date=October 13, 2017 |access-date=October 13, 2017}}</ref> and knocking the singer unconscious for 15 minutes on stage until Manson was carried out on a [[stretcher]] to a nearby hospital.<ref name="marilyn_manson_struck" /><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2017/oct/02/marilyn-manson-cancels-tour-dates-stage-prop-gun-injury |title=Marilyn Manson cancels tour dates due to stage injury |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=October 2, 2017 |access-date=October 8, 2017}}</ref>    

The following nine dates of the North American leg were immediately cancelled,<ref name="Payne">{{cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/marilyn-manson-cancel-tour-concert-date-injury-2017-7981906/ |title=Marilyn Manson Cancels Tour Dates Following Onstage Injury in New York |author=Payne, Chris |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |date=October 1, 2017 |access-date=October 8, 2017}}</ref> with the remaining October shows gradually cancelled over the next week. All of these shows – excluding festival appearances – were rescheduled for the beginning of 2018<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rte.ie/entertainment/2017/1015/912487-manson-opens-up-on-excruciating/ |title=Marilyn Manson opens up on 'excruciating' stage injury |work=[[RTÉ]] |date=October 15, 2017 |access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref>. On October 19th, Alice Glass posted on [[Facebook]] that she would not be returning to the rescheduled North American tour dates the following year, teasing her own future tour, and instead playing a show of her own at The [[North Park, San Diego#Arts, culture and cuisine|Observatory North Park]] in [[San Diego]] on October 24.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Glass |first1=Alice |title=I’ve decided that I won’t be returning for the rescheduled dates on Marilyn Manson’s tour next year |url=https://www.facebook.com/aliceglass/posts/ive-decided-that-i-wont-be-returning-for-the-rescheduled-dates-on-marilyn-manson/10154715049972136/ |website=Facebook |access-date=16 August 2026 |language=English |date=October 19, 2017}}</ref>

In October 2017, Glass posted a statement on her official website explaining her departure from Crystal Castles, and accused co-founder [[Ethan Kath]] of sexual, physical, and mental abuse. The accusations detailed that the claimed abuse started when Glass was 15 and began recording with Kath and escalated until her eventual departure from Crystal Castles.<ref>{{cite web | title=Alice Glass Statement | website=Alice Glass | url=https://www.alice-glass.com/cc/#  | access-date=9 August 2023}}</ref> Kath responded the same day in a statement issued to ''[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]]'' through his attorney, where he called the accusations "pure fiction" and said he was consulting with his lawyers as to his legal options.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pitchfork.com/news/alice-glass-accuses-crystal-castles-co-founder-ethan-kath-of-rape-and-assault |title=Alice Glass Accuses Crystal Castles Co-Founder Ethan Kath of Rape and Assault; Kath Responds |work=Pitchfork |last=Strauss |first=Matthew |date=24 October 2017 |access-date=24 October 2017}}</ref> The following month, Kath sued Glass for defamation, but this was dismissed in February 2018.<ref>
*{{cite web |url=https://www.stereogum.com/1970507/crystal-castles-ethan-kath-sues-alice-glass-for-defamation/news |title=Crystal Castles' Ethan Kath Sues Alice Glass For Defamation |work=[[Stereogum]] |last=Rettig |first=James |date=3 November 2017 |access-date=3 November 2017}}
*{{cite web|url=https://pitchfork.com/news/alice-glass-says-ethan-kaths-defamation-suit-is-dismissed |title=Alice Glass Triumphs in Ethan Kath's Defamation Suit |work=Pitchfork |last1=Strauss |first1=Matthew |last2=Minsker |first2=Evan |date=23 February 2018 |access-date=23 February 2018}}</ref> In May, Glass was awarded nearly US$21,000 in attorney fees after Kath's lawyers sought to vacate the dismissal of his defamation lawsuit against Glass.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/alice-glass-awarded-nearly-dollar21000-in-attorney-fees-after-ethan-kath-lawsuit-dismissed |title=Alice Glass Awarded Nearly $21,000 in Attorney Fees After Ethan Kath Lawsuit Dismissed |work=Pitchfork |last=Hodan |first=Marc |date=17 May 2018 |access-date=15 June 2018}}</ref>

===2018–2020: non-album single releases===
In January 2018, Glass released "[[Forgiveness (Alice Glass song)|Forgiveness]]" as the second single from her EP.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Robert Ross |first1=Alex |title=Watch Alice Glass’s Handheld Horror Video for “Forgiveness” |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/watch-alice-glasss-handheld-horror-video-for-forgiveness/ |website=Vice |publisher=Vice |access-date=16 August 2026 |language=English |date=January 11, 2018}}</ref> That month, she also released a single called "[[Cease and Desist (song)|Cease and Desist]]", which she said "is a call to arms for all survivors".<ref name="alice_glass_and">{{cite web |last1=Thiessen |first1=Brock |title=Alice Glass and Zola Jesus Team Up for "Snow Blood Tour" |url=https://exclaim.ca/music/article/alice_glass_unveils_north_american_tour |website=Exclaim! |publisher=Exclaim! |access-date=16 August 2026 |language=English |date=Feb 20, 2018}}</ref> Both singles were accompanied by music videos.<ref>{{cite web |last=Strauss |first=Matthew |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/alice-glass-new-song-is-a-call-to-arms-for-survivors-listen |title=Alice Glass' New Song Is a "Call to Arms for Survivors" |work=Pitchfork |date=23 January 2018 |access-date=15 June 2018}}</ref> 

In April 2018, Glass embarked on her SnowBlood Tour alongside American singer [[Zola Jesus]], with electronic musician [[Pictureplane]] being an [[opening act]] on select dates. The tour is named after Lady Snowblood, spurned star of the [[Lady Snowblood (film)|eponymous 1973 Japanese film]].<ref name="alice_glass_and" /> Later that month, Glass released a [[Remix album|remix EP]], consisting of remixes of songs from her [[Alice Glass (EP)|eponymous EP]] released in 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://music.apple.com/us/album/alice-glass-remixes/1372941058 |title=Alice Glass (Remixes) by Alice Glass on Apple Music |website=Apple Music |date=27 April 2018 |access-date=17 October 2018}}</ref><ref name=tinymixtapes>{{cite web |last=Kneschke |first=Tristan |url=https://www.tinymixtapes.com/news/alice-glass-release-new-remix-ep-friday-april-27-kicks-tour-week |title=Alice Glass to release new remix EP on Friday (April 27), kicks off tour this week |work=[[Tiny Mix Tapes]] |date=23 April 2018 |accessdate=17 October 2018}}</ref> The EP includes remixes from both Zola Jesus and Pictureplane.<ref name=tinymixtapes/> 

In June 2018, Glass released a new single, "[[Mine (Alice Glass song)|Mine]]", accompanied by a music video directed by Lucas David and starring American drag queen [[Violet Chachki]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.revolvermag.com/music/hear-alice-glass-brittle-soaring-new-song-mine |title=Hear Alice Glass' Brittle, Soaring New Song "Mine" |work=[[Revolver (magazine)|Revolver]] |date=15 June 2018 |access-date=15 June 2018}}</ref> 

In December 2018, Glass was featured on [[Adult Swim]]'s singles series with a new song titled "I Trusted You".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/alice-glass-new-single-i-trusted-you-2423971 |title=Listen to Alice Glass' brooding new single 'I Trusted You' |work=[[NME]] |date=21 December 2018 |access-date=3 January 2019}}</ref>

[[File:Alice Glass - Rock am Ring 2019-3520.jpg|thumb|Alice Glass live at [[Rock am Ring]] 2019]]

Throughout 2020, Alice Glass released "Nightmares" and a [[remix]] of "[[111 (Pabllo Vittar album)|Rajadão]] by [[Pabllo Vittar]] with [[experimental music|experimental]] [[record label|label]] Sermon 3 Recordings. "Nightmares" was later also re-released on [[Compilation album|label compilation album]], ''Sermon 4 Anniversary''.<ref name="rollingstone Legaspi ">{{cite web |author1=Claire Shaffer |author2=Althea Legaspi |title=Watch Alice Glass' 'Suffer and Swallow' Stop-Motion Animated Music Video |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/alice-glass-suffer-and-swallow-song-video-1109952/ |website=Rolling Stone |access-date=16 August 2026 |language=English |date=6 January 2021}}</ref> Later that year, Glass revealed that she does not receive appropriate [[royalties]] from her work in Crystal Castles. She disavowed her tenure in the band and asked fans to cease their support of the group.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Richards |first=Will |date=15 October 2020 |url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/alice-glass-says-she-is-being-gutted-over-crystal-castles-royalty-payments-2786266 |title=Alice Glass says she is being "gutted" over Crystal Castles royalty payments |website=[[NME]]|access-date=12 November 2021}}</ref><ref name="rollingstone Legaspi "/>

===2021: ''Prey//IV''===
Glass released the single "Suffer and Swallow" on 6 January 2021, which was the first song she shared from her solo debut album<ref>{{cite web |last1=Brownstein |first1=Charles |title=Alice Glass Debuts "Suffer And Swallow" |url=https://northerntransmissions.com/alice-glass-debuts-suffer-and-swallow/ |website=Northern Transmissions |publisher=Northern Transmissions |access-date=16 August 2026 |language=English |date=6 January 2021}}</ref>. The song was accompanied by a [[stop-motion]] music video by Lucas David.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Reilly |first=Nick |date=6 January 2021 |url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/alice-glass-shares-stop-motion-video-for-new-track-suffer-and-swallow-2850082 |title=Alice Glass shares stop-motion video for new track 'Suffer and Swallow' |website=[[NME]]|access-date=19 November 2021}}</ref> 

Glass had a guest appearance on [[Alice Longyu Gao]]'s single "Legend" which was released on 27 May 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Helman |first=Peter |date=27 May 2021 |url=https://www.stereogum.com/2149268/alice-longyu-gao-legend-feat-alice-glass/music/ |title=Alice Longyu Gao – "Legend" (Feat. Alice Glass) |website=[[Stereogum]] |access-date=19 November 2021}}</ref> 

On 19 November 2021, Glass unveiled the title and shared the track listing of her solo debut album ''[[Prey//IV]]'' and announced a release date of 28 January 2022 on her own Eating Glass Records.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Renshaw |first1=David |title=Alice Glass confirms debut solo album details |url=https://www.thefader.com/2021/11/19/alice-glass-prey-iv-release-date-baby-teeth-video |website=FADER |publisher=FADER |access-date=16 August 2026 |language=English |date=November 19, 2021}}</ref> The announcement was accompanied the single "Baby Teeth", which had by a music video by [[Astra Zero]] and Lucas David.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pitchfork.com/news/alice-glass-details-debut-album-shares-video-for-new-song-baby-teeth-watch/ |title=Alice Glass Details Debut Album, Shares Video for New Song "Baby Teeth": Watch |work=Pitchfork |last=Hussey |first=Allison |date=19 November 2021 |access-date=19 November 2021}}</ref> 

On 8 December 2021, Glass premiered the single "Fair Game" accompanied by a music video directed by [[Bryan M. Ferguson]].<ref>{{Cite magazine|last=Zemler|first=Emily|date=2021-12-08|title=Alice Glass Breaks Her Chains in 'Fair Game' Music Video|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/alice-glass-fair-game-video-1268486/|access-date=2021-12-08|magazine=Rolling Stone|language=en-US}}</ref>

On 28 January 2022, Glass released "Love Is Violence", after the album's release was delayed to February. The single was accompanied by a music video by Bryan M. Ferguson.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bloom |first1=Madison |title=Alice Glass Shares Gory Video for New Song “Love Is Violence”: Watch |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/alice-glass-shares-gory-video-for-new-song-love-is-violence-watch/ |website=Pitchfork |publisher=Pitchfork |access-date=16 August 2026 |language=English |date=January 28, 2022}}</ref> The early 2000s-inspired video depicts two teenagers who sensually pull out each other's entrails.<ref>{{Cite magazine |date=2022-01-28 |title=Alice Glass Serves Teen Goth Gore in 'Love Is Violence' Video |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/alice-glass-love-is-violence-music-video-1291738/ |access-date=2022-01-28 |magazine=Rolling Stone |language=en-US}}</ref> 

Upon the album's release on the 16 February 2022, Glass premiered a music video for "Everybody Else" directed by [[Astra Zero]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-02-16|title=Alice Glass drops debut full-length <nowiki>'PREY//IV'</nowiki> with "Everybody Else" video|url=https://www.altpress.com/news/alice-glass-new-album-prey-iv-everybody-else-music-video/|access-date=2022-02-16|website=Alternative Press Magazine|language=en}}</ref> 

''[[Dazed]]'' described the album: "The extreme pop album is rammed with vivid portrayals of body horror, where eerie soundscapes intertwine with distorted and warped synths, accompanied by a drum loop that punctuates the tracks. These rough dissonances create a claustrophobic panorama, while Glass’ lyrics overlay descriptions of violent fantasies."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alice Glass has some things to say about men|url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/music/article/62406/1/alice-glass-interview-wide-awake-festival-tickets|website=Dazed|date=2024-04-16|access-date=2025-12-01|language=en|last=May|first=Angelika}}</ref>

=== 2022–present: Recent activities ===
On 21 September 2022, Glass released a new single, "Lips Apart".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Robinson |first=Ellie |date=2022-09-22 |title=Alice Glass shuts herself out on melancholic new single 'Lips Apart' |url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/alice-glass-shuts-herself-out-on-melancholic-new-single-lips-apart-3314657 |access-date=2022-11-20 |website=NME |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 18 April 2024, Glass released a [[cover version|cover]] of [[The Smashing Pumpkins]] song "[[Drown (The Smashing Pumpkins song)|Drown]]," produced by [[Jupiter Keyes]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bloom |first=Madison |date=2024-04-18 |title=Alice Glass Releases New Cover of the Smashing Pumpkins' "Drown": Listen |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/alice-glass-releases-new-cover-of-the-smashing-pumpkins-drown-listen |access-date=2024-05-25 |website=Pitchfork |language=en-US}}</ref> This cover track was later featured on the [[Album#Tribute or cover|covers album]], 
''[[Sending Hearts to All My Dearies: A Tribute to the Smashing Pumpkins]]'' released on August 14, 2026 by [[Sumerian Records]], featuring artists such as [[Tame Impala]], [[Barns Courtney]], [[Nita Strauss]] and [[Palaye Royale]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Tepper |first1=Ned |title=Tame Impala Leads New Smashing Pumpkins Tribute Album Featuring Palaye Royale, The Midnight & More |url=https://bluntmag.com.au/news/tame-impala-smashing-pumpkins-tribute-album-sending-hearts-to-all-my-dearies/ |website=Blunt Magazine |access-date=16 August 2026 |language=en-AU |date=23 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Young |first1=Alex |title=Smashing Pumpkins Get New Tribute Album with Tame Impala Cover |url=https://consequence.net/2026/06/smashing-pumpkins-tribute-album-tame-impala/ |website=Consequence Sound |publisher=Consequence Sound |access-date=16 August 2026 |date=23 June 2026}}</ref>

On 21 June 2024, Glass released a new single, "Remains", featuring New York-based musician Clip.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Siroky |first1=Mary |title=Alice Glass Unveils New Song “REMAINS” with Clip: Stream |url=https://consequence.net/2024/06/alice-glass-remains-clip-stream/ |website=Consequence Sound |publisher=Consequence Sound |access-date=16 August 2026 |language=English |date=June 21, 2024}}</ref> The same day, a visualizer was also released on Glass's YouTube channel.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-06-21 |title=Alice Glass & Clip Share New Song "Remains": Listen |url=https://www.stereogum.com/2268940/alice-glass-remains-feat-clip/music/ |access-date=2024-08-11 |website=Stereogum |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W45opL_RqoQ |title=REMAINS (Official Visualizer) |date=2024-06-21 |last=Alice Glass |access-date=2024-08-11 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

In November 2025, Glass released "MERCY KILL" which Margaret Farrell of ''Stereo Gum'' described as having "demonic vocals, crackles of skittering percussion, and pearlescent synths".<ref name=stereogum>{{Cite web |last=Farrell |first=Margaret |date=2025-11-21 |title=Alice Glass Shares New Single "MERCY KILL": Listen |url=https://stereogum.com/2480347/alice-glass-mercy-kill/music/ |access-date=2025-11-21 |website=Stereogum |language=en}}</ref> The single previews a "larger project" due in 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.brooklynvegan.com/13-new-songs-out-today-60/|title=13 New Songs Out Today|first=BrooklynVegan|last=Staff}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mixmag.net/read/new-music-on-our-radar-this-week-danny-l-harle-lancey-foux-shy-one-news|title=New music on our radar this week: Danny L Harle, Lancey Foux, Shy One|website=Mixmag.net}}</ref>
The single was featured on the ''Alternative Press'' "A-sides: 10 new songs you have to hear" list for the week of November 21, 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.altpress.com/alternative-press-a-sides-playlist-november-21-2025/|title=AP A-sides: 10 songs you need to hear|first=Alternative Press|last=Magazine}}</ref>

'''Allison Harvard Burke''' (January 8, 1988) is an American model, artist, actress, and [[Internet celebrity]], best known as the runner-up of ''[[America's Next Top Model]]'' [[America's Next Top Model (season 12)|Cycle 12]] and ''[[America's Next Top Model (cycle 17)|17: All-Stars]]''. Harvard has appeared on a number of magazine covers, such as ''[[Harper's Bazaar]]'', ''[[L'Officiel]]'', ''ONE'', ''WeTheUrban'', and one of the Philippines' leading fashion magazines, ''Mega''. She was the brand endorser of the [[Vicki Belo|Belo Medical Group]] and covered their special edition magazine.

==Early life==
Harvard was born in [[Houston]], Texas, and raised in [[New Orleans]], Louisiana.<ref>{{cite web |last=Friedman |first=Molly |url=http://www.wetpaint.com/americas-next-top-model/articles/allison-harvard-celebrates-24th-birthday-with-new-kitten-photo- |title=Allison Harvard Celebrates 24th Birthday With New Kitten (PHOTO) |publisher=[[Wet Paint]] |date=January 9, 2012 |access-date=July 17, 2012 |archive-date=May 3, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120503013635/http://www.wetpaint.com/americas-next-top-model/articles/allison-harvard-celebrates-24th-birthday-with-new-kitten-photo- |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="nola">{{cite web |last=Walker |first=Dave |url=http://blog.nola.com/davewalker/2009/05/top_model_runnerup_allison_har.html |title='America's Next Top Model' runner-up Allison Harvard talks about her life |work=[[The Times-Picayune]] |publisher=[[Advance Publications]] |date=May 14, 2009 |access-date=October 25, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111101200040/http://blog.nola.com/davewalker/2009/05/top_model_runnerup_allison_har.html |archive-date=November 1, 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> She attended [[Louisiana State University]] in [[Baton Rouge, Louisiana|Baton Rouge]] before transferring to the [[University of New Orleans]], where she studied art during Spring 2009.<ref name="nola"/> Her artwork is featured in the 2007 novel ''The Story Told at Night'' by Liza Kuznetsova.<ref>{{cite book |last=Kuznetsova |first=Liza |title=The Story Told at Night |date=October 9, 2007 |publisher=InstantPublisher.com |isbn=978-1-59872-865-1}}</ref>

In 2005, before her appearance on ''[[America's Next Top Model]]'', Harvard gained notoriety as an [[Internet meme]] on [[4chan]], where she became known as Creepy-chan.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Poulsen |first=Kevin |url=https://www.wired.com/threatlevel/2009/05/creepycha/ |title='Anonymous' Pin-Up Girl Is Runner-Up For ''America's Next Top Model'' |magazine=Wired |publisher=[[Wired News]]. [[Condé Nast Publications]] |date=May 19, 2009 |access-date=May 21, 2009 |archive-date=July 5, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120705141800/http://www.wired.com/threatlevel/2009/05/creepycha |url-status=live }}</ref>

== ''America's Next Top Model'' ==

=== ''America's Next Top Model Cycle 12'' ===

After being contacted through an email by a casting agent who had seen her look online, Harvard successfully auditioned for the reality television show ''[[America's Next Top Model, Cycle 12|America's Next Top Model Cycle 12]]''. During the audition, Harvard stated that she thought [[nosebleed]]s were pretty, and that she was [[blood fetishism|fascinated by blood]].<ref name="nola" /><ref>{{cite web |last=Simmons |first=Abbey |date=May 15, 2009 |title=Exclusive Interview: Allison Harvard of America's Next Top Model Cycle 12 |url=http://www.buddytv.com/articles/americas-next-top-model/exclusive-interview-allison-ha-28716.aspx |access-date=January 18, 2010 |publisher=[[BuddyTV]] |archive-date=March 17, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100317150109/http://www.buddytv.com/articles/americas-next-top-model/exclusive-interview-allison-ha-28716.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Waldman |first=Betsy |url=http://www.celebuzz.com/video-allison-harvard-top-models-s89571/ |title=VIDEO: Allison Harvard Is Top Model's Bloodthirsty New Babe |publisher=[[Celebuzz]]. [[Buzz Media]] |date=February 27, 2009 |access-date=July 17, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090302200009/http://www.celebuzz.com/video-allison-harvard-top-models-s89571/ |archive-date=March 2, 2009 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Harvard was the fourth contestants selected (after Aminat Ayinde, [[Natalie Pack]] and Fo Porter) for the top thirteen. Her roommates on the Upper East Side of [[Manhattan]] in New York City home were Isabella Falk, Kortnie Coles, Sandra Nyanchoka, London Levi-Nance, [[Natalie Pack]] and Celia Ammerman. Over her stay, Harvard received four first call-outs<ref>''America's Next Top Model'', Cycle 12: Episodes 1, 9, 11, and 12</ref> and was selected to participate in two challenge prizes won by fellow contestant Celia Ammerman. Harvard had two collective bottom two appearances. The first where she overanalyzed her shoot with London Levi-Nance<ref>{{cite episode|series=America's Next Top Model, Cycle 12|title=Episode 4}}</ref> which she survived over Nijah Harris who was eliminated third in her first ever bottom two appearance. The second time Harvard was called forward was for her lackluster commercial and her one-dimensional look that led the judges to question her versatility.<ref>{{cite episode|series=America's Next Top Model, Cycle 12|title=Episode 7}}</ref> This time Harvard survived for the second time over Tahlia Brookins who was eliminated sixth in her first ever bottom two appearance.
 
During the Cycle 12 Finale of ''ANTM'' in [[Sao Paulo, Brazil]], Harvard shot a convincing [[CoverGirl]] commercial and was praised for her improvement from the previous commercial.<ref>{{cite episode|series=America's Next Top Model, Cycle 12|title=Season Finale}}</ref> Despite Harvard's (and Aminat Ayinde's) better performances in the [[CoverGirl]] commercial, Teyona Anderson was ultimately crowned the twelfth winner of ''[[America's Next Top Model]]''.

=== ''America's Next Top Model Cycle 17: All-Stars'' ===

After her first appearance on the show, Harvard was selected to return to ''America's Next Top Model'' to represent [[America's Next Top Model, Cycle 12|Cycle 12]] (along with fellow semifinalist, later [[America's Next Top Model (cycle 14)|Cycle 14]] contestant Angelea Preston) on [[America's Next Top Model, Cycle 17|the first All-Star edition of the show]] along with twelve other returning models from past ''[[America's Next Top Model]]'' cycles. Throughout the competition, Harvard developed her own perfume, performed in a music video for her song "Underwater", won two challenges, received two first call-outs and survived her first-ever bottom two appearance over [[Laura Kirkpatrick]] from [[America's Next Top Model (cycle 13)|''America's Next Top Model Cycle 13: the "Petite Edition"'']].

Jaclyn Marielle Jaffe was born on June 23, 1989, in [[Valencia, Santa Clarita, California]].

==Personal life==
Jaffe has been married to [[TK McKamy]] since 2014. They have two children. Jaffe has stated that she stepped away from her career to focus on her private family life.

'''Matthew Chou Bowman''' (born May 31, 1991) is an American professional [[baseball]] [[pitcher]] in the [[Minnesota Twins]] organization. He has previously played in [[Major League Baseball]] (MLB) for the [[St. Louis Cardinals]], [[Cincinnati Reds]], [[New York Yankees]], the Twins, [[Arizona Diamondbacks]], [[Seattle Mariners]], and [[Baltimore Orioles]].

==High school and college==

While growing up in [[Chevy Chase, Maryland]], Bowman attended [[St. Albans School (Washington, D.C.)|St. Albans School]] in [[Washington, D.C.]] As a senior he was All-Met Player of the Year and All-Conference as a shortstop and right-handed pitcher, and had a 0.70 ERA as a pitcher and a .419 average as a batter.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goprincetontigers.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4301|title=Matt Bowman – Baseball|access-date=October 9, 2017|archive-date=October 19, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181019124151/https://goprincetontigers.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4301|url-status=live}}</ref>

He played [[college baseball]] for the [[Princeton Tigers baseball|Princeton Tigers]] at [[Princeton University]] from 2010 to 2012. He was both a pitcher and [[shortstop]] for the Tigers.<ref name=autogenerated1>{{Cite web |url=http://m.mlb.com/news/article/32809898// |title=Mets like potential of Princeton pitcher Matthew Bowman<!-- Bot generated title --> |website=[[MLB.com]] |access-date=August 25, 2017 |archive-date=July 9, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170709092310/http://m.mlb.com/news/article/32809898// |url-status=dead }}</ref>  He had a low-90s fastball that ran as high as 95 mph, a hard slider, a curveball, and a changeup.<ref name=autogenerated1 /> He was second-team all-[[Ivy League]] at shortstop as a sophomore.<ref name=autogenerated1 />  In 2012, as a junior, he went 4–2 with a 4.66 ERA in nine starts along with batting .308 with one home run in 33 games.<ref name=autogenerated1 /> During the summers in college, he played shortstop for the [[Bethesda Big Train]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigtrain.org/history/major/|title=Bethesda Big Train Major Leaguers|access-date=February 26, 2023|archive-date=February 26, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230226145644/http://www.bigtrain.org/history/major/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===New York Mets===
The [[New York Mets]] selected Bowman in the 13th round of the [[2012 Major League Baseball draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://mlb.mlb.com/news/article.jsp?ymd=20120605&content_id=32809898&c_id=mlb|title=Mets like potential of Princeton pitcher|work=Major League Baseball|accessdate=December 4, 2014}}</ref> He made his professional debut that season for the [[Brooklyn Cyclones]]. He had a 2.45 [[earned run average]] (ERA) in {{frac|29|1|3}} innings pitched. Bowman started 2013 with the [[Savannah Sand Gnats]] and was promoted to the [[St. Lucie Mets]] during the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://php.pressconnects.com/blogs/bmets/2014/04/17/bowman-moving-faster-expected/|title=Bowman moving faster than even he expected|work=Inside the park|accessdate=December 4, 2014|archive-url=https://archive.today/20140711100118/http://php.pressconnects.com/blogs/bmets/2014/04/17/bowman-moving-faster-expected/|archive-date=July 11, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> Over 21 starts he had a 10–4 [[Win–loss record (pitching)|win–loss record]] with a 3.05 ERA and 116 [[strikeouts]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.newsday.com/sports/baseball/mets-prospect-matt-bowman-uses-his-head-on-the-mound-1.8526906|title=Mets prospect Matt Bowman uses his head on the mound|work=Newsday|access-date=December 4, 2014|archive-date=December 10, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141210181954/http://www.newsday.com/sports/baseball/mets-prospect-matt-bowman-uses-his-head-on-the-mound-1.8526906|url-status=dead}}</ref>

[[File:Matt Bowman (16778519962).jpg|thumb|upright|left|Bowman pitching for the New York Mets]]
Bowman started the 2014 season with the [[Binghamton Mets]] and was promoted to the [[Las Vegas 51s]] in July; in 24 games (23 starts) between the two teams, he was 10–8 with a 3.21 ERA. He spent the 2015 season back with Las Vegas, where he pitched to a 7–16 record and 5.53 ERA.{{citation needed|date=January 2023}}

===St. Louis Cardinals===
The [[St. Louis Cardinals]] selected Bowman in the 2015 [[Rule 5 draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/new-york/mets/post/_/id/113718/mets-lose-matt-bowman-in-rule-5-draft |title=Mets lose Matt Bowman in Rule 5 draft |access-date=July 15, 2024 |archive-date=December 5, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241205062653/https://www.espn.com/blog/new-york/mets/post/_/id/113718/mets-lose-matt-bowman-in-rule-5-draft |url-status=live }}</ref> He made his MLB debut against the [[2016 Pittsburgh Pirates season|Pittsburgh Pirates]] on April 6, [[2016 St. Louis Cardinals season|2016]], throwing two innings with one hit allowed and two strikeouts. He earned his first MLB win on June 8, 2016, in relief against the Cincinnati Reds. Bowman finished his first MLB season with a 2–5 win–loss record along with a 3.46 ERA.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.mlb.com/player/matt-bowman-621199 |title=Matt Bowman Stats, Fantasy & News {{!}} MLB.com<!-- Bot generated title --> |website=[[MLB.com]] |access-date=November 6, 2016 |archive-date=November 22, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161122042015/http://m.mlb.com/player/621199/matt-bowman |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2017, he was 3–6 with two saves and a 3.99 ERA in {{frac|58|2|3}} innings pitched in relief.

Bowman began 2018 back in St. Louis' bullpen. However, after compiling a 5.75 ERA in {{frac|20|1|3}} innings pitched with two stints on the disabled list, he was optioned to the Triple-A [[Memphis Redbirds]] on July 5.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com/midwest/story/st-louis-cardinals-transactions-dexter-fowler-back-tyler-oneill-to-disabled-list-matt-bowman-to-memphis-redbirds-070518|title=Cardinals transactions: Fowler back, O'Neill to DL, Bowman to Memphis|date=July 5, 2018|access-date=July 9, 2018|archive-date=July 9, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180709215557/https://www.foxsports.com/midwest/story/st-louis-cardinals-transactions-dexter-fowler-back-tyler-oneill-to-disabled-list-matt-bowman-to-memphis-redbirds-070518|url-status=live}}</ref> He was recalled by St. Louis on July 18 and optioned back to Memphis on July 21, and spent the remainder of the season there. In 22 relief appearances for the Cardinals he was 0–2 with a 6.26 ERA,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.kmov.com/sports/st-louis-cardinals-player-grades-bullpen/article_cc2452f8-c799-11e8-b8cb-7f5bc9257887.html | title=News | access-date=October 11, 2018 | archive-date=November 14, 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211114032145/https://www.kmov.com/sports/st-louis-cardinals-player-grades-bullpen/article_cc2452f8-c799-11e8-b8cb-7f5bc9257887.html | url-status=live }}</ref> and in 18 relief appearances for Memphis, he compiled a 0–1 record with a 4.30 ERA.

===Cincinnati Reds===
On November 2, 2018, Bowman was claimed off waivers by the [[Cincinnati Reds]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlbtraderumors.com/2018/11/reds-claim-matthew-bowman-from-cardinals-dilson-herrera-mason-williams-outrighted.html|title=Reds Claim Matthew Bowman from Cardinals; Dilson Herrera, Mason Williams Outrighted|date=November 2, 2018|access-date=November 2, 2018|archive-date=November 2, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181102225719/https://www.mlbtraderumors.com/2018/11/reds-claim-matthew-bowman-from-cardinals-dilson-herrera-mason-williams-outrighted.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He began the 2019 season with the [[Louisville Bats]], and was promoted to the Reds in May.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/baseball/news/reds-matt-bowman-recalled-by-reds/|title = Reds' Matt Bowman: Recalled by Reds| date=May 24, 2019 }}</ref> Bowman underwent [[Tommy John surgery]] in mid-September 2020. On October 14, 2020, Bowman was outrighted off of the roster.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlbtraderumors.com/2020/10/reds-outright-four-to-triple-a.html|title = Reds Outright Four to Triple-A| date=October 14, 2020 }}</ref> Bowman elected free agency two days later on October 16.

===New York Yankees===
On December 14, 2020, Bowman signed a two-year minor league contract with the [[New York Yankees]] organization.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlbtraderumors.com/2020/12/yankees-sign-matt-bowman-to-minor-league-contract.html|title=Yankees Sign Matt Bowman to Minor League Contract|date=December 14, 2020 }}</ref> Bowman did not pitch in 2021 as he recovered from surgery, and missed the entire 2022 season as well.<ref>{{cite web|title=Yankees' Matt Bowman: Won't pitch in 2022|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/baseball/news/yankees-matt-bowman-wont-pitch-in-2022/|access-date=January 13, 2023|website=cbssports.com|date=June 7, 2022|language=en|archive-date=January 13, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230113190601/https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/baseball/news/yankees-matt-bowman-wont-pitch-in-2022/|url-status=live}}</ref> He elected free agency on November 10, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|title=2022–23 Minor League Free Agents For All 30 MLB Teams|url=https://www.baseballamerica.com/stories/2022-23-minor-league-free-agents-for-all-30-mlb-teams/?amphtml|access-date=July 17, 2023|website=baseballamerica.com|date=November 13, 2022|language=en|archive-date=January 9, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230109022816/https://www.baseballamerica.com/stories/2022-23-minor-league-free-agents-for-all-30-mlb-teams/?amphtml|url-status=live}}</ref>

On January 13, 2023, Bowman re-signed with the Yankees organization on a minor league contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Yankees' Matt Bowman: Re-signs with Yankees|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/baseball/news/yankees-matt-bowman-re-signs-with-yankees/amp/|access-date=January 13, 2023|website=cbssports.com|date=January 13, 2023|language=en|archive-date=January 13, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230113190559/https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/baseball/news/yankees-matt-bowman-re-signs-with-yankees/amp/|url-status=live}}</ref> He began the year with the Triple–A [[Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders]], making 30 appearances and logging a 3.29 ERA with 36 strikeouts and 3 saves in {{fraction|38|1|3}} innings pitched. On July 16, Bowman exercised the opt–out clause in his contract and was released by the Yankees.<ref>{{cite web|title=Yankees' Matt Bowman: Opting out of contract|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/baseball/news/yankees-matt-bowman-opting-out-of-contract/amp/|access-date=July 17, 2023|website=cbssports.com|date=July 16, 2023|language=en|archive-date=July 17, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230717181851/https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/baseball/news/yankees-matt-bowman-opting-out-of-contract/amp/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/yankees/2023/07/yankees-right-hander-wants-out.html |title=Yankees' minor league right-hander wants out |publisher=nj.com |date= July 17, 2023|accessdate=September 4, 2023}}</ref> On July 20, Bowman re–signed with the Yankees on a major league contract and was optioned back to Triple–A Scranton.<ref>{{cite web|title=Yankees' Matt Bowman: Re-signs with NYY|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/baseball/news/yankees-matt-bowman-re-signs-with-nyy/amp/|access-date=July 21, 2023|website=cbssports.com|date=July 20, 2023|language=en|archive-date=July 21, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230721151407/https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/baseball/news/yankees-matt-bowman-re-signs-with-nyy/amp/|url-status=live}}</ref>

The Yankees promoted Bowman to the major leagues on September 10.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://nypost.com/2023/09/10/yankees-again-demote-ron-marinaccio-in-bullpen-re-shuffle/ | title=Yankees again demote Ron Marinaccio in bullpen re-shuffle | date=September 10, 2023 }}</ref> In three games for the Yankees, he allowed four runs on six hits with three strikeouts in four innings of work. Following the season on November 2, Bowman was removed from the 40-man roster and sent outright to Triple–A Scranton.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Yankees' Matt Bowman: Outrighted off 40-man|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/baseball/news/yankees-matt-bowman-outrighted-off-40-man/amp/|access-date=November 7, 2023|website=cbssports.com|date=November 2, 2023 |language=en}}</ref> He elected free agency on November 6.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Matt Bowman: Elects free agency|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/baseball/news/matt-bowman-elects-free-agency/|access-date=November 7, 2023|website=cbssports.com|date=November 6, 2023|language=en|archive-date=November 7, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231107100212/https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/baseball/news/matt-bowman-elects-free-agency/|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Minnesota Twins===
On January 18, 2024, Bowman signed a minor league contract with the [[Minnesota Twins]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.mlbtraderumors.com/2024/01/twins-matt-bowman-agree-to-minor-league-deal.html | title=Twins, Matt Bowman Agree to Minor League Deal | date=January 19, 2024 | access-date=January 19, 2024 | archive-date=January 19, 2024 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240119034215/https://www.mlbtraderumors.com/2024/01/twins-matt-bowman-agree-to-minor-league-deal.html | url-status=live }}</ref> He made five scoreless appearances for the Triple–A [[St. Paul Saints]] to begin the year. On April 13, the Twins selected Bowman's contract to the major league roster.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Twins Place Carlos Correa On 10-Day IL, Designate Michael Tonkin|url=https://www.mlbtraderumors.com/2024/04/twins-place-carlos-correa-on-10-day-il-designate-michael-tonkin.html|access-date=April 13, 2024|website=mlbtraderumors.com|date=April 13, 2024 |language=en}}</ref> He made five appearances for Minnesota, recording a 2.35 ERA with 6 strikeouts across {{fraction|7|2|3}} innings pitched. On April 30, Bowman was designated for assignment by the Twins.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Twins Designate Matt Bowman For Assignment|url=https://www.mlbtraderumors.com/2024/04/twins-designate-matt-bowman-for-assignment.html|access-date=April 30, 2024|website=mlbtraderumors.com|date=April 30, 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

===Arizona Diamondbacks===
On May 2, 2024, Bowman was traded to the [[Arizona Diamondbacks]] in exchange for cash.<ref>{{Cite web|title=D-Backs Acquire Matt Bowman From Twins|url=https://www.mlbtraderumors.com/2024/05/d-backs-acquire-matt-bowman-from-twins.html|access-date=May 2, 2024|website=mlbtraderumors.com|date=May 2, 2024 |language=en}}</ref> In four appearances for the Diamondbacks, he struggled to an 8.10 ERA with four strikeouts across {{fraction|6|2|3}} innings pitched. On May 26, Bowman was designated for assignment by Arizona.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Diamondbacks Designate Matt Bowman For Assignment|url=https://www.mlbtraderumors.com/2024/05/diamondbacks-designate-matt-bowman-for-assignment.html|access-date=May 26, 2024|website=mlbtraderumors.com|date=May 26, 2024|language=en|archive-date=May 26, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240526170935/https://www.mlbtraderumors.com/2024/05/diamondbacks-designate-matt-bowman-for-assignment.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He cleared waivers and was sent outright to the Triple–A [[Reno Aces]] on May 31, but rejected the assignment in favor of free agency.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Matt Bowman: Elects free agency|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/baseball/news/matt-bowman-elects-free-agency-921730/|access-date=May 31, 2024|website=cbssports.com|date=May 31, 2024|language=en|archive-date=May 31, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240531233309/https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/baseball/news/matt-bowman-elects-free-agency-921730/|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Seattle Mariners===
On June 4, 2024, Bowman signed a minor league contract with the [[Seattle Mariners]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rotoballer.com/player-news/mariners-agree-to-minor-league-deal-with-matt-bowman/1377330 |title=Mariners Agree To Minor League Deal With Matt Bowman |first=Brandon |last=Williams |publisher=rotoballer.com |access-date=June 4, 2024 }}{{Dead link|date=May 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> After two scoreless appearances for the Triple–A [[Tacoma Rainiers]], Bowman was called up by the Mariners on June 9.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fantasypros.com/mlb/news/451582/matt-bowman-selected-from-triple-a.php|title=Matt Bowman selected from Triple-A |first=Ari |last=Koslow |date=June 9, 2024 |publisher=fantasypros.com |access-date=June 9, 2024}}</ref> He made only one appearance for Seattle before he was designated for assignment on June 11.<ref>{{Cite '''Rebecca "Becca" Green''' is an American illustrator, author, and painter who is known for [[Children's literature|children's books]].<ref name=":0" />

== Biography ==
Rebecca Green was born in [[Owosso, Michigan]]. She has also lived in [[Osaka]], [[Nashville, Tennessee|Nashville]], [[Phoenix, Arizona|Phoenix]], and [[Denver]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Trimble |first=Lynn |title=Rebecca Green Returns to Phoenix to Paint New Mural at The Lodge on Grand Avenue |url=https://www.phoenixnewtimes.com/arts/rebecca-green-returns-to-phoenix-to-paint-new-mural-at-the-lodge-on-grand-avenue-6580761 |access-date=2023-05-03 |website=Phoenix New Times |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-11-20 |title=Rebecca Green - Artist Interview |url=https://wowxwow.com/artist-interview/rebecca-green-ai |access-date=2023-05-04 |website=WOW x WOW |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=About |url=https://www.myblankpaper.com/about-copy |access-date=2023-05-04 |website=Rebecca Green Illustration |language=en-US}}</ref> She graduated from [[Kendall College of Art and Design|Kendall College of Art]] and Design with a [[Bachelor of Fine Arts|bachelor of fine arts]] in illustration in 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |title=How to Make Friends with a Ghost: Alum s New Book Weaves Offbeat Humor, Quirky Illustrations |url=https://kcad.ferris.edu/news/how-to-make-friends-with-a-ghost-alums-new-book-weaves-offbeat-humor-quirky-illustrations.html |access-date=2023-05-04 |website=kcad.ferris.edu}}</ref>

=== Career ===
Green was named 21 of 100 creative forces in [[Phoenix, Arizona|Phoenix]] in the ''[[Phoenix New Times]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lawton |first=Claire |title=21: Rebecca Green |url=https://www.phoenixnewtimes.com/arts/21-rebecca-green-6563357 |access-date=2023-05-03 |website=Phoenix New Times |language=en}}</ref>

She has illustrated more than one dozen books written by other authors. She has written and illustrated one book, ''How to Make Friends with a Ghost'' ([[Tundra Books]], 2017),<ref name=":1" /> which the [[The Jim Henson Company|Jim Henson Company]] began developing for a series in 2021.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Ghost book to be developed as stop-motion series by Jim Henson Company |url=https://www.thebookseller.com/rights/rebecca-green-book-be-developed-stop-animation-series-1285741 |url-access=subscription |access-date=2023-05-03 |website=The Bookseller |language=En}}</ref>

Green is a member of the [[Society of Children's Book Writers and Illustrators]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=SCBWI {{!}} Public Profile |url=https://www.scbwi.org/members-public/rebecca-green1 |access-date=2023-05-03 |language=en-US}}</ref>

==== Critical reception ====
''[[Publishers Weekly]]'' wrote of Green's illustrations in ''Iqbal and His Ingenious Idea: How a Science Project Helps One Family and the Planet'' (Kids Can Press, 2018): "The stylized colored-pencil illustrations from Green offer realistic scenes of Bangladeshi village life in muted hues and portray the closeness of Iqbal’s family"; ''[[Kirkus Reviews]]'' wrote, "Green's illustrations are earthy and colorful and perfectly capture the soul of the story".<ref name=":3" />

''Publishers Weekly'' called her illustrations in ''A Year with Mama Earth'' (Eerdmans, 2019) as "stylized, textural".<ref name=":4" /> ''Kirkus Reviews'' noted her work in ''Becoming a Good Creature'' (HMH Books, 2020) was "visually pleasing illustrations... rendered in a warm, earth-hued palette, and they have an uncomplicated design that effectively complements the story’s wise, authentic narrative".<ref name=":5" />

''Kirkus Reviews'' said Green's work in ''[[Madame Saqui]]: Revolutionary Rope Dancer'' (Schwartz & Wade/Random, 2020) was "muted, stylized".<ref name=":6" /> About the same book, ''Publishers Weekly'' said, "mixed media illustrations by Green in dusky pastels provide period atmosphere with fancy costumes, dramatic lighting, and figures that look just a bit like marionettes".<ref name=":7" />

The [[woodcut]] and German [[Expressionism|expressionistic]] appearance of the illustrations in ''[[Franz Kafka|Kafka]] and the Doll'' (Viking, 2021) made an impression on one reviewer.<ref name=":8" /> A [[starred review]] by ''Booklist'' noted, "Green tops off her muted scenes of button-eyed figures in, alternately, autumnal and far-flung settings."<ref name=":9" />

In a starred review for ''A Bear Far from Home'' (Anne Schwartz/Random, 2022), ''[[Booklist]]'' wrote, "Green’s marvelous folk-style illustrations take their cues from medieval artwork, framing scenes with thick, gold borders and flowery flourishes".<ref name=":2" /> In another review, her work was noted for "presenting varied human skin tones throughout"; the review continues, "Green’s stylized [[gouache]] and pencil renderings complement through their use of ornate, medieval-inspired borders and floral flourishes".<ref name=":10" />

''Kirkus Reviews'' said Green's work in ''Loujain Dreams of Sunflowers: A Story Inspired by [[Loujain al-Hathloul|Loujain Alhathloul]]'' (minedition, 2022) was "beautifully representational".<ref name=":11" />

''Kirkus Reviews'' commented that her first book as both writer and illustrator, ''How to Make Friends with a Ghost'' (Tundra Books, 2017), had "a sophisticated, rather adult aesthetic."<ref name=":1" />

'''Kerby Jean-Raymond''' (born 1986) is a Haitian American [[fashion design]]er, the founder and creative director of the New York label Pyer Moss, which he started in 2013. His runway presentations combine clothing with live performance and with commentary on race in the United States.<ref name="cnn2021">{{cite news |title=Kerby Jean-Raymond will be the first Black American designer to present at Paris Couture Week |url=https://www.cnn.com/style/article/pyer-moss-kerby-jean-raymond-paris-haute-couture/index.html |work=CNN |language=en |date=May 13, 2021 |access-date=July 29, 2026 }}</ref>

He drew wide attention with a September 2015 show, presented during [[New York Fashion Week]], that addressed [[police brutality]], and between 2018 and 2019 staged "American, Also", a three-part series of collections on the place of Black Americans in national culture.<ref name="nyt2019">{{cite news |last=Friedman |first=Vanessa |title=Gambling With Fashion Fame |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/02/07/fashion/kerby-jean-raymond-pyer-moss-not-showing.html |work=The New York Times |language=en |date=February 7, 2019 |url-access=subscription |access-date=July 29, 2026 }}</ref> He won the CFDA/''Vogue'' Fashion Fund in 2018 and was named American Menswear Designer of the Year at the 2020 [[Council of Fashion Designers of America|CFDA]] Fashion Awards.<ref name="wwdcfda2020">{{cite news |title=2020 CFDA Fashion Awards Winners: See Full List of Winners |url=https://wwd.com/fashion-news/fashion-scoops/2020-cfda-fashion-awards-winners-full-list-1234582228/ |work=WWD |language=en |date=September 14, 2020 |access-date=July 29, 2026 }}</ref> He was global creative director of [[Reebok]] between 2020 and 2022, and in July 2021 became the first Black American designer to present on the official Paris [[haute couture]] schedule.<ref name="cbs2021">{{cite news |title=Pyer Moss Honors Black Inventors With 1st Couture Show |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/pyer-moss-honors-black-inventors-with-1st-couture-show |work=CBS News New York |language=en |date=July 12, 2021 |access-date=July 29, 2026 }}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Jean-Raymond was born in 1986 and grew up in the [[East Flatbush, Brooklyn|East Flatbush]] neighborhood of [[Brooklyn]], New York. His father, Jean-Claude Jean-Raymond, emigrated from [[Haiti]] to the United States in 1980 and worked as a taxi driver and later as an electrical technician. His mother, Vania Moss-Pierre, died in a house fire during a trip to Haiti when Jean-Raymond was seven, and he was raised by his father. The label Pyer Moss takes its name from her: Moss was her maiden name, and Pyer is a spelling of Pierre, the surname of a cousin already in the United States that she used on her immigration paperwork.<ref name="cut2023">{{cite news |last=Hairston |first=Tahirah |title=The Promise of Pyer Moss |url=https://www.thecut.com/article/pyer-moss-kerby-jean-raymond-designer.html |work=The Cut |language=en |date=January 30, 2023 |url-access=subscription |access-date=July 29, 2026 }}</ref>

Jean-Raymond began designing at a young age. He landed his first apprenticeship at 14 while still attending [[High School of Fashion Industries|The High School of Fashion Industries]] in Manhattan. He started his first fashion label, Mary's Jungle at the age of 15.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Miller|first=M. H.|date=March 5, 2020|title=The Designer Changing How We Think About Fashion and Race in America|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/03/05/t-magazine/pyer-moss-kerby-jean-raymond.html|access-date=August 19, 2020|issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Taught by [[Kay Unger]], Jean-Raymond worked on Unger's first women's evening collection.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Marquez|first1=Mark|title=Pyer Moss Is Killer|url=http://mi.lk/articles/2158-Pyer-Moss-Is-Killer/|publisher=mi.lk|date=September 12, 2013}}{{Dead link|date=December 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

He launched Pyer Moss in 2013.<ref>{{cite web|title=Official Pyer Moss Website|url=http://pyermoss.com/?page_id=68}}</ref> Jean-Raymond uses his brand to address racial tensions in the United States and intertwine social issues with the fashion world. He describes his brand, Pyer Moss, as an "art project" or "a timely social experiment" at times.<ref>{{Cite web |title=About |url=https://www.pyermoss.com/pages/about |access-date=October 6, 2022 |website=Pyer Moss |language=en}}</ref>

Jean-Raymond took his first job at 13, at a Flatbush sneaker store, and interned at Marchesa and Theory while at the High School of Fashion Industries.<ref name="cut2023" /> He graduated from [[Hofstra University]] with a business degree and then enrolled at [[Brooklyn Law School]], leaving after a semester.<ref name="nyt2019" /> He worked at [[AT&T]] and did freelance design for [[Marc Jacobs]], Theory and Kenneth Cole before founding Pyer Moss in 2013 with an initial investment of $35,000 from his former business partner Rayon Baker.<ref name="cut2023" />

== Career ==
Kerby Jean-Raymond first came into the spotlight for his presentation of Pyer Moss' Spring 2016 Menswear Collection during [[New York Fashion Week]].
The show highlighted [[police brutality]], referencing the [[Black Lives Matter]] movement through videos, street art, and fashion. Jean-Raymond has publicly commented about his experience as a teenage victim of [[driving while black]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Bain |first=Marc |title=A powerful show brought "Black Lives Matter" to the runway at New York Fashion Week |url=https://qz.com/500385/a-powerful-show-brought-black-lives-matter-to-the-runway-at-new-york-fashion-week |work=Quartz |language=en |access-date=July 29, 2026 }}</ref> Kerby Jean-Raymond collaborated with R&B singer and activist [[Erykah Badu]], who styled Jean-Raymond's Pyer Moss AW16 line for the 2016 New York Fashion Week show.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.dazeddigital.com/fashion/article/29792/1/erykah-badu-art-activism-nyfw-debut-pyer-moss-styling|title=Erykah Badu on art, activism and her NYFW debut|last=Dazed|date=February 13, 2016|work=Dazed|access-date=October 10, 2017|language=en}}</ref> The featured collection was titled "Double Bind."

The show took place at the Altman Building in Manhattan on September 10, 2015, and opened with a twelve-minute film, ''This Is an Intervention'', combining footage of police violence with interviews with relatives of men who had been killed. Jean-Raymond seated family members of [[Killing of Sean Bell|Sean Bell]] and [[Killing of Eric Garner|Eric Garner]] in the front row, moving some fashion editors further back; several then declined to attend. Garments carried Garner's words "I can't breathe".<ref name="cut2023" /> The collection nearly ended the label: several stores dropped the line and Jean-Raymond received death threats. He was at the same time trying to buy the business back from an investment partner, and said he sold most of his possessions to raise money before a deal with [[Reebok]] let him regain control of the company.<ref name="nyt2019" />

His brand, Pyer Moss, won the Fashion Group International Rising Star Award in the menswear category in 2014, sharing the prize with the designer Ian Velardi.<ref name="dfr2014">{{cite news |title=Lunching With Fashion Group International's Rising Stars |url=https://fashionweekdaily.com/lunching-with-fashion-group-internationals-rising-stars/ |work=The Daily Front Row |language=en |date=January 29, 2014 |access-date=July 29, 2026 }}</ref> That same year, he was a finalist in the DHL Exported Prize presented by IMG Worldwide. He was named to the ''[[Forbes]]'' "30 Under 30" list in the Art and Style category in 2015.<ref name="forbes30">{{cite web |title=Kerby Jean-Raymond |url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/kerby-jean-raymond/ |website=Forbes |language=en |date=January 1, 2015 |access-date=July 29, 2026 }}</ref> Jean-Raymond was featured on ''[[Cultured (magazine)|Cultured Magazine]]''{{'}}s fashion issue cover in April 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.culturedmag.com/pyer-moss/|title=Pyer Moss Isn't a Fashion Brand It's a Life Raft|date=April 11, 2019|website=Cultured Magazine|language=en-US|access-date=April 13, 2019}}</ref>

During Paris Fashion Week in February 2019, [[Odell Beckham Jr.]] wore a Pyer Moss Collection 2 hoodie. Others seen in Pyer Moss include producer [[Swizz Beatz]], Kiandra Layne, [[Gabrielle Union|Gabrielle Union-Wade]], [[Colin Kaepernick]]<ref>{{Cite magazine|title=TIME 100 Next 2019: Kerby Jean-Raymond|url=https://time.com/collection/time-100-next-2019/5718848/kerby-jean-raymond/|access-date=August 19, 2020|magazine=Time|language=en-us}}</ref> and First Lady [[Michelle Obama]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=17 Celebrities Wearing Pyer Moss Prove This Brand Is For Everybody|url=https://www.kolormagazine.com/fashion-1/2019/3/15/johyxrtaqi26ejovcxhhgxl7hlgdn6|access-date=August 19, 2020|website=KOLOR MAGAZINE|date=February 12, 2015 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=History|first=Future Black|title=Future Black History|url=https://fuse.tv/fbh2020-black-luxury-style-guide|access-date=August 19, 2020|website=Fuse|language=en}}</ref>

In September 2020, Jean-Raymond was named Global Creative Director of [[Reebok]]<ref>{{Cite web|last=Huber|first=Eliza|title=Reebok Taps Kerby Jean-Raymond Of Pyer Moss As Global Creative Director|url=https://www.refinery29.com/en-us/2020/09/10062233/kerby-jean-raymond-reebok-global-creative-director|access-date=October 12, 2020|website=www.refinery29.com|date=September 30, 2020 |language=en}}</ref> sportswear brand. Pyer Moss had won the top prize at the fifteenth [[Council of Fashion Designers of America|CFDA/''Vogue'' Fashion Fund]] awards in November 2018, receiving $400,000 and a year of mentorship from an industry executive.<ref name="nyt2019" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=CFDA|url=https://cfda.com/news/breaking-news-kerby-jean-raymond-of-pyer-moss-wins-15th-cfda-vogue-fashion-fund|access-date=October 12, 2020|website=cfda.com |date=November 6, 2018 }}</ref> In early 2022, he departed Reebok.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 3, 2022 |title=Pyer Moss Founder Kerby Jean-Raymond Departs Reebok |url=https://www.gq.com/story/kerby-jean-raymond-leaves-reebok |access-date=February 6, 2023 |website=GQ |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== "American, Also" (2018–2019) ===
Between 2018 and 2019, Jean-Raymond presented "American, Also", a three-part series of collections about the place of Black Americans in national culture. The first, in February 2018, drew on the history of Black cowboys and included his first womenswear alongside collaborations with [[Reebok]] and the 1990s label Cross Colours. The second, in September 2018 at the [[Weeksville Heritage Center]] in Brooklyn, imagined everyday Black American life without racism, with a forty-member choir, artwork by [[Derrick Adams]], a collaboration with [[FUBU]] and a shirt reading "Stop Calling 911 on the Culture".<ref name="nyt2019" />
 
Jean-Raymond skipped New York Fashion Week in February 2019, telling ''[[The New York Times]]'' that he had something to say but was not yet ready to say it.<ref name="nyt2019" /> The final part, "Sister", was presented at the [[Kings Theatre (Brooklyn)|Kings Theatre]] in [[Flatbush, Brooklyn|Flatbush]] in September 2019 before an audience of 3,000, and was built around [[Sister Rosetta Tharpe]] and the contribution of Black women to American popular music. It was a collaboration with Sean John and reportedly cost $400,000 to stage.<ref name="cut2023" />

=== Pyer Moss couture (2021) ===
In February 2021, Jean-Raymond was invited by the [[Fédération de la Haute Couture et de la Mode]] to show during Paris Couture Week, making him the first Black American designer on the official [[haute couture]] calendar.<ref name="cut2023" /><ref name="cnn2021" /> Rather than show in Paris, he staged the collection, titled "Wat U Iz", at [[Villa Lewaro]], the [[Irvington, New York]], estate built by [[Madam C. J. Walker]]. A storm on July 8 forced a postponement, and organizers in Paris extended the couture calendar so that the show could go ahead on July 10.<ref name="cbs2021" /> The garments were sculptural pieces modelled on objects invented by Black Americans, among them a jar of peanut butter, a lampshade and an air-conditioning unit. The presentation opened with a speech by [[Elaine Brown]], a former chairwoman of the [[Black Panther Party]].<ref name="cbs2021" />

=== Business difficulties (2021–2022) ===
Pyer Moss produced little after the couture show. In a January 2023 investigation for ''The Cut'', Tahirah Hairston reported that the label had no store and no functioning online shop, that several runway collections had never been manufactured for sale, and that Jean-Raymond had laid off most of his staff in December 2021 and again in August 2022. [[Kering]], which had invested in Pyer Moss, said through a spokesperson that it had not audited the company and that its relationship with Jean-Raymond was unchanged. Jean-Raymond disputed the account, saying the brand regularly sold clothing, bags and footwear from its runway shows, that fashion houses do not put everything shown on a runway into production, and that the suggestion that investment had been misused was false.<ref name="cut2023" />
