'''Mathew Hubert Houston Bone Murray'''{{efn|Bone's full name is listed on his website}} (born June 4, 1993{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}}), credited professionally as '''M. H. Murray''' or '''Houston Bone''',<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tracy |first=Andrew |title=TIFF ’23 premiere I Don’t Know Who You Are locks sales partner |url=https://playbackonline.ca/2025/08/22/tiff-23-premiere-i-dont-know-who-you-are-locks-sales-partner/ |access-date=2025-11-01}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Tracy |first=Andrew |title=Houston Bone’s ‘Son of Sara’ to premiere at Blood in the Snow |url=https://playbackonline.ca/2025/10/27/houston-bones-son-of-sara-to-premiere-at-blood-in-the-snow/ |access-date=2025-11-01}}</ref> is a Canadian [[Filmmaking|filmmaker]], writer, director, and producer. Bone first attracted attention for his work on the [[web series]] ''[[Teenagers (web series)|Teenagers]]'' (2014–2017), which won [[Teenagers (web series)#Accolades|several accolades]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|url=https://www.cbc.ca/radio/q/schedule-for-tuesday-december-20-2016-1.3902909/m-h-murray-doesn-t-gloss-over-the-gritty-details-of-being-a-teenager-in-his-web-series-1.3902938|title=M. H. Murray doesn't gloss over the gritty details of being a teenager in his web series {{!}} CBC Radio|last=|first=|date=December 20, 2016|work=CBC|access-date=June 25, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Clay">{{Cite news |last=Clay |first=Chris |date=May 11, 2018 |title=Mississauga-based web series 'Teenagers' earns pair of awards, racks up views |language=en-CA |work=Mississauga News |url=https://www.mississauga.com/whatson-story/8598189-mississauga-based-web-series-teenagers-earns-pair-of-awards-racks-up-views/ |access-date=June 25, 2018 |quote=}}</ref> His [[List of directorial debuts#2023|feature-length film debut]], ''[[I Don't Know Who You Are]]'', premiered at the [[2023 Toronto International Film Festival]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kay |first=Jeremy |title=TIFF premiere 'I Don't Know Who You Are' lands US deal (exclusive) |url=https://www.screendaily.com/news/tiff-premiere-i-dont-know-who-you-are-lands-us-deal-exclusive/5191256.article |access-date=2024-08-16 |website=Screen |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life==
Bone was born in [[Toronto]] and raised in the [[Port Credit]] area of [[Mississauga]],<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.mississauga.com/whatson-story/6521190-mississauga-director-s-web-series-a-raw-take-on-teenage-life/|title=Mississauga director's web series a raw take on teenage life|last=Clay|first=Chris|date=April 29, 2016|website=Mississauga News|access-date=June 1, 2016}}</ref> by a [[French Canadian]] mother and a [[Scottish Canadian]] father.<ref name=":13">{{Cite web|date=2021-05-12|title=Filmmaker M.H. Murray Tackles Modern-Dating Anxieties in 'Ghost'|url=https://occhimagazine.com/filmmaker-m-h-murray-tackles-modern-dating-anxieties-in-ghost/|access-date=2021-05-16|website=Occhi Magazine|language=en-US}}</ref> In high school, he began a [[YouTube videos|YouTube channel]] and created "little [[slasher film]]s" with his family and friends.<ref name=":13" /> He graduated from [[York University]]'s [[film school]].<ref name=":11">{{Cite web|url=http://www.excal.on.ca/a-teenage-dream/|title=A teenage dream|last=Mitchell|first=Ashlee|date=January 30, 2014|website=Excalibur|language=en-US|access-date=July 14, 2016|archive-date=May 10, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170510070533/http://www.excal.on.ca/a-teenage-dream/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Career ==
While in film school, Bone began working on his first [[web series]], titled ''[[Teenagers (web series)|Teenagers]]''.<ref name=":11" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Greene |first=Steve |date=December 13, 2016 |title=Indiewire's Project of the Day: 'teenagers' {{!}} IndieWire |url=http://www.indiewire.com/2016/12/project-of-the-day-teenagers-1201757377/ |access-date=January 16, 2017 |website=IndieWire}}</ref> The series ran for three seasons, from 2014 to 2017, initially attracting media attention because its cast included former ''[[Degrassi: The Next Generation|Degrassi]]'' stars such as [[Chloe Rose]] and [[Raymond Ablack]].<ref name=":03">{{Cite web |last=Chunovic |first=Louis |date=January 15, 2014 |title=New web series Teenagers attracts Degrassi alum |url=http://playbackonline.ca/2014/01/15/new-web-series-teenagers-attracts-degrassi-alum/ |access-date=January 23, 2017 |website=Playback}}</ref> Bone co-created the series with close friend Sara Tamosauskas and produced the first season alongside [[Emmanuel Kabongo]], who also starred in all three seasons of the series.<ref>{{Cite web |title=teenagers' Enters its Final Season All Grown Up {{!}} Stareable Blog |url=https://www.stareable.com//blog/teenagers-enters-its-final-season-all-grown-up |access-date=2023-08-02 |website=www.stareable.com |language=en}}</ref> The second season's premiere episode went [[Viral video|viral]],<ref>{{Citation|title=teenagers (web series) - S2, E1 - "The Difference Between Sex and Fucking"| date=July 26, 2015 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=46lEpsZv5vA|language=en|access-date=2022-02-09}}</ref> amassing millions of views on YouTube.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://nowtoronto.com/movies/dvds-downloads-and-streaming/binge-worthy-toronto-web-series/|title=Binge-worthy Toronto web series|last=Durnford|first=Samie|date=August 17, 2016|website=NOW Magazine|access-date=August 21, 2016}}</ref> Since its release, ''Teenagers'' has received positive reviews from critics and [[Teenagers (web series)#Accolades|several accolades]], including a [[Canadian Screen Awards|Canadian Screen Award]] nomination and an [[Indie Series Awards|Indie Series Award]].<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=AS IF BEING A TEENAGER WAS EVER EASY : Teenagers Webseries {{!}} Starved Magazine|url=http://www.culturestarved.com/2014/03/as-if-being-a-teenager-was-ever-easy-teenagers-webseries/|website=www.culturestarved.com|accessdate=November 28, 2015|archive-date=July 2, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170702230418/http://www.culturestarved.com/2014/03/as-if-being-a-teenager-was-ever-easy-teenagers-webseries/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/arts/7-reasons-you-should-care-about-the-canadian-screen-awards-this-year-1.3410270|title=7 reasons you should care about the Canadian Screen Awards this year|last=Knegt|first=Peter|date=January 20, 2016|website=CBC Arts|access-date=April 7, 2016}}</ref><ref name=":22">{{Cite web |date=2021-03-05 |title=Where You've Seen The Ginny And Georgia Cast Before |url=https://www.cinemablend.com/television/2563500/where-youve-seen-the-ginny-and-georgia-cast-before |access-date=2021-05-06 |website=CINEMABLEND}}</ref>

Following the conclusion of ''Teenagers'', Bone wrote and directed a short film titled ''Ghost''.<ref name=":13" /> The short film stars [[Mark Clennon]] as Benjamin, a gay musician who is "[[Ghosting (relationships)|ghosted]]" by his lover.<ref name=":16">{{Cite web|date=2021-05-30|title='Ghost'|url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/video/?clipId=2212329/|access-date=2021-06-05|website=CTVNews|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":17">{{Cite web|date=2021-06-08|title=Short film 'Ghost' is a character study of a gay man getting ghosted|url=https://www.etalk.ca/movies/2021/6/short-film-ghost-is-a-character-study-on-getting-ghosted.html|access-date=2021-06-09|website=etalk|language=en-US}}</ref> In 2022, Bone co-directed the music video for Clennon's song "Kingston".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bell |first=Kaelen |date=June 15, 2022 |title=Mark Clennon Shares New "Kingston" Video, the First Shot in Jamaica to Feature an Onscreen Romance Between Two Men {{!}} Exclaim! |url=https://exclaim.ca/music/article/mark_clennon_shares_new_kingston_video_the_first_shot_in_jamaica_to_feature_an_onscreen_romance_between_two_men |access-date= |website=Exclaim! |language=en-ca}}</ref>

Bone's [[List of directorial debuts#2023|feature-length film debut]], ''[[I Don't Know Who You Are]]'', also starring Clennon, premiered in the Discovery program at the [[2023 Toronto International Film Festival]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hazelton |first=John |title=TIFF Discovery and Midnight Madness line-ups revealed |url=https://www.screendaily.com/news/tiff-discovery-and-midnight-madness-line-ups-revealed/5184627.article |access-date=2023-09-26 |website=Screen |language=en}}</ref> The film has received positive reviews from critics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=I Don't Know Who You Are {{!}} Rotten Tomatoes |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/i_dont_know_who_you_are |access-date=2024-03-26 |website=www.rottentomatoes.com |language=en}}</ref> Barry Hertz of ''[[The Globe and Mail]]'' ranked the film 7th on his list of the top 10 Canadian films of 2023.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-12-26 |title=The 10 best Canadian films of 2023, a year of crises and breakthroughs |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/arts/film/article-the-10-best-canadian-films-of-2023-a-year-of-crises-and-breakthroughs/ |access-date=2024-03-26 |work=The Globe and Mail |language=en-CA}}</ref>

His second feature film, ''[[Son of Sara: Volume 1]]'',<ref>{{Cite web |title=Son of Sara|url=https://tiff.net/films/son-of-sara|access-date=2025-10-26|website=TIFF|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mack |first=Andrew |date=November 13, 2025 |title=SON OF SARA: VOLUME 1 Exclusive Clip: Our First Look at Houston Bone's New Horror Flick |url=https://screenanarchy.com/2025/11/son-of-sara-volume-1-exclusive.html |website=[[Screen Anarchy]]}}</ref> starring [[Chloe Van Landschoot]] and [[Tymika Tafari]], opened [[Blood in the Snow Canadian Film Festival|Blood in the Snow]] on November 17, 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tracy |first=Andrew |title=Houston Bone’s ‘Son of Sara’ to premiere at Blood in the Snow |url=https://playbackonline.ca/2025/10/27/houston-bones-son-of-sara-to-premiere-at-blood-in-the-snow/ |access-date=2025-11-01}}</ref> 

== Influences ==
Bone's work on ''Teenagers'' has been compared to the [[Degrassi (franchise)|''Degrassi'' franchise]] and the [[Skins (UK TV series)|UK television series ''Skins'']].<ref name=":23">{{cite web |date=August 10, 2015 |title=Sex, drugs & violence: Toronto's provocative Web Series "Teenagers" returns for Season Two |url=http://www.shedoesthecity.com/sex-drugs-violence-torontos-provocative-web-series-teenagers-returns-for-season-two |access-date=December 1, 2015 |website=www.shedoesthecity |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Teenagers - The Canadian Skins - The Daily Spectacle |url=http://dailyspectacle.co.uk/2016/10/teenagers-canadian-skins/ |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104203519/http://dailyspectacle.co.uk/2016/10/teenagers-canadian-skins/ |archive-date=November 4, 2016 |access-date=December 4, 2016 |website=www.dailyspectacle.co.uk}}</ref> In an interview with [[CBC Television|CBC]]'s [[Q (radio show)|''q'' radio show]], Bone refuted ''Degrassi'' comparisons, saying that while he "respects" the show, he believes that ''Teenagers'' is "a fresh take on that experience".<ref name=":162">{{Cite news |date=December 20, 2016 |title=M. H. Murray doesn't gloss over the gritty details of being a teenager in his web series |url=http://www.cbc.ca/radio/q/schedule-for-tuesday-december-20-2016-1.3902909/m-h-murray-doesn-t-gloss-over-the-gritty-details-of-being-a-teenager-in-his-web-series-1.3902938 |access-date=January 12, 2017 |newspaper=CBC Radio}}</ref> Bone has stated that he was influenced by [[Issa Rae]]'s ''[[The Mis-Adventures of Awkward Black Girl|The Misadventures of Awkward Black Girl]]'', [[John Hughes (filmmaker)|John Hughes]]'s ''[[The Breakfast Club]]'', and [[Larry Clark]]'s ''[[Kids (film)|Kids]]''.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web|url=http://talknerdywithus.com/2016/04/29/exclusive-interview-with-teenagers-creator-mathew-murray/|title=Exclusive Interview with Teenagers Creator Mathew Murray|date=April 2, 2016|website=TalkNerdyWithUs|language=en-US|access-date=June 1, 2016|archive-date=September 23, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160923014140/http://talknerdywithus.com/2016/04/29/exclusive-interview-with-teenagers-creator-mathew-murray|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Bone has cited American actor and filmmaker [[John Cassavetes]] as an influence, along with "people who use their own resources and money to get their projects going when studios or other people ignore them."<ref name=":02">{{Cite web|date=2021-05-13|title=M.H. Murray Talks GHOST, What Audiences Can Glean From It and More|url=https://www.geekgirlauthority.com/m-h-murray-ghost-interview/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210513001358/https://www.geekgirlauthority.com/m-h-murray-ghost-interview/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=May 13, 2021|access-date=2021-05-16|website=Geek Girl Authority|language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Yasmine Alexandra Arrington''' (born February 17, 1993)<ref name="SIMMONS: Jack Kent Cooke's legacy continues to produce winners">{{cite web|last1=Simmons|first1=Deborah|title=SIMMONS: Jack Kent Cooke's legacy continues to produce winners|url=http://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2013/dec/1/simmons-jack-kent-cookes-ultimate-legacy-continues/?page=all|publisher=The Washington Times|access-date=18 November 2015|date=1 December 2013}}</ref>  is the Founder and Executive Director of ScholarCHIPS and a 2015 winner of the Peace First Prize, the JM Kaplan Innovation Prize and DC Social Innovation Prize.<ref name="Peace First Announces 2015 Prize Winners">{{cite web|title=10/27/2015 Peace First Announces 2015 Prize Winners|url=http://www.newprofit.org/peace-first-announces-2015-prize-winners/|website=Newprofit.org|publisher=New Profit|access-date=18 November 2015|date=27 October 2015|archive-date=19 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119005811/http://www.newprofit.org/peace-first-announces-2015-prize-winners/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Early life and education==

Yasmine Arrington was born and grew up in [[Washington, D.C.]]<ref name="CRFW-CRFW 2013 Curvy Spokesmodel Contest">{{cite web|title=CRFW 2013 Curvy Spokesmodel Contest|url=http://www.curvesrockweekend.com/2013curvyspokesmodel.html|publisher=Curves Rock Fashion Weekend|access-date=18 November 2015|archive-date=18 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151118232822/http://www.curvesrockweekend.com/2013curvyspokesmodel.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>  From the time of her infancy until she was a teenager Arrington's father was often in prison.<ref name="Huff Post-Growing Up With an Incarcerated Parent, Learning How to Forgive">{{cite web|last1=Arrington|first1=Yasmine|title=Growing Up With an Incarcerated Parent, Learning How to Forgive|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/yasmine-arrington/growing-up-with-an-incarc_1_b_8178014.html|publisher=Huffington Post|access-date=18 November 2015|date=22 September 2015}}</ref>  Arrington's mother died in her freshman year of high school. She attended [[Benjamin Banneker Academic High School]] in Northwest D.C.,<ref name="SIMMONS: Jack Kent Cooke's legacy continues to produce winners" />  where she was in a program called LearnServe International, a DC non-profit that equips youth to be social changemakers.<ref name="Beyond Inspiring: Meet Yasmine Arrington, Founder Of ScholarCHIPS">{{cite web|last1=Penn|first1=Stephanie|title=Beyond Inspiring: Meet Yasmine Arrington, Founder Of ScholarCHIPS|url=http://dailyvenusdiva.com/2015/09/03/beyond-inspiring-meet-yasmine-arrington-founder-of-scholarchips/|publisher=Daily Venus Diva|access-date=18 November 2015|date=3 September 2015}}</ref>  She studied Strategic Communications and History at [[Elon University]] in [[Elon, North Carolina]].<ref name="CRFW-CRFW 2013 Curvy Spokesmodel Contest" />  Arrington graduated in 2015.<ref name="BISNOW-Fred Abramson's Lasting Legacy">{{cite web|last1=Slavinsky|first1=Roksana|title=Fred Abramson's Lasting Legacy|url=https://www.bisnow.com/washington-dc/news/washington-dc-legal/fred-abramsons-lasting-legacy-47557|publisher=BISNOW|access-date=18 November 2015|date=1 July 2015}}</ref> Arrington is a graduate student at Howard University School of Divinity.

==ScholarCHIPS==


In 2010 Arrington founded ScholarCHIPS, a non-profit organization which provides high school graduates with incarcerated parents mentoring, support and funds to pursue higher education.<ref name="Huff Post-Growing Up With an Incarcerated Parent, Learning How to Forgive" />  As of July 2015 the organizations has given over $180,000 in scholarship funds to 61 scholars pursuing their educations in college.<ref name="Beyond Inspiring: Meet Yasmine Arrington, Founder Of ScholarCHIPS" /> ScholarCHIPS also hosts an annual College Life Skills Conference which provides local youth with training on topics such as [[financial literacy]], how to build credit, sexual health, healthy relationships, and professional development. ScholarCHIPS seeks to break down the stigma and burden of shame that comes with having an incarcerated parent. Today there are over 2 million youth in the United States with a parent in prison.

==Career==
Arrington is a professional plus-size or curvy fashion model<ref name="CRFW-CRFW 2013 Curvy Spokesmodel Contest" /> and motivational speaker. Arrington was named CurvySpokesmodel for Curves Rock Fashion Weekend<ref>{{Cite web|title = CRFW Curvy Spokesmodel Contest|url = http://www.curvesrockweekend.com/2013curvyspokesmodel.html|website = www.curvesrockweekend.com|access-date = 2015-12-12|archive-date = 2015-11-18|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151118232822/http://www.curvesrockweekend.com/2013curvyspokesmodel.html|url-status = dead}}</ref> 2013 and was named October 2015 Curvy Girl of the Month for CurvyGirlChronicles.net,<ref>{{Cite web|title = Kristina Denise|url = http://www.curvygirlchronicles.net/|website = Kristina Denise|access-date = 2015-12-12}}</ref> a blog dedicated to body confidence, healthy curves and inner beauty.

Arrington has worked as a Public Relations intern with the Public Broadcasting Station, an Account Management intern at Ogilvy and Mather and as an Education Fellow with Hager Sharp. '''Jacqueline Toboni''' (born February 18, 1992) is an American actress,<ref name="auto">{{cite web |url=http://zap2it.com/2015/12/nick-wesen-nacht-grimm/ |title=Nick Wesen Nacht Grimm |work=[[Zap2It]]|access-date=28 December 2015 |url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151225202418/http://zap2it.com/2015/12/nick-wesen-nacht-grimm/ |archive-date=25 December 2015}}</ref> known for her role as Theresa "Trubel" Rubel on ''[[Grimm (TV series)|Grimm]]'' (2014–2017).

==Early life and education==
Born February 18, 1992, in San Francisco,<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image-view/659348250/?clipping_id=184332892 Your Horoscope: Birthday Star]. ''The Montreal Gazette''. February 18, 2020. p. A7. Retrieved November 4, 2025.</ref> Toboni graduated from [[St. Ignatius College Preparatory]] in San Francisco in 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.siprep.org/page.cfm?p=7176|title=St. Ignatius College Preparatory, San Francisco, CA: SI Performing Arts Graduates|publisher=[[St. Ignatius College Preparatory]] website|accessdate=December 28, 2015|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160107175249/http://www.siprep.org/page.cfm?p=7176|archivedate=January 7, 2016}}</ref> and from the [[University of Michigan]] in 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.yahoo.com/tv/bp/20-something-student-jacqueline-toboni-on-how-she-landed-a--grimm--tv-gig-in-less-than-a-month-211446285.html|title=20-Something Student Jacqueline Toboni on How She Landed a 'Grimm' TV Gig in Less Than a Month|date=March 21, 2014|publisher=[[Yahoo!]]|accessdate=December 28, 2015|url-status=live|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160120223652/https://www.yahoo.com/tv/bp/20-something-student-jacqueline-toboni-on-how-she-landed-a--grimm--tv-gig-in-less-than-a-month-211446285.html|archivedate=January 20, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/movies/index.ssf/2014/05/grimm_jacqueline_toboni_who_pl.html|title='Grimm': Jacqueline Toboni, who plays 'Trubel,' was cast while still in college|work=[[OregonLive.com]]|date=15 May 2014 |accessdate=December 28, 2015|url-status=live|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160122105106/http://www.oregonlive.com/movies/index.ssf/2014/05/grimm_jacqueline_toboni_who_pl.html|archivedate=January 22, 2016}}</ref>

==Career==
Toboni is known for her recurring role of Trubel in the [[NBC]] drama ''[[Grimm (TV series)|Grimm]]'' from 2014 to 2017.<ref name="auto"/>

In 2015, she appeared on one episode of ''[[Major Crimes (TV series)|Major Crimes]]''.

Beginning in 2016, she also appeared in five episodes of the [[Netflix]] anthology series ''[[Easy (TV series)|Easy]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2016/03/joe-swanberg-easy-anthology-series-nextflix-1201719779/|title=Netflix Sets Joe Swanberg Anthology Series 'Easy'|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|work=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=March 14, 2016|accessdate=October 1, 2020|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160925181758/http://deadline.com/2016/03/joe-swanberg-easy-anthology-series-nextflix-1201719779/|archivedate=September 25, 2016|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2017, she appeared in the sixteenth season of ''[[Hell's Kitchen (American TV series)|Hell's Kitchen]]'' as a guest for episode 11's dinner service that honored the contributors from [[Stand Up to Cancer]].

In 2019, it was announced that she will star in ''[[The L Word: Generation Q]]'', a sequel of the hit series ''[[The L Word]]''. Her lesbian character Sarah Finley is an executive assistant who works for [[Alice Pieszecki|Alice]].

== Personal life ==
On August 18, 2021, Toboni announced her engagement to Australian actress [[Kassandra Clementi]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Toboni Engagement|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/CSu2cI3pmIk/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/s/instagram/CSu2cI3pmIk |archive-date=2021-12-24 |url-access=registration|url-status=live|access-date=2021-08-18|website=www.instagram.com}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-08-19|title=Jacqueline Toboni Is Engaged! She Proposed, Promptly Broke Into Hives, and Still Got the Girl!|url=https://www.autostraddle.com/jacqueline-toboni-engaged/|access-date=2021-08-19|website=Autostraddle|language=en-US}}</ref> However, as of August 7, 2022, Kassandra confirmed via an Instagram comment that she and Jacqueline had "separated awhile{{sic}} ago, amicably".<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-08-09|title=Dr. Chris Brown's ex Kassandra Clementi leaves actress fiancee Jacqueline Toboni for another animal man|url=https://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/entertainment/kassandra-clementi-ends-engagement-with-the-l-word-generation-qs-jacqueline-toboni/news-story/a77f3b5613cfc68d97a80ea40eb63f6c|access-date=2022-11-17|website=Daily Telegraph|language=en-AU}}</ref>

Her brother, [[Paul Toboni]] is the current President of Baseball Operations for [[Major League Baseball]]’s [[Washington Nationals]].<ref>{{Cite web | first=Jeff |last=Passan|date=2025-09-24 |title=Sources: Nationals bringing in Paul Toboni to lead operations |url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/46367899/source-nationals-bringing-paul-toboni-lead-operations | access-date=2025-10-09| publisher=ESPN |language=en}}</ref>

===Winds of Plague===
In 2008, Cruz was asked to join [[Winds of Plague]] and recorded the album ''[[The Great Stone War]]''. The album peaked at No. 72 on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]].<ref name="Billboard 200">{{cite magazine | url={{BillboardURLbyName|artist=winds of plague|chart=Billboard 200}} | title=Winds of Plague – Chart History: Billboard 200 | magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] | publisher=[[Prometheus Global Media]] | accessdate=January 2, 2016}}</ref> In 2011 he performed on the band's next album, ''[[Against the World]]'', which peaked at No. 60 on the ''Billboard'' 200. In 2012, Cruz left Winds of Plague, citing "creative differences".<ref>[http://loudwire.com/winds-of-plague-drummer-art-cruz-go-separate-ways/ Winds of Plague and Drummer Art Cruz Go Their Separate Ways - Loudwire.com]</ref> Cruz returned as their drummer in 2015 and would also perform on the album ''Blood of My Enemy'' in 2017. In 2021, he left Winds of Plague in order to focus on [[Lamb of God (band)|Lamb of God]], which he officially joined in 2019.

===Prong===
[[File:Prong Eier mit Speck 01.jpg|upright=0.85|thumb|Cruz with [[Prong (band)|Prong]] in 2014]]
Following his departure from Winds of Plague, Cruz was asked to play for [[Prong (band)|Prong]]. Cruz has toured and recorded on their album ''[[Songs from the Black Hole (Prong album)|Songs from the Black Hole]]''. Cruz left Prong in 2018.

===Klogr and The Rasmus===
In 2017, Cruz collaborated on drums on the alternative metal project [[Klogr]] for the single "Technocracy" and a European tour with [[The Rasmus]].

===Lamb of God===
In 2018, Cruz filled in for [[Chris Adler]] on [[Lamb of God (band)|Lamb of God]]'s North American tour, which also included supporting [[Slayer]] on their [[Slayer Farewell Tour|farewell tour]].

In 2019, he officially became the drummer for Lamb of God following [[Chris Adler]]'s departure from the band.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://metalinjection.net/latest-news/breakups/lamb-of-god-parts-ways-with-drummer-chris-adler|title=LAMB OF GOD Parts Ways With Drummer Chris Adler; Replacement Announced|date=July 19, 2019|website=Metal Injection|access-date=July 22, 2019}}</ref>

Cruz's first release with Lamb of God was their 2020 [[Lamb of God (album)|self-titled album]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/lamb-of-god-to-release-self-titled-album-in-may-track-listing-cover-artwork-unveiled/|title=LAMB OF GOD To Release Self-Titled Album In May; Track Listing, Cover Artwork Unveiled|publisher=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|accessdate=February 6, 2020|date=February 5, 2020}}</ref>

==Equipment==
Cruz endorses [[Zildjian Cymbals|Zildjian]] cymbals,<ref name="Zildjian">{{cite web | url=https://zildjian.com/blogs/artist/art-cruz| title=Art Cruz | Zildjian Artist}}</ref> and he uses [[Ludwig Drums|Ludwig]] drums, Evans drumheads, Trick pedals, Gibraltar Hardware, and [[Vic Firth]] drumsticks.

[[WWE Performance Center]] | debut = August 25, 2015 }} Joshua "Yeti" Bredl (born January 28, 1991) is an American former professional wrestler, actor, musician, and entrepreneur. He is best known for winning the sixth season of [[WWE Tough Enough]] in 2015, earning a $250,000 prize and a developmental contract with WWE under the ring name The Yeti and later Bronson Matthews. Since his departure from professional wrestling, Bredl has built careers in fitness entrepreneurship, recording under the name Yetskii, and acting. ==Early life and football career== Bredl was born in Thornton, Colorado, and has a younger sister named Brandi Bredl.{{cite web |title=Josh Bredl |url=https://gothunderwolves.com/sports/football/roster/josh-bredl/1505 |website=GoThunderWolves.com |access-date=January 31, 2016}} He attended Horizon High School. Coming out of Horizon, he was ranked the 93rd-best tight end prospect in the nation by ESPN and the 15th-best high school prospect in Colorado by Rivals.com, and was an All-Region and All-Conference selection. He redshirted in 2009 and played as a reserve tight end in 2010 before converting to defensive end. The school listed him at 6 feet 8 inches and 275 pounds. He played defensive end and defensive tackle for the Colorado State University–Pueblo ThunderWolves football team, majoring in exercise science, and was a member of the 2014 NCAA Division II national championship team. In his final season he was an All-Rocky Mountain Athletic Conference honorable mention selection, recording 24 tackles, four sacks and two fumble recoveries; he returned one fumble 66 yards for a touchdown and blocked a field goal attempt in the national championship game.{{cite web |title=Bredl "The Yeti" set for WWE Tough Enough finale Tuesday; Watch Party at Andy Mac's |url=https://gothunderwolves.com/news/2015/8/24/8_24_2015_988 |website=CSU-Pueblo Athletics |date=August 24, 2015 |access-date=October 4, 2026}}{{cite news |last=Cervi |first=Joe E. |date=September 25, 2013 |title=Big family man on campus |work=Pueblo Chieftain}} He also played basketball for the Colorado Hawks. In April 2015 he worked out for the Denver Broncos, and he subsequently signed with the Green Bay Packers as an undrafted free agent.{{cite news |title=Former CSU-Pueblo star Josh Bredl works out with the Broncos |work=The Denver Post |date=April 10, 2015}} Bredl grew up a professional wrestling fan, citing [[Stone Cold Steve Austin]] as his favorite wrestler.{{cite news |last=Nguyen |first=Joe |date=August 26, 2015 |title=Josh Bredl, former CSU-Pueblo star, wins WWE Tough Enough |work=The Denver Post}} ==Professional wrestling career (2015–2017)== ===WWE Tough Enough=== In June 2015, Bredl was announced as one of thirteen finalists for the sixth season of the WWE competition Tough Enough. After surviving elimination three times, he was chosen by fan vote as one of the two winners on August 25, 2015, alongside [[Sara Lee (wrestler)|Sara Lee]], earning a $250,000 prize and a one-year WWE developmental contract, which WWE immediately upgraded to a four-year deal.{{cite web |title=Joshua Bredl: YETSKII, the Trainer Who Designed and Built Justin Bieber's Gym Inside the Webby Award-Winning Compound, Launches Yeti Ultra on Father's Day |url=https://news.columbusnewsonline.com/story/607725/joshua-bredl-yetskii-the-trainer-who-designed-and-built-justin-biebers-gym-inside-the-webby-awardwinning-compound-launches-yeti-ultra-on-fathers-day.html |website=Columbus News Online |date=June 1, 2026 |access-date=June 1, 2026}} Lee was released from WWE in 2016 and died on October 5, 2022, at the age of 30.{{cite web |title=Sara Lee, former WWE wrestler and 'Tough Enough' winner, dies at 30 |url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/10/06/entertainment/wwe-wrestler-sara-lee-dies/ |website=CNN |date=October 6, 2022 |access-date=May 24, 2026}} During the finale, Bredl adopted the ring name The Yeti and wrestled a singles match against Cesaro.{{cite web |title=WWE Tough Enough Recap, August 25, 2015: And The Winners Are... |url=https://www.wwe.com/shows/toughenough/article/tough-enough-recap-august-25-2015 |website=WWE |date=August 25, 2015 |access-date=August 25, 2015}} ===NXT (2015–2016)=== In September 2015, Bredl was assigned to WWE's developmental territory NXT, training at the WWE Performance Center in Orlando, Florida.{{cite web |title=Tough Enough competitors join new class of recruits at the WWE Performance Center |url=https://www.wwe.com/shows/nxt/article/tough-enough-competitors-join-nxt |website=WWE |date=October 28, 2015 |access-date=January 31, 2016}} At an NXT live event on December 3, 2015, he debuted under the ring name Bronson Matthews.{{cite news |title=More On Josh Bredl Debuting New Name, WWE Superstar Turns 35, Live Xavier Woods Taping |work=WrestlingInc |date=December 4, 2015}} In January 2016, Bredl posted a tweet referring to the mid-card stable The Social Outcasts as "Social Jobbers," generating backstage criticism from WWE wrestlers including Cody Rhodes and Kevin Owens, and resulting in a temporary ban from NXT locker rooms.{{cite web |last=Satin |first=Ryan |title=Tough Enough Winner Joshua Bredl Discussed Backstage Backlash from 'Jobber' Tweet |url=https://www.prowrestlingsheet.com/tough-enough-joshua-bredl-backlash-jobber-tweet/ |website=Pro Wrestling Sheet |date=September 1, 2020 |access-date=August 31, 2026}} Bredl wrestled his final match on July 7, 2016, and remained under WWE contract for more than a year afterward.{{cite web |last=Csonka |first=Larry |title=Tough Enough Winner Josh Bredl Still Under WWE Contract |url=https://411mania.com/wrestling/tough-enough-winner-josh-brendl-still-wwe-contract/ |website=411Mania |date=August 10, 2017 |access-date=August 31, 2026}} He was released by WWE on November 5, 2017.{{cite web |title=WWE releases Tough Enough winner Josh Bredl |url=https://www.cagesideseats.com/wwe/2017/11/6/16616490/wwe-releases-tough-enough-winner-josh-bredl |website=Cageside Seats |date=November 6, 2017 |access-date=May 24, 2026}} ==Post-wrestling career== ===Fitness and personal training=== Following his wrestling career, Bredl built a career in the fitness industry as a personal trainer. He became a founding trainer at The Dogpound, a celebrity gym with locations in New York City and West Hollywood, Los Angeles, where his clients included Kelly Rowland, Ricky Martin, Vanessa Hudgens, and Adam Levine.{{cite web |title=Meet Joshua Bredl |url=https://boldjourney.com/meet-joshua-bredl/ |website=Bold Journey |date=June 18, 2024 |access-date=May 28, 2026}} He subsequently founded No Cap Fitness in 2021, later rebranded as Yeti Ultra, an online fitness coaching platform based in Denver, Colorado, which launched on Father's Day, June 21, 2026. In early 2024, Bredl publicly disclosed that he had been hospitalized for 15 days after being diagnosed with sepsis, requiring emergency exploratory surgery. He subsequently adopted a vegan diet.{{cite web |last=Miltner |first=Andrew |date=March 28, 2024 |title=WWE Tough Enough winner Josh Bredl details life-saving surgery he underwent |url=https://www.postwrestling.com/2024/03/28/wwe-tough-enough-winner-josh-bredl-details-life-saving-surgery-he-underwent/ |website=Post Wrestling |access-date=May 24, 2026}} In late 2025, Bredl served as the personal trainer for musician [[Justin Bieber]] during the production of Bieber's live-streamed compound on the Universal Studios backlot in Los Angeles. Bredl designed the gym layout, sourced the equipment list, and oversaw installation of the training facility inside the compound. Bieber trained in the gym during Twitch streams viewed around the world. The production ran from October 2025 through spring 2026 and won two awards at the 30th Annual [[Webby Awards]]: Best Livestream and Creator Launch or Drop.{{cite web |title=Best Livestream — Justin Bieber Livestream on Twitch |url=https://winners.webbyawards.com/2026/creators/creator-excellence/best-livestream/375842/justin-bieber-livestream-on-twitch |website=Webby Awards |access-date=June 1, 2026}}{{cite web |title=Creator Launch or Drop — Justin Bieber Livestream on Twitch |url=https://winners.webbyawards.com/2026/creators/creator-business/creator-launch-or-drop/375842/justin-bieber-livestream-on-twitch |website=Webby Awards |access-date=June 8, 2026}} ===Mixed martial arts=== On April 30, 2022, Bredl made his mixed martial arts debut at Sparta Combat League's Army vs. Marines 13 event. He lost to Alvin Abitz via guillotine choke in the first round.{{cite web |title=Josh Bredl |url=https://www.sherdog.com/fighter/Josh-Bredl-407430 |website=Sherdog |access-date=May 24, 2026}} ===Music=== [[File:Yetskii performing at HazFest 2, 2026.jpg|thumb|Bredl performing as Yetskii at HazFest 2 in Los Angeles, May 2026]] Bredl records and performs as Yetskii.{{cite web |title=Yetskii |url=https://music.apple.com/us/artist/yetskii/1878285617 |website=Apple Music |access-date=May 21, 2026}} Before his debut EP, he released two singles: "pain will guide you" (featuring OJXO) on October 3, 2025, and "shawty like my music" on February 18, 2026.{{cite web |title=shawty like my music – Single |url=https://music.apple.com/us/album/shawty-like-my-music-single/1879412921 |website=Apple Music |access-date=May 25, 2026}} His debut EP, ''Laggin Off a Jet'', was released on March 8, 2026, comprising six tracks: "two tinted into", "bae pull up", "bad guy", "BIG BALOOGA", "considerate" (featuring LiL Crimes), and "WUNDERBAR". The music videos for "BIG BALOOGA" and "bad guy" were released on YouTube.{{cite web |title=YETSKII – BIG BALOOGA (Official Music Video) |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QM2NrmEh4m0 |website=YouTube |access-date=May 25, 2026}}{{cite web |title=YETSKII – bad guy (Official Music Video) |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g6Il5myx3k4 |website=YouTube |access-date=June 28, 2026}} He performed at HazFest 2, a free multi-genre music festival co-presented by Metal Edge magazine and held in Los Angeles on May 16, 2026.{{cite web |date=May 20, 2026 |title=No Barriers, No Boundaries: Hazfest 2 Was L.A. at Its Most Alive |url=https://metaledgemag.com/blogs/homepage-featured/no-barriers-no-boundaries-hazfest2-was-l-a-at-its-most-alive |website=Metal Edge |access-date=October 16, 2026}} ===Acting=== Bredl has appeared in WWE television programming and has pursued film and television roles. He was cast as Mr. Large in the horror film ''You Lose You Die'', directed by Carlos Suarez and co-starring Freddy Rodriguez, Charlotte Flair, and Anuel AA.{{cite web |title=Josh Bredl |url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm7467261/ |website=IMDb |access-date=May 21, 2026}}{{cite web |last=Al-Ghamdi |first=Abdullah |date=May 14, 2024 |title=WWE's Charlotte Flair To Lead Horror Movie You Lose You Die |url=https://www.comingsoon.net/movies/news/1718217-charlotte-flair-wwe-horror-movie-you-lose-you-die |website=ComingSoon.net |access-date=October 16, 2026}}{{cite web |last=Thompson |first=Andrew |date=May 14, 2024 |title=Charlotte Flair starring in horror/thriller titled 'You Lose You Die' |url=https://www.postwrestling.com/2024/05/14/charlotte-flair-starring-in-horror-thriller-titled-you-lose-you-die/ |website=POST Wrestling |access-date=October 16, 2026}}{{cite web |last=Cordero |first=Rosy |date=May 14, 2024 |title=Freddy Rodriguez & Ashley Elizabeth Fliehr To Lead Indie Horror Feature 'You Lose You Die' |url=https://deadline.com/2024/05/freddy-rodriguez-ashley-elizabeth-fliehr-cast-film-you-lose-you-die-1235914167/ |website=Deadline |access-date=May 22, 2026}} ===Entrepreneurship and digital media=== Bredl is a co-founder of Portal Health AI, a guided peptide optimization platform offering personalized health protocols developed by human coaches and nurses, with an AI agent available to clients around the clock. In December 2025, Bredl executive-produced a custom Game Boy Color for Justin Bieber, featuring an original 8-bit game titled ''Skylark Island'', built in collaboration with developer Alex Constante. The project was covered by Complex Style.{{cite web |title=Swag! Justin Bieber was gifted a custom Swagboy Color by @yetihood |url=https://www.threads.net/@complexstyle/post/DSp5NCFkcyd/ |website=Complex Style on Threads |date=December 24, 2025 |access-date=June 28, 2026}} ==Filmography== ===Film=== {| class="wikitable" ! |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221031105102/https://dotesports.com/dota-2/news/tundra-esports-dominates-the-dota-2-world-sweeps-team-secret-to-lift-the-aegis-at-ti11 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |author=Titas Khan |date=2025-09-15 |title=Ame remains uncrowned as Team Falcons outclass Xtreme Gaming in TI 2025 final |url=https://dotesports.com/dota-2/news/falcons-wins-ti-2025 |access-date=2025-09-15 |website=Dot Esports |language=en-US |archive-date=September 30, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250930040140/https://dotesports.com/dota-2/news/falcons-wins-ti-2025 |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Kurtis attended the [[University of British Columbia]] before dropping out to play ''Dota 2'' professionally full-time. His parents were initially skeptical of his career choice but eventually accepted it as he won more tournaments.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ubyssey.ca/features/our-campus-kurtis-ling-esports-dota-311/|title=Our Campus: In the eSports ring, Kurtis Ling is king|last=Wright|first=Nikos|website=The Ubyssey|access-date=2016-03-03|archive-date=March 6, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306052030/http://ubyssey.ca/features/our-campus-kurtis-ling-esports-dota-311/|url-status=live}}</ref>

== History ==
EG acquired Ling from [[Cloud9 (esports)|Cloud9]] in January 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.dailydot.com/esports/evil-geniuses-cloud9-aui-2000/|title = Evil Geniuses in talks with Cloud9 to acquire AUI 2000|website = [[The Daily Dot]]|date = 31 December 2014|access-date = April 22, 2016|archive-date = December 8, 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151208123856/http://www.dailydot.com/esports/evil-geniuses-cloud9-aui-2000/|url-status = live}}</ref>

On August 14, Aui_2000 was kicked off of the team just days after winning TI5. [[Artour "Arteezy" Babaev]] replaced him on the roster.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kotaku.com.au/2015/08/evil-geniuses-decided-to-kick-one-of-their-new-millionaires-before-the-international-finished/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150818211140/http://www.kotaku.com.au/2015/08/evil-geniuses-decided-to-kick-one-of-their-new-millionaires-before-the-international-finished/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=August 18, 2015|title=Evil Geniuses Decided To Kick One Of Their New Millionaires Before The International Finished|first=Alex|last=Walker|website=[[Kotaku]]|date=August 18, 2015|accessdate=December 1, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ecumenicalnews.com/article/dota-2-professional-player-aui-2000-kicked-out-of-evil-geniuses-replaced-by-team-secrets-arteezy-32745|title=Dota 2' professional player AUI_2000 replaced in Evil Geniuses by Team Secret's Arteezy|first=Bryan|last=Ke|website=[[Ecumenical News]]|date=August 20, 2015|access-date=March 5, 2016|archive-date=February 17, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160217050841/http://www.ecumenicalnews.com/article/dota-2-professional-player-aui-2000-kicked-out-of-evil-geniuses-replaced-by-team-secrets-arteezy-32745|url-status=live}}</ref> His sudden dismissal after winning the ''Dota 2'' championships sparked some outrage from the community,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.reddit.com/r/DotA2/comments/3h1uco/aui_2000_claims_he_was_kicked_from_eg|title=Aui_2000 claims he was kicked from EG.|website=reddit.com/r/dota2|date=15 August 2015|access-date=2016-03-05}}</ref> and forced team captain Peter "ppd" Dager to write a blog detailing the reasons behind Aui_2000's removal from the team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://peterpandam.blogspot.com/2015/08/post-ti5-blog.html|title=POST TI5 blog|first=Peter|last=Dager|website=peterpandam.blogspot.com|date=August 18, 2015|access-date=March 5, 2016|archive-date=March 8, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160308023037/http://peterpandam.blogspot.com/2015/08/post-ti5-blog.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Shortly after being kicked from EG, Ling formed his own team, [[Digital Chaos]], but struggled to achieve any significant results. On March 25, following the abrupt departure of [[Artour "Arteezy" Babaev]] and [[Saahil "UNiVeRsE" Arora]] from Evil Geniuses, Ling announced that he would be rejoining the team.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://evilgeniuses.gg/Read/561,Evil-Geniuses-Announces-Dota-2-Roster-Changes/ | title = Evil Geniuses Announces Dota 2 Roster Changes | date = March 25, 2016 | accessdate = March 26, 2016 | archive-date = March 28, 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160328123152/http://evilgeniuses.gg/Read/561,Evil-Geniuses-Announces-Dota-2-Roster-Changes/ | url-status = dead }}</ref> Ling was kicked from the team once again after the [[Manila Major 2016]] in June.<ref>{{cite web|title=Zai Returns to World Champions Evil Geniuses|url=https://pvplive.net/c/zai-returns-to-eg|website=PVP Live|accessdate=14 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160614020407/https://pvplive.net/c/zai-returns-to-eg|archive-date=14 June 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

For the 2017 season, Aui_2000 joined Team NP. They managed to qualify for [[The International 2017]] before being signed by the Cloud9 organization.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cloud9 signs Team NP, bringing old members back into the brand|url=https://dotesports.com/dota-2/cloud-9-dota-signs-team-np-16043|website=dotesports.com|date=21 July 2017|access-date=9 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171010004817/https://dotesports.com/dota-2/cloud-9-dota-signs-team-np-16043|archive-date=10 October 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> They were eliminated during the first round of the Lower Bracket by Team Empire.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cloud 9 are eliminated from The International 7 by Team Empire |url=http://www.gosugamers.net/dota2/news/45110-cloud-9-are-eliminated-from-the-international-7-by-team-empire|website=gosugamers.net|date=8 August 2017|accessdate=8 August 2017}}</ref>

For the 2018 season, Aui_2000 joined Forward Gaming as a coach.<ref>{{cite web|title=Forward Gaming Dota 2 Roster Changes|url=https://forward.gg/2019/04/30/dota-2-roster-changes-2|access-date=2019-07-18|archive-date=2019-07-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190718042856/https://forward.gg/2019/04/30/dota-2-roster-changes-2/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On July 21, 2019, Forward Gaming was dissolved;<ref>{{cite web|title=Forward Gaming Termination|url=https://forward.gg/2019/07/21/forward-gaming-termination|access-date=July 22, 2019|archive-date=December 11, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211044600/https://forward.gg/2019/07/21/forward-gaming-termination|url-status=dead}}</ref> the roster was then signed to represent Chinese organization [[Newbee]] at [[The International 2019]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Newbee Picks Up Ex Forward Gaming Roaster for TI9|date=25 July 2019|url=https://dotesports.com/dota-2/news/newbee-picks-up-ex-forward-gaming-roster-for-ti9|access-date=August 13, 2019|archive-date=July 27, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190727133252/https://dotesports.com/dota-2/news/newbee-picks-up-ex-forward-gaming-roster-for-ti9|url-status=live}}</ref>

In August 2026, following Team Falcons' run at The International 2026, Ling said that he did not intend to continue his Dota 2 career and believed the 2026 season would likely be his last, as he cited the strain of frequent travel<ref>{{cite web|last=Khuzhenov|first=Ruslan|title=Aui_2000: "I think this was my last season in Dota 2"|url=https://esports.ru/dota-2/news/aui-2000-rasskazal-o-planah-zavershit-kareru-v-dota-2/|website=Esports.ru|date=August 24, 2026|access-date=August 26, 2026}}</ref>

'''Mark-Anthony Greene''', better known by his stage name '''Skrizzy''' and formerly known as '''Young Scrap''', is an American rapper, singer and songwriter.<ref name="hhv">{{cite news|url=http://www.hip-hopvibe.com/2014/06/13/hhv-exclusive-young-scrap-talks-west-coast-success-love-la-faded-ambition-and-more/|title=HHV Exclusive:Young Scrap talks West Coast success, "Love LA," "Faded Ambition," and more|work=HipHopVibe|date=June 13, 2014|access-date=March 20, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://hhbmedia.com/blog/2015/12/28/young-scrap-introduces-us-to-trill-b/|title=YOUNG SCRAP INTRODUCES US TO TRILL & B|work=HipHop Battle Media|last=Tucker|first=Tisha|date=December 28, 2015|access-date=March 20, 2016}}</ref> His single titled "Love L.A" from his ''Faded Ambition'' album charted at No.{{Nbsp}}18 on the ''[[Billboard charts|Billboard]]'' [[Billboard Twitter Real-Time|Twitter Top Tracks]] during the week of July{{Nbsp}}12, 2016.<ref name="billboard">{{cite news|url=http://www.billboard.com/charts/twitter-top-tracks/2014-07-12|title=The Week of July 12, 2014|work=[[Billboard Twitter Real-Time|Billboard Twitter Top Tracks]]|date=July 7, 2014|access-date=March 19, 2016}}</ref> He is also credited as writing [[V.I.C. (rapper)|V.I.C.]]'s song titled "Twerk It" & “Wobble” which charted at No.{{Nbsp}}69 on the ''Billboard'' [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mtv.com/artists/young-scrap/biography/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140822183451/http://www.mtv.com/artists/young-scrap/biography/|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 22, 2014|title=Young Scrap Biography|work=[[MTV]]|access-date=March 20, 2016}}</ref>

==Early life and career==
Skrizzy performed with [[Debbie Allen]] and [[Savion Glover]] until he moved to [[Maryland]]. While in his [[Sophomore|second year]] in high school, he released his first album titled ''Puppy Power'' under his uncle's record label and in 2008 he signed a recording contract with [[Universal Music Group]] under which he released the single "The Melody" which was positively received among music fans.<ref name="hhv"/>

On September 12, 2016, Skrizzy released the first of his "Music We Can Fuck To" series titled ''Music We Can Fuck Too'' which featured [[guest appearance]]s from notable rappers like [[Yo Gotti]] and [[V.I.C. (rapper)|V.I.C]].{{citation needed|date=July 2023}} His [[Jahlil Beats]]-produced single titled "Love L.A" charted at No. 18 during the week of July 12, 2016, on the ''[[Billboard charts|Billboard]]'' [[Billboard Twitter Real-Time|Twitter Top Tracks]].<ref name="billboard" /> On August 4, 2016, he released a [[mixtape]] titled ''Faded Ambition'' with a guest appearance from [[Lil Wayne]] and music production from producers [[DJ Mustard]] and Jahlil Beats.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.thefader.com/2013/10/17/download-young-scraps-music-we-can-fuck-to-5-mixtape/|title=Download Young Scrap's Music We Can Fuck To 5 Mixtape|work=[[The Fader]]|last=Garvey|first=Meaghan|date=October 17, 2013|access-date=March 20, 2016}}</ref> On June 20, 2016, Skrizzy released ''[[Trill and B]]'', a project he started recording in 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://respect-mag.com/2016/06/young-scrap-rebrands-love-trill-b/|title=Young Scrap Rebrands Love On "Trill and B"|work=[[Respect. (magazine)|RESPECT.]]|last=Mayo|first=Jake|date=June 24, 2016|access-date=June 24, 2016}}</ref>

In 2016 Skrizzy's career path was put on hold due to [[thyroid cancer]] while also dealing with the loss of his voice, putting a pause on any new music releases for 2 years.{{Cn|date=September 2024}} On June 21, 2020, Skrizzy released a slew of new music including "Undercover hoe" which featured [[24hrs (rapper)|24hrs]]. Covering the track, [[HotNewHipHop]] said "both artists can be heard lamenting about their issues with women and how some just want to play games, while hiding their true intentions".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cole |first=Alexander |date=2020-06-21 |title=Skrizzy & 24hrs Are Done With The Games On "Undercover Hoe" |url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/259420-skrizzy-and-24hrs-are-done-with-the-games-on-undercover-hoe-new-song |access-date=2024-02-28 |website=HotNewHipHop |language=en}}</ref>

Taking a hiatus until July 11, 2021,{{Cn|date=September 2024}} Skrizzy released "Troublesome" featuring [[South Carolina]] rapper [[Renni Rucci]] which also premiered with [[HotNewHipHop|HotNewHiphop]] who said Skrizzy and Renni Rucci are the perfect duo.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Powell |first=Jon |title=Skrizzy and Renni Rucci are "Troublesome" on new single |url=https://www.revolt.tv/article/2021-07-02/50020/skrizzy-and-renni-rucci-are-troublesome-on-new-single |access-date=2024-02-28 |website=REVOLT}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Quinitchett |first=Kevin |date=2021-07-11 |title=Skrizzy & Renni Rucci Make A "Troublesome" Pair |url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/338064-skrizzy-and-renni-rucci-make-a-troublesome-pair-new-song |access-date=2024-09-24 |website=HotNewHipHop |language=en}}</ref> Skrizzy announced an R&B album, titled ''I'm Not Toxic, You Are'', to be released July 26, 2024, along with a rap album tentatively titled ''I'm Not A Rapper 2'' which is slated for release October 25, 2024.{{Cn|date=September 2024}}{{Update needed|date=September 2024}}

'''Ashleigh Murray''' (born January 18, 1988)<ref>{{cite news|last=Rose|first=Mike|title=Today's famous birthdays list for January 18, 2023 includes celebrities Kevin Costner, Dave Bautista|website=[[The Plain Dealer]]|date=January 18, 2023|accessdate=January 18, 2023|url=https://www.cleveland.com/entertainment/2023/01/todays-famous-birthdays-list-for-january-18-2023-includes-celebrities-kevin-costner-dave-bautista.html}}</ref> is an American actress and singer. She is best known for her [[breakthrough role]] as [[Josie McCoy]], the lead singer of the fictional band [[Josie and the Pussycats (comics)|Josie and the Pussycats]], on [[The CW]] television series ''[[Riverdale (American TV series)|Riverdale]]'', in which she appeared from 2017 to 2019. Murray reprised the role in the spin‑off series ''[[Katy Keene (TV series)|Katy Keene]]'' (2020) and later returned to ''Riverdale'' as a guest star in 2021 and 2023. Her film credits include ''[[Deidra & Laney Rob a Train]]'' (2017) and ''[[Valley Girl (2020 film)|Valley Girl]]'' (2020), and she has also starred in the television series ''[[Tom Swift (TV series)|Tom Swift]]'' (2022) and ''[[The Other Black Girl (TV series)|The Other Black Girl]]'' (2023).

==Early life and education==
Murray was born on January 18, 1988, in [[Kansas City, Missouri]]. She developed an interest in acting at age ten after appearing in a school play. Following high school, she moved to [[New York City]] to study at the [[New York Conservatory for Dramatic Arts]], graduating in 2009.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Garland|first=May|date=July 13, 2022|title=Interview - Ashleigh Murray|url=https://schonmagazine.com/interview-ashleigh-murray/|access-date=August 21, 2023|website=[[Schön!]]|archive-date=July 13, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220713204637/https://schonmagazine.com/interview-ashleigh-murray/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Vulnerable In Your Acting - Ashleigh Murray |publisher=[[New York Conservatory for Dramatic Arts]]|date=September 4, 2018|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t863uWo1SoQ|via=[[YouTube]]|access-date=August 21, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230821012519/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t863uWo1SoQ|archive-date=August 21, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Career==
In 2016, Murray was cast as a series regular in [[The CW]] teen drama ''[[Riverdale (American TV series)|Riverdale]]'', portraying [[Josie McCoy]], described as "a gorgeous, snooty and ambitious girl who is the lead singer for the popular band Josie and the Pussycats".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2016/02/riverdale-archie-cast-kj-apa-cw-pilot-1201708847/|title=''Riverdale'' Finds Its Archie & Josie: KJ Apa To Topline CW Pilot|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=February 24, 2016|accessdate=February 25, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/entry/ashleigh-murray-josie-and-the-pussycats-spinoff_us_58debb96e4b0ba359594e5c8/|title=''Riverdale'' Star Ashleigh Murray Would Absolutely Do A ''Josie And The Pussycats'' Spinoff|last=Delbyck|first=Cole|work=[[HuffPost]]|date=March 31, 2017|accessdate=April 18, 2017}}</ref> The show premiered in 2017, and Murray remained a cast member until 2019. Her own singing voice is used in all of her performance scenes as Josie and the Pussycats, although she has stated that she is not interested in pursuing a professional singing career.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Williams|first=Kori|date=October 29, 2021|title='Riverdale' Star Ashleigh Murray Is an Actress - but Is She Also a Singer?|url=https://www.distractify.com/p/can-ashleigh-murray-really-sing|access-date=August 21, 2023|website=[[Distractify]]|archive-date=November 28, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211128063625/https://www.distractify.com/p/can-ashleigh-murray-really-sing|url-status=live}}</ref> In February 2019, it was announced that Murray would reprise her role as Josie McCoy as part of the main cast of the ''Riverdale'' spin‑off pilot ''[[Katy Keene]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2019/02/katy-keene-ashleigh-murray-star-the-cw-riverdale-spinoff-pilot-1202549634/|title=''Katy Keene'': Ashleigh Murray To Star In the CW's ''Riverdale'' Spinoff Pilot|last=Petski|first=Denise|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=February 4, 2019|accessdate=February 5, 2019}}</ref> In May 2019, The CW ordered ''Katy Keene'' to series.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tvline.com/casting-news/riverdale-ashleigh-murray-leaving-josie-katy-keene-1053904/|title=''Riverdale'': Ashleigh Murray to Exit, Following ''Katy Keene'' Series Order|last=Nemetz|first=Dave|website=[[TVLine]]|date=May 7, 2019|access-date=May 8, 2019}}</ref> ''Katy Keene'' was canceled after one season in July 2020<ref>{{Cite web|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|date=July 2, 2020|title='Katy Keene' Canceled By The CW After One Season; 'Riverdale' Spinoff To Look For New Home|url=https://deadline.com/2020/07/katy-keene-canceled-the-cw-one-season-no-season-2-riverdale-spinoff-series-shopped-new-home-1202976671/|access-date=August 21, 2023|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|archive-date=July 3, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200703060847/https://deadline.com/2020/07/katy-keene-canceled-the-cw-one-season-no-season-2-riverdale-spinoff-series-shopped-new-home-1202976671/|url-status=live}}</ref> and Murray returned to ''Riverdale'' as a guest star in 2021 and 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Humphrey|first=Julia|date=July 14, 2023|title='Riverdale's' Final Season Is Bringing Back a Fan-Favorite Character|url=https://collider.com/riverdale-season-7-ashleigh-murray-josie-mccoy/|access-date=August 21, 2023|website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]]|archive-date=July 15, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230715114509/https://collider.com/riverdale-season-7-ashleigh-murray-josie-mccoy/|url-status=live}}</ref>

'''Charone Eric Peake'''<ref name="RMON">{{cite web | title=Profile | work=rostermon.com | url=http://www.rostermon.com/player/6223/ | access-date=June 16, 2016 | archive-date=August 8, 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160808173602/http://www.rostermon.com/player/6223/ | url-status=dead }}</ref> (born October 16, 1992) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[wide receiver]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson]]. Peake was selected by the [[New York Jets]] in the seventh round of the [[2016 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Peake played both the [[U.S. Army All-American game]] and Shrine Bowl. He was a ''[[USA Today]]'' Second-team [[All-American]] and ranked the 14th overall player in the nation by [[ESPN]]. Peake was rated as 50th overall player in the nation by [[247Sports.com]].  Peake was also ranked the 73rd player in the nation by [[Scout.com]], ranked 66th overall player in the nation by ''[[Sporting News]]'' and was ranked as the 83rd overall player in the nation by [[Rivals.com]]. Peake was a finalist for Mr. Football in South Carolina where he helped his [[Dorman High School]] football team to the state championship game. In his senior season at high school, Peake had 65 [[Reception (gridiron football)|receptions]] for 1,053 yards and nine receiving [[touchdown]]s and had 18 [[Carry (gridiron football)|carries]] for 120 rushing yards. Peake was named region Male Student-Athlete-of-the-Year in senior season. In his senior season at high school, Peake 52 receptions for 881 receiving yards and nine receiving touchdowns and 41 carries for 319 rushing yards. He had 19 catches for 300 receiving yards in his sophomore season.

==College career==
Peake was named to the [[Biletnikoff Award]] Watch List member prior to the preseason of his junior season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 16, 2013 |title=Watkins and Peake Named to Biletnikoff Watch List |url=http://www.clemsontigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=208697369 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160603184405/http://www.clemsontigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=208697369 |archive-date=June 3, 2016 |access-date=July 16, 2013 |website=Clemson Tigers Athletics}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=2013 Biletnikoff Award Pre-season Watch List Released | work=biletnikoffaward.com | url=http://biletnikoffaward.com/2013-biletnikoff-award-pre-season-watch-list-released |access-date=July 16, 2013}}</ref> Peake was named to [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) Academic Honor Roll at Clemson in his junior season.

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
On January 21, 2016, it was announced that Peake would be playing in the [[2016 Senior Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crumpton |first=Tony |date=January 21, 2016 |title=Clemson WR to play in Reese's Senior Bowl |url=https://www.tigernet.com/update/Clemson-WR-to-play-in-Reeses-Senior-Bowl-22261 |access-date=December 29, 2017 |website=TigerNet.com}}</ref> Throughout the week leading up to the [[Senior Bowl]], Peake impressed many team representatives and scouts and was praised for his route running ability and speed.<ref>{{cite web| title=Charone Peake Just Made Himself Some Money| url=https://www.rubbingtherock.com/2016/01/30/charone-peake-just-made-himself-some-money/amp/| access-date=December 29, 2017| website=RubbingtheRock.com| author=Andrew Boardwine| archive-date=December 29, 2017| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171229231655/https://rubbingtherock.com/2016/01/30/charone-peake-just-made-himself-some-money/amp/| url-status=dead}}</ref> On January 30, 2016, Peake caught two passes for 13-yards and helped [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] head coach [[Gus Bradley]]'s South team that defeated the North 27–13.<ref>{{cite web| title=ESPN.com: 2016 Senior Bowl stats/box score| url=http://www.espn.com/college-football/boxscore?gameId=400859832| access-date=December 29, 2017| website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He was one of 43 collegiate [[wide receiver]]s to receive an invitation to the [[NFL Scouting Combine]] in [[Indianapolis, Indiana]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Here's the complete list of players invited to the 2016 NFL Combine, led by 14 from Ohio State| url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2016/2/11/10967624/2016-nfl-scouting-combine-invited-players-list-ohio-state| access-date=December 29, 2017| website=SBNation.com| author=Katie Sharp| date=February 11, 2016}}</ref> Peake completed all of the combine drills and ran the sixth fastest [[40-yard dash]] time among all wide receivers.<ref>{{cite web| title=Who Ran the Best 40 Among WRs at the Combine?| url=https://www.scout.com/Article/2016-NFL-Combine-40-Yard-Dash-Times-for-Wide-Receivers-75007217/Amp| access-date=December 29, 2017| website=Scout.com| date=February 27, 2016}}</ref> On March 10, 2016, Peake opted to participate at Clemson's pro day, along with [[Kevin Dodd]], [[Mackensie Alexander]], [[T. J. Green]], [[Jayron Kearse]], [[Shaq Lawson]], and then others. Team representatives and scouts from all 32 NFL team attended, including head coaches [[Rex Ryan]] ([[Buffalo Bills]]), [[Marvin Lewis]] ([[Cincinnati Bengals]]), [[Mike Tomlin]] ([[Pittsburgh Steelers]]), and [[Chuck Pagano]] ([[Indianapolis Colts]]), as Peake performed positional drills and also chose to run the [[40-yard dash]] (4.38[[second|s]]), 20-yard dash (2.55s), and 10-yard dash (1.50s).<ref>{{cite web| title=Clemson pro day looms large for Mackensie Alexander, Kevin Dodd and others| url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/acc/clemson-university/article65132392.html| access-date=December 29, 2017| website=thestate.com| author=Dan Hope| date=March 9, 2016}}</ref> Peake's unofficial time of 4.38 in the 40-yard dash would've finished third among all receivers at the NFL combine, behind [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame's]] [[Will Fuller]] and [[TCU Horned Frogs football|TCU's]] [[Kolby Listenbee]]. Although he experienced a few drops during receiving drills, Peake's overall performance was still well received by scouts and draft analysts.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brandt |first=Gil  |author-link=Gil Brandt |date=March 12, 2016 |title=Four NFL head coaches attend Clemson Pro Day |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/four-nfl-head-coaches-attend-clemson-s-pro-day-0ap3000000644017 |access-date=December 29, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> At the conclusion of the pre-draft process, Peake was projected to be a third or fourth round pick by NFL draft experts and scouts. ===New York Jets===
====2016====
The [[New York Jets]] selected Peake in the seventh round (241st overall) of the [[2016 NFL draft]].<ref name="i493">{{cite web |last=Butchko |first=John |date=2016-04-30 |title=Jets Select Charone Peake With the 241st Pick in the 2016 NFL Draft |url=http://www.ganggreennation.com/2016/4/30/11546096/jets-select-charone-peake-with-the-241st-pick-in-the-2016-nfl-draft |access-date=2024-08-06 |website=Gang Green Nation|publisher=SB Nation}}</ref> Peake was the 32nd wide receiver selected in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2016/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He unexpectedly fell in the draft, although he was projected to be a third round pick by [[NFL.com]] and a third or fourth by [[CBS Sports]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Jets draft Clemson receiver Charone Peake in 7th round| url=https://www.nj.com/jets/index.ssf/2016/04/jets_draft_clemson_receiver_charone_peake_in_7th_r.amp| access-date=December 29, 2017| website=nj.com| author=Darryl Slater| date=April 30, 2016}}{{Dead link|date=November 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> On May 12, 2016, the Jets signed Peake to a four-year, $2.40 million [[contract]] that includes a [[signing bonus]] of $68,382.<ref>{{cite web| title=Spotrac.com: Charone Peake contract| url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/new-york-jets/charone-peake-19195/| access-date=December 29, 2017| website=Spotrac.com}}</ref>

Throughout [[training camp]], he competed for a roster spot against [[Quincy Enunwa]], [[Kenbrell Thompkins]], [[Kyle Williams (wide receiver, born 1988)|Kyle Williams]], [[Chandler Worthy]], [[Jeremy Ross]], [[Titus Davis]], [[Robby Anderson]], and [[Jalin Marshall]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: New York Jets depth chart: 07/01/2016| url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/185/NYJ| access-date=December 29, 2017| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> Head coach [[Todd Bowles]] named him the sixth wide receiver on the depth chart, behind [[Brandon Marshall]], [[Eric Decker]], Jalin Marshall, Enunwa, and Anderson.<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: New York Jets depth chart: 10/01/2016| url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/185/NYJ| access-date=December 29, 2017| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

He made his professional regular season debut in the Jets' season-opening 23–22 loss to the Bengals. On October 2, 2016, Peake scored his first professional touchdown in an unusual occurrence when Jets' quarterback [[Ryan Fitzpatrick]] fumbled the ball forward to Peake, who recovered it and ran 40-yards for the a touchdown. He also made his first career reception on a 16-yard pass by Ryan Fitzpatrick in the second quarter and finished with three catches for 30-yards in their 27–17 loss to the [[Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Game Center: Week 4-2016: Seattle Sea hawks @ New York Jets| url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2016100206/2016/REG4/seahawks@jets| access-date=December 29, 2017| website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Hanzus|first1=Dan|title=Jets rookie Charone Peake scores weird TD|website=[[NFL.com]] |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000713831/article/jets-rookie-charone-peake-scores-weird-td|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161005220313/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000713831/article/jets-rookie-charone-peake-scores-weird-td|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 5, 2016|access-date=October 2, 2016}}</ref> He earned his first playing time on offense due to injuries to Decker and Jalin Marshall.<ref name="j782">{{cite web | last=Myers | first=Keith | title=Seahawks vs Jets: inactives analysis | website=12th Man Rising | date=2016-10-02 | url=https://12thmanrising.com/2016/10/02/seahawks-vs-jets-inactives-analysis/ | access-date=2024-08-06}}</ref> On October 17, 2016, Peake caught a season-high five passes for 43-yards during a 28–3 loss at the [[Arizona Cardinals]]. In Week 9, Peake earned his first career start during a 27–23 loss to the [[Miami Dolphins]]. Peake was inactive for a Week 12 matchup against the [[New England Patriots]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Inactives for Jets vs Patriots| url=https://www.northjersey.com/amp/94517284| access-date=December 29, 2017| website=northjersey.com| author=Andy Vasquez}}</ref> He finished the {{NFL Year|2016}} season with 19 receptions for 186 receiving yards in 15 games and one start.<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Charone Peake (2016)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/charonepeake/2555477/gamelogs?season=2016| access-date=December 29, 2017| website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2017====
Peake entered training camp competing for one of the starting wide receiver jobs after the departures of Brandon Marshall and Decker on free agency. He competed against Anderson, [[ArDarius Stewart]], [[Chad Hansen]], [[Myles White]], and Frank Hammond. Head coach Todd Bowles named him the Jets' fourth wide receiver on the depth chart after they traded the [[Seattle Seahawks]] for Jermaine Kearse and signed [[Jeremy Kerley]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Jets put Charone Peake on injured reserve, sign Travaris Cadet| url=https://www.nj.com/jets/index.ssf/2017/09/jets_put_charone_peake_on_injured_reserve_sign_tra.amp| access-date=December 29, 2017| website=NJ.com| author=Connor Hughes| date=September 27, 2017}}{{Dead link|date=November 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

On September 24, 2017, Peake suffered an ankle.injury during the Jets' 20–6 victory over the Dolphins. On September 27, 2017, the Jets placed Peake on [[injured reserve]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Greenberg|first1=Ethan|title=Jets Sign RB-KR Cadet, Place Peake on IR|url=http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-7/Jets-Sign-RB-KR-Cadet-Place-Peake-on-IR/b9667bdd-0060-41c9-912f-21861702c4fe|website=NewYorkJets.com|access-date=September 27, 2017|date=September 27, 2017}}</ref>

On August 31, 2019, Peake was released by the Jets.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Announce 38 Moves to Get Down to 53-Man Roster|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-announce-38-moves-to-get-down-to-53-man-roster|author=Lange, Randy|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=August 31, 2019}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
On January 2, 2020, Peake signed a reserve/future contract with the Jaguars.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaguars Make Roster Moves|url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/jaguars-make-roster-moves-x2400|website=Jaguars.com|date=January 2, 2020|access-date=January 3, 2020|archive-date=November 18, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201118150051/https://www.jaguars.com/news/jaguars-make-roster-moves-x2400|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was released on April 27, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=Offseason Update: Undrafted free agents bring rookie class to 30|url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/offseason-update-undrafted-free-agents-bring-rookie-class-to-30|author=Oehser, John|website=Jaguars.com|date=April 27, 2020}}</ref>

===Saskatchewan Roughriders===
Peake signed with the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) on January 8, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Riders Transactions – January 8 |url=https://www.riderville.com/2021/01/08/riders-transactions-january-8/ |website=Riderville.com |date=January 8, 2021 |access-date=February 16, 2021}}</ref> He was released among the final training camp cuts on July 30, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Roughriders trim roster ahead of 2021 season |url=https://www.riderville.com/2021/07/30/roughriders-trim-roster-ahead-of-2021-season/ |website=Riderville.com |date=July 30, 2021 |access-date=August 2, 2021}}</ref>

===Ottawa Redblacks===
On August 2, 2021, it was announced that Peake had signed with the [[Ottawa Redblacks]] of the CFL.<ref>{{cite news |title=Redblacks add REC Charone Peake among five roster moves |url=https://www.cfl.ca/2021/08/02/redblacks-add-rec-charone-peake-among-five-roster-moves/ |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |date=July 30, 2021 |access-date=August 2, 2021}}</ref> He was released on February 14, 2023.

[[Jett Cleary]] (brother) }} }} '''Nathan Cleary''' (born 14 November 1997) is an Australian professional [[rugby league]] footballer who co-captains and plays as a {{rlp|hb}} for the [[Penrith Panthers]] in the [[NRL]]. Widely considered one of the best players in the modern era, Cleary was {{rlp|hb}} in five consecutive grand finals from [[2020 NRL Grand Final|2020]]–[[2024 NRL Grand Final|2024]]. He was co-captain in four straight grand finals wins ([[2021 NRL Grand Final|2021]], [[2022 NRL Grand Final|2022]], [[2023 NRL Grand Final|2023]], [[2024 NRL Grand Final|2024]]) and received the [[Clive Churchill Medal]] as man of the match in the [[2021 NRL Grand Final|2021]] and [[2023 NRL Grand Final|2023]] grand finals. Cleary was awarded [[Dally M Awards|Dally M]] Player of Year in 2026 and [[Dally M Awards|Dally M]] Halfback of The Year in [[2020 Dally M Awards|2020]], [[2021 Dally M Awards|2021]], [[2025 Dally M Awards|2025]] and [[2026 Dally M Awards|2026]]. He was also awarded the [[State of Origin series|Wally Lewis Medal]] as player of the [[2026 State of Origin series]] and became [[New South Wales rugby league team records|New South Wales]] highest all-time points scorer. Cleary was a part of [[State of Origin series|New South Wales]] [[2018 State of Origin series|2018]], [[2019 State of Origin series|2019]], [[2021 State of Origin series|2021]] and [[2026 State of Origin series|2026]] [[State of Origin series]] wins and was the vice-captain of [[New South Wales rugby league team|New South Wales]] from 2020 to 2025. He has represented [[Australia national rugby league team|Australia]] at international level, winning the [[2021 Rugby League World Cup]] and the [[2025 Kangaroo tour of England|2025 Rugby League Ashes series]]. He represented [[City New South Wales rugby league team|City NSW]] in 2017. ==Background== Cleary is the son of coach and former professional rugby league footballer [[Ivan Cleary]] who coaches him at the Penrith Panthers.{{cite web|url=https://www.penrithpanthers.com.au/teams/?competition=111&team=500014|title=Panthers Team|website=penrithpanthers.com.au}} Cleary was born in [[Sydney]], New South Wales, Australia. He spent a number of his childhood years living in [[Auckland]], New Zealand while his father was playing for, and later coaching, the [[New Zealand Warriors]]. He attended [[Sacred Heart College, Auckland]] for two years and, having grown up playing [[soccer]], Cleary switched to rugby league during his pre-teens, playing at a junior level for the [[Mount Albert Lions]] in Auckland and the [[Penrith Brothers]] in Sydney.{{cite web|last=Skipwith|first=David|date=30 July 2016|title=Nathan Cleary a chip and chase off old block|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/news/article.cfm?c_id=4&objectid=11684401|work=New Zealand Herald|access-date=29 January 2018}}{{cite web|last=Chammas|first=Michael|date=27 February 2017|title=Penrith Panthers' Nathan Cleary only began playing rugby league six years ago|url=http://www.smh.com.au/rugby-league/league-news/penrith-panthers-nathan-cleary-only-began-playing-rugby-league-six-years-ago-20170227-gum8a8.html|work=The Sydney Morning Herald|access-date=29 January 2018}} He completed his [[Higher School Certificate (New South Wales)|HSC]] while attending [[St Dominic's College, Penrith]] in 2015, where he was a [[School Captain|prefect]]. Cleary is of Croatian and Ukrainian descent.{{cite web|url=http://www.nzfootball.co.nz/football-and-rugby-league-unite-for-special-training-session/|title=Football and rugby league unite for special training session – New Zealand Football|website=nzfootball.co.nz}}{{cite web|last=Heming|first=Wayne|date=13 September 2017|title=Penrith young gun Nathan Cleary's growing case for the title of best teen NRL player ever.|url=https://www.theaustralian.com.au/sport/penrith-young-gun-nathan-clearys-growing-case-for-the-title-of-best-teen-nrl-player-ever/news-story/437e6cb1c70cec9a4faf8a6fa0455a3a|work=The Australian|access-date=29 January 2018}} He is the nephew of [[Josh Stuart]] and [[Jason Death]].{{cite web|last=Ritchie|first=Dean|date=29 September 2011|title=Warriors coach Ivan Cleary grew up in Manly heartland|url=https://www.perthnow.com.au/news/nsw/warriors-coach-ivan-cleary-grew-up-in-manly-heartland-ng-57eb854d592b01113778472e8dbd7cd9|work=Perth Now|access-date=29 January 2018}} ==Playing career== [[File:nathancleary.jpg|right|thumb|Cleary playing for the [[Windsor Wolves]] in 2015]] [[File:Nathan Cleary.jpg|right|thumb|Cleary playing in the NYC in 2015]] ===Early career=== Cleary progressed through the Penrith club's junior system, playing in their [[Harold Matthews Cup]] (under 16){{cite web|last=Pengilly|first=Adam|date=29 July 2016|title=Penrith Panthers teenager Nathan Cleary mature beyond his years|url=http://www.smh.com.au/rugby-league/penrith-panthers/penrith-panthers-teenager-nathan-cleary-mature-beyond-his-years-20160728-gqgai5.html|work=The Sydney Morning Herald}} and [[S. Cleary was awarded with the Wally Lewis Medal for the Player of the Series.{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/nrl/state-of-origin/state-of-origin-2026-who-won-the-wally-lewis-medal-man-of-the-series-man-of-the-match-sam-walker-nathan-cleary-odds/news-story/54b905b11035d1d507892b688749982d/|title='Cometh the hour, cometh the champion': Cleary puts 'lazy and lame' Origin criticism to bed|website=www.foxsports.com.au}} In week 3 of the 2026 finals series during the Panthers 14-22 loss against the Newcastle Knights, Cleary suffered a compound fracture of his lower leg from a hip drop tackle from Knights player [[Phoenix Crossland]].{{Cite web |date=2026-09-27 |title=’Stadium silenced’ as Nathan Cleary suffers horrific injury |url=https://7news.com.au/sport/rugby-league/nathan-cleary-suffers-horrific-compound-fracture-as-phoenix-crossland-sent-off-for-dangerous-hip-drop-tackle-c-22933808 |access-date=2026-09-27 |website=7NEWS |language=en}} [[File:Nathan Cleary kicking at goal for Australia.jpg|right|thumb|Cleary kicking a goal for the Kangaroos in 2025]] ==Honours== '''Individual''' * '''Dally M Medal:''' 2026 * '''Clive Churchill Medal''': 2021, 2023 * '''Wally Lewis Medal:''' 2026 * '''Dally M Halfback of the Year''': 2020, 2021, 2025, 2026 * '''RLPA Players' Champion''': 2020, 2026 * '''RLPA Halfback of the Year''': 2020, 2021, 2026 * '''Brad Fittler Medal''': 2020, 2026 * '''Merv Cartwright Medal''': 2020, 2021, 2025 * '''State of Origin Man of the Match''': 4 (2020 game 2, 2022 game 2, 2026 game 1, 2026 game 3) '''Penrith Panthers''' *'''NRL Premiership''': 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 *'''NRL Minor Premiership''': 2020, 2022, 2023, 2026 *'''55th Penrith Panthers Captain''' '''New South Wales''' * '''State of Origin Series''': 2018, 2019, 2021, 2026 '''Australia''' * '''World Cup''': 2021 * '''Ashes Series''': 2025 ==Statistics== ===Club statistics=== {| class="wikitable" |- | style="background:#afe6ba;
