'''Jake Arnold Fraley''' (born May 25, 1995) is an American professional [[baseball]] [[outfielder]] who is a free agent. He has previously played in [[Major League Baseball]] (MLB) for the [[Seattle Mariners]], [[Cincinnati Reds]], [[Atlanta Braves]], and [[Tampa Bay Rays]].

==Amateur career==
Fraley attended Caravel Academy in [[Bear, Delaware]],<ref name=delaware>{{cite web|url=http://www.delawareonline.com/story/sports/college/2015/06/12/caravel-grad-jake-fraley-key-lsus-world-series-run/71133502/|title=Caravel grad Jake Fraley key to LSU's World Series run|work=The News Journal|access-date=June 9, 2016}}</ref> where he played for their baseball team. He [[batting average (baseball)|batted]] .536 as a junior and .492 as a senior, and in his senior year was named to Louisville Slugger's [[All-America]]n first team and the All-State first team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.delawareonline.com/story/sports/college/2014/04/18/seeking-best-caravel-grad-fraley-finding-place-lsu-baseball-team/7893485/|title=Caravel grad Jake Fraley finding place at LSU|work=The News Journal|access-date=June 9, 2016}}</ref>

Fraley enrolled at [[Louisiana State University]] (LSU) to play [[college baseball]] for the [[LSU Tigers baseball|LSU Tigers]]. He batted .372 as a freshman in 2014, and was named a Freshman [[All-America]]n by the [[National Collegiate Baseball Writers Association]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sportsnola.com/jared-poche-jake-fraley-named-freshmen-all-americans-by-ncbwa/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160809023927/http://sportsnola.com/jared-poche-jake-fraley-named-freshmen-all-americans-by-ncbwa/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=August 9, 2016|title=Jared Poche', Jake Fraley Named Freshmen All-Americans By NCBWA - SportsNOLA|date=June 9, 2014|publisher=SportsNOLA|access-date=June 9, 2016}}</ref> He played [[collegiate summer baseball]] for the [[Chatham Anglers]] of the [[Cape Cod Baseball League]] after his freshman and sophomore years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://baseball.pointstreak.com/player.html?playerid=576195&seasonid=26713 |title=#22 Jake Fraley |publisher=pointstreak.com |accessdate=September 23, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://baseball.pointstreak.com/player.html?playerid=743208&seasonid=29767 |title=#45 Jake Fraley |publisher=pointstreak.com |accessdate=September 23, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/younger-players-following-example-of-tigers-outfielder-jake-fraley/article_247649b5-1bc3-541d-b286-fba4241f1f04.html|title=Younger players following example of Tigers outfielder Jake Fraley|work=The Advocate|access-date=August 7, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nola.com/lsu/index.ssf/2014/10/a_year_later_lsu_left_fielder.html|title=A year later, LSU's Jake Fraley doesn't have to worry about wrestling with confidence|work=The Times-Picayune|date=October 10, 2014 |access-date=June 9, 2016}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Tampa Bay Rays===
The [[Tampa Bay Rays]] selected Fraley with the 77th overall selection of the [[2016 MLB draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.shreveporttimes.com/story/sports/college/lsu/2016/06/10/tampa-bay-rays-select-lsus-jake-fraley/85695536/ |title=Tampa Bay Rays select LSU's Jake Fraley |publisher=Shreveporttimes.com |date=June 10, 2016 |access-date=August 20, 2019}}</ref> He spent the 2016 season with the Low-A [[Hudson Valley Renegades]] where he batted .238 with one home run, 18 RBI and 33 stolen bases in 55 games. In 2017, Fraley played for the High-A [[Charlotte Stone Crabs]], posting a .170 batting average with one home run and 12 RBI in only 26 games due to injury. In 2018, he returned to the Stone Crabs, batting .347/.415/.547 with four home runs, 41 RBI, and 11 stolen bases in 66 games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.milb.com/player/index.jsp?player_id=641584#/career/R/hitting/2018/ALL|title=Jake Fraley Stats, Highlights, Bio - MiLB.com Stats - The Official Site of Minor League Baseball|publisher=MiLB.com|access-date=October 21, 2018}}</ref>

In the subsequent offseason, Fraley played in the [[2017–18 Australian Baseball League season]] for the [[Perth Heat]] batting .361/.449/.680 in 40 games, setting the runs (50) and stolen base (39) records.<ref>[https://www.baseball-reference.com/register/leader.cgi?type=bat&id=d2a24e58 2017 Australian Baseball League Batting Leaders] Baseball Reference</ref>

===Seattle Mariners===
On November 8, 2018, Fraley was traded to the [[Seattle Mariners]] along with [[Mallex Smith]] for [[Mike Zunino]], [[Guillermo Heredia (baseball)|Guillermo Heredia]], and [[Michael Plassmeyer]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/mariners/news/mariners-acquire-mallex-smith/c-300413960|title=Mariners complete Zunino-Mallex deal|last=Johns|first=Greg|work=MLB.com|date=November 8, 2018|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> He began the 2019 season with the [[Arkansas Travelers]] of the [[Class AA|Double-A]] [[Texas League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2019/apr/05/travelers-prevail-in-opener-20190405/ |title=Travelers prevail in opener |publisher=Arkansasonline.com |date=April 5, 2019 |access-date=August 20, 2019}}</ref> The Mariners promoted Fraley to the [[Tacoma Rainiers]] of the [[Class AAA|Triple-A]] [[Pacific Coast League]] on June 20.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/mariners/mariners-promote-outfield-prospect-jake-fraley-to-class-aaa-tacoma/ |title=Mariners promote outfield prospect Jake Fraley to Class AAA Tacoma |publisher=The Seattle Times |date=June 20, 2019 |access-date=August 20, 2019}}</ref>

On August 20, 2019, the Mariners selected Fraley's contract and promoted him to the major leagues.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://marinersblog.mlblogs.com/mariners-select-outfielder-jake-fraley-from-tacoma-a82546134bdf?sf107501237=1|title=Mariners Select Outfielder Jake Fraley from Tacoma|website=marinersblog.mlblogs.com|author=MarinersPR|date=August 20, 2019|access-date=August 20, 2019}}</ref> He made his major league debut on August 21 versus the [[Tampa Bay Rays]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/jake-fraley-makes-mlb-debut-for-mariners|title=Fraley makes MLB debut for Mariners in CF|website=[[MLB.com]]|author=Dawn Klemish|date=August 21, 2019|access-date=August 22, 2019}}</ref> He batted .150 in 12 games.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.baseball-reference.com/register/player.fcgi?id=fraley000jak|title=Jake Fraley College, Amateur & Minor Leagues Statistics & History|website=Baseball-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=March 23, 2020}}</ref> For the abbreviated 2020 season, Fraley appeared in seven games with the Mariners, getting four hits in 23 at-bats.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/mariners/mariners-outfielder-jake-fraley-isnt-letting-an-eye-opening-and-frustrating-2020-season-define-him/|title=Mariners outfielder Jake Fraley isn't letting an eye-opening and frustrating 2020 season define him|date=February 27, 2021 }}</ref>

On June 6, 2021, Fraley hit his first career home run, a three-run shot off [[Griffin Canning]] of the [[Los Angeles Angels]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/jake-fraley-hits-first-homer-in-mariners-win?game_pk=633832|title=Fraley's eye-opening 1st HR lifts Mariners|website=[[MLB.com]]|date=June 3, 2021|accessdate=June 4, 2021}}</ref> In a June 9 matchup against the [[Detroit Tigers]], Fraley made a leaping catch to rob rookie [[Isaac Paredes]] of a [[walk-off home run]], instead sending the game to extras when a quick relay to first base allowed for an inning-ending double play. He notched a go-ahead single in the 11th inning to carry his team to a 9–6 victory.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sodomojo.com/2021/06/10/jake-fraley-saves-mariners/|title=Jake Fraley saves the Mariners, and then delivers a win against Tigers|date=June 10, 2021 |accessdate=June 10, 2021}}</ref> Fraley finished the 2021 season batting .210 with 9 home runs, 36 RBIs and 10 stolen bases in 78 games.

===Cincinnati Reds===
On March 14, 2022, the Mariners traded Fraley, [[Justin Dunn]], [[Brandon Williamson (baseball)|Brandon Williamson]], and a [[player to be named later]] ([[Connor Phillips]]) to the [[Cincinnati Reds]] in exchange for [[Eugenio Suárez]] and [[Jesse Winker]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://marinersblog.mlblogs.com/mariners-acquire-inf-eugenio-suárez-of-jesse-winker-from-cincinnati-174b93de336b|title=Mariners Acquire INF Eugenio Suárez & OF Jesse Winker from Cincinnati|date=March 14, 2022|access-date=March 14, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Mariners Send Minor League RHP Connor Phillips To Cincinnati as PTBNL in Suárez-Winker Trade|url=https://marinersblog.mlblogs.com/mariners-send-minor-league-rhp-connor-phillips-to-cincinnati-as-ptbnl-in-suárez-winker-trade-d176011c30dc|date=March 29, 2022|accessdate=March 29, 2022}}</ref> He would make 68 appearances for the team, batting .259/.344/.468 with 12 home runs, 28 RBI, and four stolen bases.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jake Fraley 2022 batting Stats Per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/gamelog/_/id/37974/year/2022/category/batting|access-date=October 27, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

On May 1, 2023, Fraley was placed on the injured list with right knee inflammation, and was shifted to the 60-day injured list on June 13.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Reds' Jake Fraley: Lands on injured list|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/baseball/news/reds-jake-fraley-lands-on-injured-list/amp/|access-date=February 26, 2023|website=cbssports.com|language=en}}</ref> He was activated on July 29.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Reds activate Ross Detwiler, Jake Fraley from the injured list|url=https://www.redlegnation.com/2022/07/29/cincinnati-reds-activate-ross-detwiler-jake-fraley-from-the-injured-list/|access-date=May 25, 2023|website=redlegnation.com|date=July 29, 2022 |language=en}}</ref> Fraley made 111 total appearances for the Reds, slashing .256/.339/.443 with 15 home runs, 65 RBI, and 21 stolen bases.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jake Fraley 2023 batting Stats Per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/gamelog/_/id/37974/year/2023/category/batting|access-date=October 27, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

Fraley appeared in 116 contests for the Reds in 2024, hitting .277/.330/.386 with five home runs, 26 RBI, and 20 stolen bases.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jake Fraley 2024 batting Stats Per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/gamelog/_/id/37974/year/2024/category/batting|access-date=October 27, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> He made 67 appearances for Cincinnati in 2025, batting .232/.332/.387 with six home runs, 23 RBI, and four stolen bases. Fraley was [[designated for assignment]] by the Reds on August 17, 2025.<ref>{{cite news |title=Reds designate Jake Fraley for assignment, activate Tyler Stephenson |url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/46001713/reds-designate-jake-fraley-assignment-activate-tyler-stephenson |access-date=August 17, 2025 |agency=Associated Press |publisher=ESPN.com |date=August 17, 2025}}</ref>

On September 14, Fraley was placed on the injured list due to a strained right oblique muscle.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Braves Select Luke Williams, Place Jake Fraley On Injured List|url=https://www.mlbtraderumors.com/2025/09/braves-select-luke-williams-place-jake-fraley-on-injured-list.html|access-date=September 17, 2025|website=mlbtraderumors.com|language=en}}</ref> He was transferred to the 60-day injured list on September 17, officially ending his season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Braves Claim Carson Ragsdale|url=https://www.mlbtraderumors.com/2025/09/braves-claim-carson-ragsdale-waivers-orioles.html|access-date=September 17, 2025|website=mlbtraderumors.com|language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Fraley was born in [[Frederick, Maryland]] on May 25, 1995. He is a Christian.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nola.com/lsu/index.ssf/2015/06/lsus_jake_fraley_relies_on_a_s.html|title=LSU's Jake Fraley relies on an ironclad faith to keep him grounded on the diamond|work=The Times-Picayune|date=June 13, 2015 |access-date=June 9, 2016}}</ref> He has an older sister, Lauren, and two younger brothers, Andrew, and Brandon and two younger sisters, Hallie and Megan Myers. His younger brother, Brandon, is also a baseball player who attended Caravel Academy.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2015/caravels-brandon-fraley-is-the-athlete-of-the-week|title=Caravel's Brandon Fraley is the Athlete of the Week|date=April 27, 2015|work=USA Today|access-date=June 9, 2016}}</ref> Fraley married Angelica Caceres on October 21, 2016, in Miami, Florida. They have two children.{{cn|date=August 2019}} According to an [[Ancestry.com]] test, he is a descendant of [[Vikings]] and [[Anglo-Saxons]] people, which was a major reason as to why the Reds adopted a dugout celebration for the 2023 season involving a Viking outfit, also involving bullpen pitcher [[Luis Cessa]] telling him late in the 2022 season that he "looked like a Viking with the big beard and long blonde hair.".<ref>{{cite web | last=Sheldon | first=Mark | title=Jonathan India, Reds debut Viking home run celebration | website=MLB.com | date=2023-04-02 | url=https://www.mlb.com/news/jonathan-india-reds-debut-viking-home-run-celebration | access-date=2026-01-11}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last=Sutelan | first=Edward | title=Reds home run celebration, explained: Why Cincinnati players wear Viking apparel after homers | website=Sporting News | date=2023-04-11 | url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/mlb/news/cincinnati-reds-home-run-celebration-viking-apparel/njjvk28fkyapkmnydfwxuakj | access-date=2025-11-08}}</ref>

|language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-florida-shooting-father-idUSKCN0YY109 |access-date=October 5, 2022}} His mother, Shahla Mateen, was taken into custody after she allegedly attacked her husband while he was brushing his teeth on the night of December 7, 2002.{{cite web |url=http://radaronline.com/exclusives/2016/06/orlando-shooting-omar-mateen-mother-shahla-mateen-domestic-violence-arrest-mugshot/ |title=Locked Up! The Proof Of Orlando Shooter's Dark Family Past Exposed |author=Montero, Noelani |date=June 13, 2016 |publisher=Radar Online}} Both of his parents first settled in New York, having four children, including Omar.{{cite web |url=http://www.sun-sentinel.com/news/fl-omar-mateen-family-details-20160619-story.html |title=Eccentricity, violence at home may have helped shape Orlando shooter Omar Mateen |publisher=Sun Sentinel |date=June 18, 2016 |author=Clary, Mike}} After being raised in New York for a few years, he moved with his family to [[Port St. Lucie, Florida]], in 1991.{{cite web |url=https://www.tampabay.com/news/publicsafety/before-orlando-massacre-killer-omar-mateen-visited-parents-one-last-time/2281507/ |title=Before Orlando massacre, killer Omar Mateen visited parents one last time |work=Tampa Bay Times |date=June 13, 2016 |access-date=June 13, 2016 |first1=Ben |last1=Montgomery |first2=Samuel |last2=Howard |first3=Michael |last3=LaForgia}} His family was described as being [[moderate Muslim]]s and "all-American". {{cite news |last1=Sullivan |first1=Kevin |last2=Wan |first2=William |title=Troubled. Quiet. Macho. Angry. The volatile life of the Orlando shooter. |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/national/troubled-quiet-macho-angry-the-volatile-life-of-omar-mateen/2016/06/17/15229250-34a6-11e6-8758-d58e76e11b12_story.html |access-date=June 18, 2016 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=June 17, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160618014638/https://www.washingtonpost.com/national/troubled-quiet-macho-angry-the-volatile-life-of-omar-mateen/2016/06/17/15229250-34a6-11e6-8758-d58e76e11b12_story.html |archive-date=June 18, 2016 |url-status=live}} ===Behavior in school=== At a young age, Mateen displayed a preoccupation with violence, the [[Associated Press]] and ''[[The Washington Post]]'' reported. For his elementary and middle school education, he attended classes in [[St. Lucie County, Florida]]. While at Mariposa Elementary School, a [[third grade]] teacher wrote that Mateen was "very active ... constantly moving, verbally abusive, rude, aggressive ... much talk about violence & sex ... hands all over the place – on other children, in his mouth." In the [[seventh grade]], Mateen was moved to a separate class with the purpose of avoiding "conflicts with other students" and suffered from poor scholarly performance due to "many instances of behavioral problems." {{cite news |last1=Weiss |first1=Mitch |last2=Bynum |first2=Russ |title=Records: Orlando gunman talked about violence in 3rd grade |url=http://www.seattletimes.com/nation-world/apnewsbreak-woman-says-nightclub-shooter-stalked-her/ |access-date=June 17, 2016 |work=[[The Seattle Times]] |date=June 17, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160617165414/http://www.seattletimes.com/nation-world/apnewsbreak-woman-says-nightclub-shooter-stalked-her/ |archive-date=June 17, 2016 |url-status=live}} A classmate at Mariposa said that Mateen was a [[bullying|bully]], disrespectful to girls and acted like he was better than his classmates. Another classmate reported that Mateen was bullied at school because of his weight and his Afghan heritage. His parents were described as "dismissive" of his poor behavior while his father "had a reputation for being disrespectful of female teachers and dismissive of complaints about his son." In 1999, while Mateen was in the eighth grade, his teacher sent a letter to his father regarding an "attitude and inability to show self-control." Mateen began his secondary education at [[Martin County High School]] in 2000, and at the age of 14 was expelled after being in a fight in math class, where he was briefly arrested without being handcuffed and charged with [[Battery (crime)|battery]] and disrupting school, though the charges were later dropped.{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-florida-shooting-gunman-idUSKCN0YY11B |title=Gunman in worst U.S. massacre described as 'quiet' but grew hateful |work=Reuters |date=June 13, 2016 |access-date=June 13, 2016 |first=Zachary |last=Fagenson}}{{cite web |url=http://www.nbcnews.com/storyline/orlando-nightclub-massacre/orlando-shooter-omar-mateen-arrested-teen-fight-records-show-n593971 |title=Orlando Shooter Omar Mateen Arrested as Teen for Fight, Records Show |publisher=NBC News |date=June 16, 2016 |access-date=June 16, 2016 |first1=Stephanie |last1=Gosk |first2=Tom |last2=Winter |first3=Tracy |last3=Connor}} While a sophomore attending Spectrum, an alternative high school for students with behavioral issues, classmates told ''The Washington Post'' that Mateen cheered in support of [[Hijackers in the September 11 attacks|the hijackers]] during the [[September 11 attacks]] and stated that [[Osama bin Laden]] was his uncle who taught him how to shoot [[AK-47]]s. After his outburst, Mateen's father arrived at the school to pick him up and slapped him in the face, with Mateen later being suspended for five days after the incident. Soon after the September 11 attacks, "he shocked other students on his school bus by imitating an exploding plane," reported ''[[The New York Times]]''.{{cite news |title='Always Agitated. Always Mad': Omar Mateen, According to Those Who Knew Him |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/06/19/us/omar-mateen-gunman-orlando-shooting.html |access-date=June 19, 2016 |work=The New York Times |date=June 18, 2016 |quote=was Omar Mateen betraying his latent extremist sympathies — or was he just being tone-deaf — when, at 14, he shocked other students on his school bus by imitating an exploding plane so soon after the Sept. 11 attacks? 'He got on, walked up the first couple of steps, held his arms out and made sounds like a motor and then made an explosion sound — and slipped into his seat', Robert Zirkle, another student on the bus, remembered. 'He did this three or four times |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160619033803/http://www.nytimes.com/2016/06/19/us/omar-mateen-gunman-orlando-shooting.html |archive-date=June 19, 2016 |url-status=live |last1=Barry |first1=Dan |last2=Kovaleski |first2=Serge F. |last3=Blinder |first3=Alan |last4=Mashal |first4=Mujib }} A retired Martin County High School dean, Dan Alley, said the school personnel "tried to counsel him and show him the error of his ways, but it never had the effect that we were hoping for" and that his father "would not back up the school, and he would always take his son's side." Mateen was later sent to [[St. Lucie West Centennial High School]] after getting into a fight with another student.{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/post-nation/wp/2016/06/13/on-911-omar-mateens-classmates-mourned-some-say-he-celebrated/ |title=On 9/11, the Orlando shooter's classmates mourned. |first3=Rene |last3=Stutzman |url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/news/pulse-orlando-nightclub-shooting/os-orlando-nightclub-omar-mateen-profile-20160613-story.html |title=Gunman Omar Mateen visited About Orlando Nightclub Shooter Omar Mateen |work=ABC News |date=June 15, 2016 |access-date=June 15, 2016 |first=Julia |last=Jacobo}} By the time Mateen returned to and graduated from Martin County's Stuart Adult Vocational School in 2003, he had been suspended for 48 days for being involved in fights and injuring other students. ==Post-secondary education and employment== Mateen attended [[Indian River State College]]'s Criminal Justice Training program and in a questionnaire, he admitted to committing or being involved in a crime that went undetected, but did not provide specific details. He went on to earn an [[Associate of Science degree]] in [[criminal justice]] technology from the college in 2006.{{cite news |url=http://www.tcpalm.com/news/crime/st-lucie-county/who-is-omar-mateen-35140633-45ca-1fbf-e053-0100007fbd3e-382613281.html |title=Who is Omar Mateen? |last=Jones |first=Elliott |date=June 12, 2016 |publisher=Treasure Coast Newspapers |access-date=June 12, 2016 |archive-date=June 13, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160613113858/http://www.tcpalm.com/news/crime/st-lucie-county/who-is-omar-mateen-35140633-45ca-1fbf-e053-0100007fbd3e-382613281.html |url-status=dead }} He worked in a number of local stores and restaurants while attending school. In October 2006, Mateen began working as a recruit for the [[Florida Department of Corrections]], being assigned to the Martin Correctional Institution. In a letter explaining his juvenile record as part of his successful application, Mateen explained the incident of when he was arrested at school when he was fourteen. He also wrote that he had experimented with marijuana as a young teenager. Following the [[Virginia Tech shooting]] in April 2007, Mateen suggested in a corrections officer training class that he would bring a gun to class. P.H. Skipper, who was the warden at the institution, wrote that "in light of the tragic events at Virginia Tech officer Mateen's inquiry about bringing a weapon to class is at best extremely disturbing." Days later on April 27, 2007, Mateen "was involuntarily dismissed" from the program and never became a certified [[corrections officer]]. {{cite news |last1=Connor |first1=Tracy |last2=Winter |first2=Tom |title=Orlando Gunman Talked About Bringing Gun to Training Class in 2007 |url=http://www.nbcnews.com/storyline/orlando-nightclub-massacre/orlando-shooter-omar-mateen-talked-about-bringing-gun-training-class-n594786 |access-date=June 18, 2016 |publisher=[[NBC News]] |date=June 17, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160618011327/http://www.nbcnews.com/storyline/orlando-nightclub-massacre/orlando-shooter-omar-mateen-talked-about-bringing-gun-training-class-n594786 |archive-date=June 18, 2016 |url-status=live}} {{cite web |url=https://www.tampabay.com/news/publicsafety/crime/omar-mateen-what-we-know-about-orlando-nightclub-shooter/2281484/ |title=Omar Mateen: What we know, don't know about Orlando nightclub shooter |date=June 13, 2016 |work=Tampa Bay Times |access-date=June 14, 2016}} Mateen then worked for British-based security firm [[G4S Secure Solutions]] in [[Jupiter, Florida]], from September 2007 until his death.{{cite news |url=http://www.palmbeachpost.com/news/news/local/fort-pierce-apartment-building-evacuated-has-ties-/nrfFf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160612233449/http://www.palmbeachpost.com/news/news/local/fort-pierce-apartment-building-evacuated-has-ties-/nrfFf/|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 12, 2016 |title=Vero Beach bomber tied to Mateen posted anti-gay video on Facebook |date=June 12, 2016 |work=[[The Palm Beach Post]] |last2=Morgan |first2=Matt |last3=Mower |first3=Lawrence |last4=Stapleton |first4=Christine |first1=Pat |last1=Beall |access-date=December 21, 2016}} {{cite news |url=http://www.palmbeachpost.com/news/local/vero-beach-bomber-tied-mateen-posted-anti-gay-video-facebook/KZ9zXxKFAC0nKTkm3ApXhM/ |title=A G4S Secure Solutions (USA) Inc. Publication |date=Fall 2012 |publisher=[[G4S|g4s.com]] |page=10 |access-date=June 14, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161016235344/http://www.palmbeachpost.com/news/local/vero-beach-bomber-tied-mateen-posted-anti-gay-video-facebook/KZ9zXxKFAC0nKTkm3ApXhM/ |archive-date=October 16, 2016 |url-status=dead}} In 2010, Mateen, while working for G4S, was interviewed for and appears in ''[[The Big Fix (2012 film)|The Big Fix]]'', the 2012 documentary about the [[Deepwater Horizon oil spill]].{{cite web |url=http://news.sky.com/story/1712088/documentary-footage-shows-omar-mateen-in-2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616171416/http://news.sky.com/story/1712088/documentary-footage-shows-omar-mateen-in-2010|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 16, 2016 |title=Documentary Footage Shows Omar Mateen In 2010 |publisher=Sky News |date=June 15, 2016 |access-date=June 15, 2016}}{{cite news |last1=Mauney |first1=Matt |title=2012 documentary shows Omar Mateen working security during BP oil spill |url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/news/pulse-orlando-nightclub-shooting/os-omar-mateen-security-oil-spill-story.html |access-date=June 15, 2016 |work=Orlando Sentinel |date=June 15, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616050914/http://www.orlandosentinel.com/news/pulse-orlando-nightclub-shooting/os-omar-mateen-security-oil-spill-story.html |archive-date=June 16, 2016 |url-status=live}} Mateen said of those working on the cleanup: "Nobody gives a shit here. Everybody's just, get out to get paid. They're like hoping for more oil to come out and more people to complain so they'll have jobs. They want more disaster to happen."{{Cite web|url=https://www.thewrap.com/orlando-shooter-omar-mateen-in-bp-documentary-big-fix/|title=Orlando Shooter Omar Mateen Was in BP Oil Spill Documentary (Video)|first=Reid|last=Nakamura|date=June 15, 2016}} === Screening issues === G4S said two screenings of Mateen—one conducted upon hiring and the other in 2013—had raised no red flags.{{cite web |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/orlando-shooter-employer-g4s-saw-no-red-flags-1465817844 |title=Orlando Nightclub Shooting Puts G4S in Spotlight Again: U.K.-based security giant that employed Omar Mateen said its vetting had raised no red flags |last=Woo |first=Stu |date=June 13, 2016 |work=The Wall Street Journal |access-date=June 14, 2016}} Under Florida state law, for him to work as an armed guard the company was required either to make a full psychiatric evaluation of Mateen, or to administer a "validated written psychological test."{{cite web |url=http://www.securityinfowatch.com/news/12225644/orlando-shooting-sharpens-scrutiny-on-screening-of-security-guards-in-florida |title=Orlando shooting sharpens scrutiny on screening of security guards in Florida |author=David Ovalle |publisher=McClatchy/Security Info Watch |date=June 27, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160702062829/http://www.securityinfowatch.com/news/12225644/orlando-shooting-sharpens-scrutiny-on-screening-of-security-guards-in-florida |archive-date=July 2, 2016 }} The test administered was the updated [[Minnesota Multiphasic Personality Inventory]] (MMPI-2), a test used for job screenings and court cases requiring those subjected to it to agree or disagree with statements such as "My soul sometimes leaves my body" and "Once in a while I think of things too bad to talk about." Carol Nudelman, the psychologist listed on the character certification submitted by G4S to the state, said she stopped working for the company in 2005. After the shooting, Nudelman, who according to the records of the security company [[G4S]], was said to have evaluated and cleared Mateen for his firearms license in 2007, denied ever meeting him or living in Florida at the time, and said she had stopped her practice in Florida in January 2006. G4S said Mateen was not actually interviewed by a psychologist, but rather a psychologist evaluated the results of a standard test used in job screenings and his test was evaluated by the firm that bought Nudelman's practice, Headquarters for Psychological Evaluation.{{cite web |url=https://www.scmp.com/news/world/united-states-canada/article/1977077/security-firm-g4s-under-scrutiny-over-mistakes |title=Security firm G4S under scrutiny over mistakes on psychological report for Orlando shooter |publisher=South China Morning Post |date=June 18, 2016}}{{cite web |url=https://www.stratfor.com/weekly/vetting-against-odds |title=Vetting Against the Odds |publisher=STRATFOR |date=June 23, 2016 |editor=Mike Parks}} On September 10, 2016, the [[Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services]] fined G4S $151,400 for providing inaccurate psychological testing information after it found the psychologist whose opinion was necessary to permit Mateen to carry a weapon was not practicing as a screener. Between 2006 and 2016, 1,514 forms were submitted erroneously listing Nudelman's name. Mateen's form was among those investigated. [http://www.mypalmbeachpost.com/news/national/florida-slaps-151k-fine-security-company-that-hired-pulse-shooter/lsXYlPK2JJFi30JyGW6FtO/ Florida slaps $151K fine on security company that hired Pulse shooter] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170403072037/http://www.mypalmbeachpost.com/news/national/florida-slaps-151k-fine-security-company-that-hired-pulse-shooter/lsXYlPK2JJFi30JyGW6FtO/ |date=April 3, 2017 }}, ''[[Palm Beach Post]]'', September 10, 2016. Retrieved June 1, 2017. He had taken the MMPI-2 and Dr. Syed Shafeeq Rahman, a family physician who had close ties with Mateen's family, gave him a medical clearance. Rahman was also the imam of the Fort Pierce mosque to which the family belonged and said that Mateen had become progressively more "reclusive," and did not speak to other congregants before or after services.[https://www.nytimes.com/live/orlando-nightclub-shooting-live-updates/imam-w Florida Shooting: Live Updates], ''[[New York Times]]'', Alan Blinder, June 12, 2016. Retrieved October 18, 2017. G4S admitted Mateen's form had a "clerical error," and clarified that he had instead been cleared by Rahman, who was from the same firm that bought the wrongly named doctor's practice. Rahman had not interviewed Mateen, but evaluated the results of a standard test used in the screening he undertook before being hired. Nonetheless, G4S removed Mateen from his job post at a courthouse because of threats he made towards coworkers, including one threat where he claimed he would have [[al-Qaeda]] kill a deputy's family.{{cite web |url=http://www.wptv.com/news/region-st-lucie-county/port-st-lucie/pga-village-residents-present-findings-of-investigation-into-g4s-following-concern-of-omar-mateen |title=PGA Village residents present findings of investigation into G4S following concern of Omar Mateen |work=WPTV |date=October 19, 2016 |access-date=October 19, 2016 |first=Meghan |last=McRoberts}} Mateen had claimed that his coworkers and courthouse deputies were making racist comments towards him. Despite this, G4S "kept Mateen as an employee" but moved him "to a kiosk at a gated community in Palm Beach County."{{cite news |last=Ovalle |first=David |date=June 17, 2016 |title='Clerical error' on Orlando killer's psychological eval named wrong doctor |url=http://www.miamiherald.com/news/state/florida/article84490302.html |access-date=June 19, 2016 |work=The Miami Herald |quote=The company kept Mateen as an employee, moving him to a kiosk at a gated community in Palm Beach County |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160619144733/http://www.miamiherald.com/news/state/florida/article84490302.html |archive-date=June 19, 2016 |url-status=live}} They never informed the community or its property management company about why he was transferred there. Mateen held an active [[concealed carry permit]] and an [[security guard|armed security guard]] license. {{cite news |url=https://licensing.freshfromflorida.com/access/individual.aspx?TYPE=INDIVIDUAL&CATEGORY=&COUNTY=00&LICENSE=D%202723758&STATUS=IND_DETAIL |title=Mateen, Omar |publisher=[[Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services]] |access-date=June 14, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160612230614/https://licensing.freshfromflorida.com/access/individual.aspx?TYPE=INDIVIDUAL&CATEGORY=&COUNTY=00&LICENSE=D%202723758&STATUS=IND_DETAIL |archive-date=June 12, 2016 |url-status=live}} It was also noted that Mateen had no adult criminal record. According to licensing records, he was a proficient shooter who scored at or above the 98th percentile with a [[9mm]] semiautomatic pistol.{{cite web |url=https://www.tampabay.com/news/nation/state-slaps-150000-fine-on-security-firm-that-employed-orlando-shooter/2292978/ |title=State slaps $150,000 fine on security firm that employed Orlando Pulse shooter Omar Mateen |work=The Tampa Bay Times |date=September 9, 2016 |access-date=September 10, 2016 |first=Anthony |last=Cormier}} ==Personal life== In 2006, Mateen filed a petition for a name change, adding Mateen as his surname to match that of his parents. In April 2009, Mateen married his first wife, Sitora Alisherzoda Yusufiy,{{cite web |url=https://heavy.com/news/2016/06/omar-mateen-wife-married-divorce-sitora-yusufiy-isis-facebook-page/ |title=Sitora Yusufiy, Omar Mateen's Ex-Wife: 5 Fast Facts You Need to Know |publisher=Heavy |date=June 12, 2016 |author=Farrell, Paul}} an [[Uzbekistan]]-born woman whom he met in 2008 through [[Myspace]], a [[social networking]] site.{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/06/14/us/sitora-yusufiy-omar-mateen-orlando-shooting.html |work=The New York Times |access-date=June 14, 2016 |date=June 13, 2016 |title=Sitora Yusufiy, Ex-Wife of Orlando Suspect, Describes Abusive Marriage |first=Jack |last=Healy}} They separated after four months and divorced in July 2011.{{cite news |url=http://www.courierpress.com/news/382613301.xhtml|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160612233440/http://www.courierpress.com/news/382613301.xhtml|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 12, 2016 |title=Orlando shooting suspect married, divorced within 2 years |date=June 12, 2016 |publisher=Evansville Courier & Press |access-date=June 13, 2016}}{{cite news |url=http://www.cnn.com/2016/06/12/us/orlando-nightclub-shooting/index.html |title=Orlando shooting: 49 killed, shooter pledged ISIS allegiance |last1=Fantz |first1=Ashley |date=June 12, 2016 |access-date=June 14, 2016 |work=CNN|last2=Karimi |first2=Faith |last3=McLaughlin |first3=Eliott C.}} Mateen visited [[Saudi Arabia]] for an eight-day trip in March 2011 and a ten-day trip in March 2012. The latter was organized by the Islamic Center at [[New York University]]. By September 2013, they were living in a house in Port St. Lucie with Mateen's father and another relative. She reportedly left Mateen and joined relatives in [[Rodeo, California]] by December 2015. At the time of his death, Mateen had a three-year-old son with Salman.{{cite news |url=http://www.slate.com/blogs/the_slatest/2016/06/14/omar_mateen_wife_noor_salman_may_be_charged_report_says.html |title=Omar Mateen Had Remarried, and His Wife Apparently Knew About His Attack Plans |work=Slate |date=June 14, 2016 |access-date=June 14, 2016 |first=Ben |last=Mathis-Lilley}}{{cite news |url=http://www.foxnews.com/us/florida-nightclub-shooter-apparently-made-threats-in-the-past-ex-wife-claims-he-beat-her |title=Florida nightclub shooter apparently made threats in the past; ex-wife claims he beat her and took steroids |date=June 12, 2016 |publisher=[[Fox News Channel]] |access-date=June 12, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160612151526/http://www.foxnews.com/us/2016/06/12/florida-nightclub-shooter-had-made-threats-in-past-reports-claim.html |archive-date=June 12, 2016 |url-status=live}} At the time of the shooting, he lived about {{convert|100|mi|km}} from [[Orlando, Florida]], in Fort Pierce, but received mail at his parents' home in nearby Port St. Lucie. Mateen's second wife also said that Mateen became physically and verbally abusive towards her six months into their marriage, though she noted him being kinder in the weeks leading up to the shooting. A former high school student told ''The Washington Post'' that he witnessed 14-year-old Mateen, on the day of the September 11, 2001, attacks, being [[Assault|physically assaulted]] by his father, Mir Seddique Mateen, in front of other students. [[Imam]] Shafiq Rahman at the Fort Pierce Islamic Center told reporters that Mateen would come to the [[mosque]] "three or four times a week"{{cite news |last1=Nehamas |first1=Nicholas |last2=Gurney |first2=Kyra |last3=Ovalle |first3=David |last4=Brown |first4=Julie K. |title=Omar Mateen: Portrait of America's deadliest mass shooter |url=http://www.miamiherald.com/news/state/florida/article83368952.html |access-date=June 13, 2016 |date=June 12, 2016 |quote=Imam Syed Shafeeq Rahman said Mateen had been a regular attendee since childhood and came in for worship three or four times a week. |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160613020900/http://www.miamiherald.com/news/state/florida/article83368952.html |archive-date=June 13, 2016 |url-status=live}} with his father and his three-year-old son as recently as two days before the shooting, and said, "He was the most quiet guy. He would come and pray and leave. There was no indication at all of violence." Rahman added that he did not preach violence toward homosexuals.{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/post-nation-live/liveblog/live-updates-orlando-shooting/?tid=sm_tw#4613c1fa-eecf-4c09-bef2-089c3c6d4f54 |title=Orlando shooting |date=June 12, 2016 |newspaper=The Washington Post |access-date=June 12, 2016}}{{cite news |last1=Lawler |first1=David |title=Omar Mateen's imam says he was known at the mosque for being aggressive |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2016/06/13/orlando-imam-says-he-had-not-feared-omar-mateen-could-be-radical/ |work=The Daily Telegraph |date=June 13, 2016 |access-date=June 14, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160614175557/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2016/06/13/orlando-imam-says-he-had-not-feared-omar-mateen-could-be-radical/ |archive-date=June 14, 2016 |url-status=live}} A former high school friend and coworker said that Mateen had no obvious conflicts with his gay coworkers at [[Treasure Coast Square]], a shopping mall at [[Jensen Beach, Florida|Jensen Beach]].{{cite web |url=http://www.thedailybeast.com/articles/2016/06/12/drag-queen-orlando-gunman-omar-mateen-was-my-friend.html |title=Drag Queen: Orlando Gunman Omar Mateen Was My Friend |work=The Daily Beast |date=June 12, 2016 |access-date=June 12, 2016 |first1=Katie |last1=Zavadski |first2=Lynn |last2=Waddell}} A former coworker who worked with Mateen in a [[gated community]] in western Port St. Lucie described him as "unhinged and unstable." He also said that he frequently made [[Homophobia|homophobic]], [[racist]], and [[sexist]] comments, and talked about killing people.{{cite web |url=http://www.floridatoday.com/story/news/crime/2016/06/12/who-omar-mateen/85791280 |title=Co-worker: Omar Mateen homophobic, 'unhinged' |last2=Rodriguez |first2=Nicole |date=June 12, 2016 |work=USA Today |publisher=Florida Today |last3=Jones |first3=Elliot |access-date=June 12, 2016 |first1=Anthony |last1=Westbury}} The coworker stated he complained to G4S about Mateen "several times";{{cite news |url=http://www.floridatoday.com/story/news/crime/2016/06/12/who-omar-mateen/85791280/ |title=Co-worker: Omar Mateen homophobic, 'unhinged' |date=June 12, 2016 |agency=USA Today Network |quote=Gilroy, a former Fort Pierce police officer, said Mateen frequently made homophobic and racial comments. Gilroy said he complained to his employer several times but it did nothing because he was Muslim. |access-date=June 13, 2016}} another co-worker told ''The New York Times'' Mateen made people wait at the gate for a number of reasons, including "if it was time for him to do his prayers." A resident who had lived at the community since 2011 described Mateen as "very polite" and "a very nice, positive person"; however, another customer said Mateen "acted like a straight-up predator." ===Sexual orientation=== Several people who knew Mateen have speculated that he might have been [[gay]] or [[bisexual]]. A male friend of his from 2006, when the two were in [[police academy]] together, said that Mateen went to gay clubs with him and that Mateen once expressed an interest in dating him. Club-goers also recalled Mateen dancing with another man.{{cite news |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/news/national/orlando-shooter-reported-pulse-club-regular-patrons-article-1.2672445 |title=Orlando shooter was regular at Pulse gay club; former classmate says Omar Mateen was homosexual |last=Sandoval |first=Edgar |date=June 13, 2016 |work=The New York Daily News |access-date=June 13, 2016}}{{cite news |last=Mower |first=Lawrence |date=June 14, 2016 |url=http://www.palmbeachpost.com/news/news/orlando-shooter-omar-mateen-was-gay-former-classma/nrfwW/ |title=Orlando shooter Omar Mateen was gay, former classmate says |work=[[The Palm Beach Post]] |access-date=June 14, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160614095038/http://www.palmbeachpost.com/news/news/orlando-shooter-omar-mateen-was-gay-former-classma/nrfwW/ |archive-date=June 14, 2016 |url-status=dead}} One classmate, who asked not to be identified by name, said Mateen asked him if he was gay. The FBI has investigated many of these claims but has not found reasonable evidence to establish Mateen's [[sexual orientation]]. After the shooting, the ''[[Orlando Sentinel]]'' and ''[[The Palm Beach Post]]'' reported that at least five regular customers at the [[Pulse (nightclub)|Pulse]] nightclub had seen Mateen visit the venue on at least a dozen occasions. Sometimes Mateen drank in a corner by himself "and other times he would get so drunk he was loud and belligerent." A witness, who recognized Mateen outside the club an hour before the shootings, told investigators that Mateen had been messaging him for about a year using a gay [[Mobile dating|dating app]] called [[Jack'd]]. He gave his phone to the FBI for analysis, along with his login details for the application.{{cite news |title=Orlando gunman had used gay dating app and visited LGBT nightclub on other occasions, witnesses say |url=https://www.latimes.com/nation/la-na-orlando-nightclub-shooting-20160613-snap-story.html |work=Los Angeles Times |date=June 13, 2016 |access-date=June 13, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160613233653/http://www.latimes.com/nation/la-na-orlando-nightclub-shooting-20160613-snap-story.html |archive-date=June 13, 2016 |url-status=live}} A third witness said that Mateen had tried to pick up men at the nightclub.{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2016/jun/14/orlando-shooter-omar-mateen-was-a-regular-at-nightclub |title=Orlando gunman Omar Mateen 'was a regular at Pulse nightclub' |work=The Guardian |date=June 14, 2016 |access-date=June 14, 2016 |first1=Ed |last1=Pilkington |first2=Jessica |last2=Elgot}} Dozens of other witnesses, however, told the ''[[Tampa Bay Times]]'' that they had never seen Mateen at the nightclub. A spokesperson for Barbara Poma, the owner of the Pulse nightclub, called the statement that Mateen had been a regular patron "untrue and totally ridiculous."{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/florida-shooting-idUSL1N19709C |access-date=June 15, 2016 |work=Reuters |title=Federal grand jury could charge wife of Orlando shooter |date=June 15, 2016 |first1=Letitia |last1=Stein |first2=Julia |last2=Edwards}} Mateen's father Seddique denied that his son was [[closeted]], saying, "If he was gay, why would he do something like this?" Two days later, after multiple reports questioned whether Mateen was homosexual, Mateen's father said, "I didn't see any of it and I don't believe that was the case."{{cite news |title=Orlando gunman's father reacts to speculation son was gay |url=http://www.cbsnews.com/news/orlando-shooting-gunman-omar-mateen-father-reacts-to-speculation-son-was-gay |work=CBS News |date=June 14, 2016 |access-date=June 14, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160615124012/http://www.cbsnews.com/news/orlando-shooting-gunman-omar-mateen-father-reacts-to-speculation-son-was-gay/ |archive-date=June 15, 2016 |url-status=live}} However, during an interview with the Brazilian television station [[Sistema Brasileiro de Televisão|SBT Brazil]], Mateen's ex-wife claimed that his father called him gay while in her presence.{{cite news |title=Ex-wife's bombshell claim: Club shooter was gay |url=https://nypost.com/2016/06/13/shooter-used-to-visit-orlando-gay-club-use-gay-dating-apps/ |work=New York Post |date=June 13, 2016 |access-date=June 16, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616032218/http://nypost.com/2016/06/13/shooter-used-to-visit-orlando-gay-club-use-gay-dating-apps/ |archive-date=June 16, 2016 |url-status=live}} Following the shooting, Mateen's father stated, in an online video in his native language, "In this month of [[Ramadan]], the gay and lesbian issue is something that God will punish," though "the servants of God shouldn't have anything to do with it." ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' reported Mateen's ex-wife as saying that "[he] did feel strongly about homosexuality."{{cite news |last1=Mitchell |first1=Josh |last2=Bauerlein |first2=Valerie |last3=Paletta |first3=Damian |title=Before Orlando Shooter's Routine Last Days, Hints of Instability |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/before-orlando-shooters-routine-last-days-hints-of-instability-1465858489 |date=June 14, 2016 |access-date=June 14, 2016 |work=The Wall Street Journal |quote=Mr. Mateen had 'confessed' to his ex-wife that in the past 'he very much enjoyed going to clubs and nightlife,' she told CNN on Monday. He 'never made any indication while we were together that he was gay, but he did feel strongly about homosexuality,' she said. |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160614002256/http://www.wsj.com/articles/before-orlando-shooters-routine-last-days-hints-of-instability-1465858489 |archive-date=June 14, 2016 |url-status=live}} When asked if Mateen was gay, his ex-wife said she "didn't know" and recalled that he had confessed to going to nightclubs.{{cite web |url=http://www.9news.com.au/world/2016/06/14/13/16/omar-mateen-used-gay-dating-app-jackd |title=Omar Mateen used gay dating app Jack'd: witness |work=Ninemsn |date=June 14, 2016 |access-date=June 14, 2016}} ====Investigation into claims==== On June 16, ''[[The New York Times]]'' reported that the FBI was skeptical of reports that Mateen was "gay but 'closeted{{'"}} and that he had made use of homosexual bars and apps.{{cite news |title=Omar Mateen Posted to Facebook Amid Orlando Attack, Lawmaker Says |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/06/17/us/orlando-shooting.html |work=The New York Times |access-date=June 18, 2016 |date=June 16, 2016 |quote=Federal law enforcement officials said Thursday that the F.B.I. is increasingly skeptical of reports that Mr. Mateen was gay but 'closeted', that he had been visiting gay clubs or that he had used gay dating apps. |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160618111744/http://www.nytimes.com/2016/06/17/us/orlando-shooting.html |archive-date=June 18, 2016 |url-status=live}} On June 18, the same source added that "federal officials say they have found no evidence in his effects or online presence to back them up." On June 23, the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' reported that the FBI had found no evidence "to support claims by those who say Mateen had gay lovers or communicated on gay dating apps." Investigators considered at least one claimant of homosexual relationships with Mateen as not "credible." "Miguel," a man who self-identified as Mateen's lover-of-two-months, had said that he believed the massacre was committed in revenge against Latino men, following Mateen's learning that he might have been exposed to [[HIV]] from a Puerto Rican man with whom he had sex. Mateen had told his coworkers that his family was linked to [[al-Qaeda]] and that he had joined [[Hezbollah]], both rivals of the [[Islamic State]] (IS) and of one another. Mateen [[Bay'ah|pledged allegiance]] to IS during his 2016 shooting.{{Cite web |url=http://www.cnn.com/2016/06/13/us/orlando-shooter-omar-mateen/index.html |title=Omar Mateen: Angry, violent 'bigot' who pledged allegiance to ISIS |last1=Perez |first1=Evan |last2=Prokupecz |first2=Shimon |website=CNN|access-date=June 27, 2017 |quote=But both of the investigations were closed, and Mateen -- who would go on to call 911 and pledge allegiance to ISIS during his rampage -- was not under investigation or surveillance at the time of the attack. |last3=Shoichet |first3=Catherine E. |last4=Hume |first4=Tim|date=June 13, 2016 }} FBI Director James Comey commented on the contradictions within Mateen's statements. The FBI interviewed Mateen twice after opening the investigation; in these interviews, Mateen admitted to making the statements but "explained that he said them in anger because his co-workers were teasing him." After ten months, the investigation was closed and Mateen determined not to be a threat. Mateen had been placed on a [[Interpol Terrorism Watch List|terrorist watch list]] while the investigation was under way, but he was removed from it afterwards. Mateen came to the FBI's attention again in July 2014, when he was linked to [[Moner Mohammad Abu Salha]], an American who had traveled to Syria and committed a [[suicide bombing]] in late May 2014. The two had been acquainted and "attended the same mosque." He released video footage showing what appeared to be Mateen on June 8, four days before the shooting, praying for about ten minutes.{{cite web |url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/features/religion/religion-world/os-kissimmee-islamic-center-mateen-video-the-american-muslim-leadership-council-20160928-story.html |title=Imam: Omar Mateen prayed at Kissimmee mosque days before attack |work=Orlando Sentinel |date=September 28, 2016 |access-date=September 29, 2016 |first=Bethany |last=Rodgers}} Hours before the attack, Mateen stopped by his parents' home to visit his father, who said he did not notice anything strange about his son during the visit. That same day, Omar gave his second wife, Noor Salman, $1,000 and allowed her to depart to visit her mother in California. On June 14, 2016, [[NBC News]] reported that Noor Salman told the FBI she "drove him once to the gay nightclub, Pulse, because he wanted to scope it out."{{cite news |title=Omar Mateen's Wife Tried to Talk Him Out of Orlando Attack, Sources Say |url=http://www.nbcnews.com/storyline/orlando-nightclub-massacre/omar-mateen-s-wife-tried-talk-him-out-orlando-attack-n592051 |publisher=NBC News |date=June 14, 2016 |access-date=June 14, 2016 |first1=Pete |last1=Williams |first2=Tom |last2=Winter |first3=Jonathan |last3=Dienst |first4=Ken |last4=Dilanian |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160615010907/http://www.nbcnews.com/storyline/orlando-nightclub-massacre/omar-mateen-s-wife-tried-talk-him-out-orlando-attack-n592051 |archive-date=June 15, 2016 |url-status=live}} The FBI was almost immediately aware that this was not true, due to its review of cell phone location records from the day in question.{{cite web |url=https://www.clickorlando.com/news/noor-salman-trial/feds-call-final-witnesses-in-noor-salman-trial |title=Attorneys ask judge to dismiss charges against Pulse gunman's widow mid trial: Government witness proves Noor Salman did not scout nightclub before shooting |first=Emilee |last=Speck |date=March 22, 2018 |publisher=WKMG-TV}} Omar Mateen had searched for Orlando nightclub locations in the evening before the attack. An official involved with the investigation told the [[Associated Press]] that authorities believed she knew about the plot beforehand, but were reluctant to charge her based only on this suspicion.{{cite web |first=Andrea |last=Noble |url=http://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2016/jun/14/omar-mateen-a-regular-at-pulse-he-was-a-homosexual/ |title=Omar Mateen a regular at Pulse: 'He was a homosexual, and he was trying to pick up men' |work=The Washington Times |date=June 14, 2016 |access-date=June 14, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160615123859/http://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2016/jun/14/omar-mateen-a-regular-at-pulse-he-was-a-homosexual/ |archive-date=June 15, 2016 |url-status=live}} Days before the shooting, she had accompanied Mateen on a shopping trip where he purchased ammunition while she was elsewhere buying a child's toy. She warned him the evening before the event against anything that he might be planning. On March 30, 2018, an Orlando jury found her not guilty as the prosecution had not met its burden of providing evidentiary proof. According to the jury foreman, the jury felt she had vague foreknowledge of her husband's intentions. The FBI agent's interrogation went untaped, meaning the jurors did not get to see or hear it. She had been held in jail awaiting trial since her arrest in California five months after the massacre. Retrieved April 3, 2018. ===Shooting and death=== At approximately 2:02 a.m. on June 12, 2016, Mateen entered the [[Pulse (nightclub)|Pulse]] nightclub in [[Orlando, Florida]], and began shooting. At 2:22 a.m., he made a [[911 (emergency telephone number)|911]] call in which he pledged allegiance to IS, referenced [[Tamerlan Tsarnaev|Tamerlan]] and [[Dzhokhar Tsarnaev]], the [[Boston Marathon bombing|Boston Marathon bombers]], and mentioned [[Moner Mohammad Abu Salha]], an acquaintance of his who died in a suicide bombing in Syria for the [[Al-Nusra Front]] in 2014.{{cite web|last1=Bertrand|first1=Natasha|author-link=Natasha Bertrand|last2=Engel|first2=Pamela|date=June 13, 2016|title=The FBI director just painted a bizarre picture of the man behind the worst mass shooting in US history|url=http://www.businessinsider.com/james-comey-orlando-shooting-omar-mateen-fbi-2016-6|access-date=June 13, 2016|website=[[Business Insider]]}} According to [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]] officials, Mateen made two other 911 calls during the shooting.{{cite web |url=http://www.wbur.org/news/2016/06/13/mateen-orlando-tsarnaevs-monday |title=FBI Boston Chief: In Call, Mateen Referred To Tsarnaevs As His 'Homeboys' |work=WBUR News |date=June 13, 2016 |access-date=June 14, 2016}} He also called [[News 13]] of Orlando and identified himself as the nightclub shooter; ''[[The Washington Post]]'' reported that he said "he had carried out the Pulse attack for the Islamic State."{{cite news |last1=Miller |first1=Michael E. |title='I'm the shooter. {{Short description|American singer-songwriter}} {{redirect|Xylo}} {{BLP sources|date=November 2020}} {{Use mdy dates|date=January 2025}} {{Infobox musical artist | name = Paige Turner | image = XYLO @ The Echo 11 10 2022 (52526515128) (cropped).jpg | image_size = 220 | alt = | caption = Xylø performing in 2022 | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|1994|08|08}} | birth_place = United States | origin = [[Los Angeles]], [[California]], US | genre = {{flatlist| * [[Alternative pop]] * [[electropop]] * [[indie pop]] * [[dance-pop]] * [[synth-pop]] * [[Alternative rock]] }} | years_active = 2015–present | label = {{flatlist| * [[Sumerian Records|Sumerian]] * [[Sony Music|Sony]] * [[Columbia Records|Columbia]] * [[Disruptor Records|Disruptor]] }} | website = {{URL|http://www.xylo-music.com/}} | current_members = * Paige Duddy | past_members = * Chase Duddy }} '''Paige Duddy''', also known as '''Paige Turner''', is an American singer-songwriter. She began her career as a member of the musical duo '''Xylø''' (stylised in [[all caps]]) with her brother and maintained the name as a solo project after his departure. Since 2024, she has been the lead vocalist and songwriter, for the band [[Sunday (1994)|Sunday (1994)]]. As a duo, Xylø was best known for the debut single, "America", which was self-released in February 2015 and saw commercial success online through digital outlets such as [[NoiseTrade]]. The single's success resulted in Xylø securing a record deal with [[Sony Music Entertainment]].{{Cite web|title=XYLØ - America - on NoiseTrade|url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/noisetrade/music/xylomusic/america|access-date=December 21, 2021|website=pastemagazine.com|language=en|archive-date=December 21, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211221213913/https://www.pastemagazine.com/noisetrade/music/xylomusic/america|url-status=live}} Following the departure of Chase in 2018, Paige continued to release new music under the moniker. The releases included four [[Extended play|EPs]]: ''Pretty Sad'', ''Yes and No'', ''The Ganglands of My Heart'' and ''Outsiders Club''. All were released under independent label Pretty Records. The title track from ''Yes & No'' is her most successful song on [[Spotify]] to date, garnering almost 30 million streams as of December 2021.{{cn|date=March 2026}} ==Background== Paige Duddy is the granddaughter of late jazz drummer [[Joe Porcaro]], and niece of three members of [[Toto (band)|Toto]].{{Cite web |date=15 June 2022 |title=Interview with XYLØ |url=https://www.bringinitbackwards.com/interview-with-xylo/ |url-status=live |access-date=20 March 2026 |website=Bringin' it Backwards}} ==Career== ===2015-2017: ''America'' EP and singles=== [[File:XYLO live.jpg|thumb|Paige Duddy performing in 2016]] In February 2015, XYLØ released their debut single, "America", which received attention on [[YouTube]]. The self-released song was promoted through [[Hype Machine]] and [[NoiseTrade]]. The song eventually made it onto the top 10 of the Hype Machine chart and was debuted on American radio through [[KCRW]]. On June 4, XYLØ released their second song, "Between the Devil and the Deep Blue Sea". Through [[Apple Music]], the duo released their third song, "Afterlife", on July 22, 2015. In September 2015, they were featured as special guests on [[Oh Wonder]]'s live show in Los Angeles. Their fourth song, entitled "L.A. Love Song", was released on October 7, 2015. The following month, the group announced they were taking a break to focus on producing more material. Shortly afterward, they announced as signees to [[Sony Music Entertainment]]. In 2016, the duo had embarked on a number of their own live shows and released their debut EP, ''America''. On February 19, 2016, they announced their fifth single "Bang Bang", released through Apple Music. Two days before the extended play's release, they announced their sixth and final single to be released through the EP, entitled "BLK CLD", released February 26, 2016. The EP was released on February 27, 2016, through [[Sony Music Entertainment]]. During the release, the duo launched their official VEVO channel on YouTube with the music video for their debut single "America", which sparked the single's official release, to celebrate a year since its original release. On June 10, 2016, they released the ''America (The Remixes)'' EP, which includes remixes from [[Young Bombs]] and Win & Woo.{{cite web|url=https://open.spotify.com/album/4odqf3eJ5PwlIj5xhqWvut|title=America (The Remixes) EP|date=June 10, 2016|website=Open.spotify.com|access-date=June 22, 2016|archive-date=August 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160809124146/https://open.spotify.com/album/4odqf3eJ5PwlIj5xhqWvut|url-status=live}} The group was slated to headline a North American tour with 26 dates across the US and Canada, but the tour was cancelled on August 29, 2017, "due to unforeseen circumstances". The duo released a new single "Fool's Paradise" on August 5, 2016.{{Cite web|url=https://www.thedailylistening.com/listen-xylo-fools-paradise/|title=[LISTEN] XYLØ - "Fool's Paradise"|website=Thedailylistening.com|date=August 5, 2016|access-date=November 20, 2020|archive-date=September 6, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210906014401/https://www.thedailylistening.com/listen-xylo-fools-paradise/|url-status=live}} The duo was featured on "[[Setting Fires (song)|Setting Fires]]" by [[the Chainsmokers]], released as part of the ''[[Collage (EP)|Collage]]'' EP on November 4, 2016. "Gossip" was released on September 7, 2016. The instrumental of the song was used by [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] in their commercial for the [[Apple Keynote]]. They went on to release two more singles, "Dead End Love" and "Get Closer" before 2017 ended. Both of which gained accompanying music videos. In 2017, they released the single "I Still Wait For You" which become arguably their most successful single to date. They also released the singles "Alive" and "What We're Looking For" as a two-part series in music video form. ===2018–2020: Chase's departure and multiple EPs=== On June 1, 2018 "Heaven Only Knows" was released. Paige announced via [[Twitter]] that Chase had left the group to focus on other projects, leaving her as the sole member. "Don't Panic" was released on June 29, 2018, and "I Don't Want To See You Anymore" was released on August 3, 2018. Xylø went on to release "Tears & Tantrums" and "Freak" later in the year, both of which had music videos. Sometime at the end of 2018, Paige cut ties with Disruptor Records, and started releasing her music under the independent label Pretty Records. On February 12, 2019, it was announced that an EP titled ''Pretty Sad'' would be released March 1, 2019. The lead single "Nothing Left To Say" was released two days later. It was announced via social media on May 3, 2019, that Xylø's new EP, ''Yes & No'', would be released on May 31, 2019, with the lead single "Ride or Die" being released on May 17. On May 21, 2019, a second single "The End" was announced to be released on May 24, 2019. In June 2019, Xylø announced she would be embarking on the ''Yes & No Tour'', which concluded in September 2019. She released her fourth EP, ''The Ganglands of My Heart'' on February 14, 2020, which was preceded by the singles "Tongue in the Bag" and "American Sadness". On March 27, 2020, a compilation album including all the instrumentals from her three previous releases was released. Later that year, Xylø released her fifth EP, ''Outsiders Club'', for which she launched an official website for. The EP was released on November 20, 2020, with "Apple Pie", "Chlorine", and "Lefty" being released as singles prior to the EP's release.{{Cite web|last=TotalNtertainment|date=July 27, 2020|title=XYLØ releases new single 'Chlorine'|url=https://www.totalntertainment.com/music/xylo-releases-new-single-chlorine/|access-date=December 21, 2021|website=TotalNtertainment|language=en-GB|archive-date=December 21, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211221215424/https://www.totalntertainment.com/music/xylo-releases-new-single-chlorine/|url-status=live}} Music videos were also released for the latter two singles. ===2021–present: ''Unamerican Beauty'' and American tour=== During 2021, Xylø teased via social media that her debut album was in the works. On December 13, Xylø posted on various social medias a photo of her and the phone number "(310)-564-7089".{{Cite web|title=(310)-564-7089|url=https://twitter.com/xylo/status/1470439412215468036|url-status=live|access-date=December 22, 2021|website=Twitter|language=en|archive-date=December 13, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211213170529/https://twitter.com/xylo/status/1470439412215468036}} By calling the number, Xylø reads the listener a monologue. Two days later, Xylø uploaded an official trailer for the album, revealing the album's title to be ''Unamerican Beauty'' and that it would be released in 2022. Xylø then also announced via Twitter that the album's first single would be released in January. The album was finally released in June 9. In order to promote the album, Xylo embarked on the 10 date Unamerican Beauty Tour through North America in October. In January 2024, she was featured in [[Lovelyz]]'s [[Ryu Su-jeong]]'s second extended play ''[[2Rox]]'', "Fallen Angel" which was released on January 10, 2024, and "SHXT" which was released on January 24, 2024. ==Discography== ===Studio albums=== {| class="wikitable plainrowheaders" style="text-align:center" |+ List of studio albums, with selected details ! '''Justina Valentine''' (born February 14, 1987<ref>{{cite book |author1=Robert J. Dornan |title=February 14: Unlocking the Secrets of Your Birthdate |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ELxgEQAAQBAJ&pg=PT107&dq=justina+valentine+1987&hl=en&newbks=1&newbks_redir=0&source=gb_mobile_search&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwjm6b70oa6VAxWtlIkEHQgAN7MQ6AF6BAgQEAM#v=onepage&q=justina%20valentine%201987&f=false |access-date=June 30, 2026}}</ref>) is an American television host, rapper and singer from [[Passaic County, New Jersey]], best known for her singles "Candy Land"<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://thesource.com/2015/07/03/listen-as-new-jerseys-own-justina-valentine-and-fetty-wap-link-up-on-candy-land/|title=Listen As New Jersey's Own Justina Valentine And Fetty Wop Link Up On 'Candy Land'|last=Rathon|first=Rocko|date=July 3, 2015|website=The Source|access-date=July 17, 2016}}</ref> featuring rapper [[Fetty Wap]], "All The Way" and "Unbelievable".<ref name="allmusic">{{Cite web |last=Jeffries |first=David |title=Justina Valentine – Biography & History |url=http://www.allmusic.com/artist/justina-valentine-mn0003423792/biography |access-date=July 17, 2016 |publisher=AllMusic}}</ref><ref name=revolt>{{Cite web|url=https://revolt.tv/stories/2016/05/16/spotlight-revolt-justina-valentine-ft-futuristic-0a7f1d7046|title=Spotlight on REVOLT: Justina Valentine "All The Way" Feat. Futuristic|date=May 16, 2016|publisher=REVOLT TV|access-date=July 17, 2016|archive-date=August 18, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818132751/https://revolt.tv/stories/2016/05/16/spotlight-revolt-justina-valentine-ft-futuristic-0a7f1d7046|url-status=dead}}</ref> She is also known as a cast member on the improv comedy show ''[[Wild 'n Out]]'' (2016–present).

== Early life ==
Justina Valentine was born on February 14, 1987, in [[Passaic County, New Jersey]]. She is of [[Italians|Italian]] descent.<ref>{{Citation |title=Justina Valentine talks Growing up Italian in Jersey, New Movie & More |url=https://soundcloud.com/growingupitalian/justina-valentine |language=en |access-date=2022-03-22}}</ref> She grew up in a family of musicians and worked in theatre and studied dancing as a child. Valentine always had a love for [[Hip-hop|hip hop]] and [[Contemporary R&B|R&B]]. In 2006, she started recording her own music.<ref name="stupiddope">{{cite web |last=James |first=Jesse |date=April 23, 2012 |title=Interview with Justina |url=http://www.stupiddope.com/2012/04/23/interview-w-justina |archive-url=https://archive.today/20161011050247/http://stupiddope.com/2012/04/23/interview-w-justina/ |archive-date=October 11, 2016 |website=StupidDope |publisher=}}</ref><ref name="socialifestylemag">{{cite web |last=Rahim |first=Olivia |date=May 24, 2014 |title=Justina |url=http://socialifestylemag.com/justina/ |access-date=September 12, 2016 |website=Social Magazine |publisher=}}</ref>

== Career ==
Valentine released her first [[mixtape]] ''Route 80'' in 2012,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Adams |first=Rain |date=2024-01-29 |title=Justina Valentine Net Worth 2024: How Much Is The "Wild 'N' Out" Rapper Worth? |url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/756578-justina-valentine-net-worth |access-date=2025-05-20 |website=HotNewHipHop |language=en}}</ref> which included the singles "Bubble Gum" and "Hip-hop Joan Jett". She released the [[Extended play|EP]] ''Valentine'' in 2013, debuting at number 38 on the iTunes R&B charts.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://issuu.com/wearejersey/docs/march2015|title=We Are Jersey: March 2015|access-date=September 8, 2016}} pages 29–38</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Blanco |first=Evie |date=2017-11-16 |title=Justina Valentine Drops New Mixtape – Feminem [Stream] |url=https://respect-mag.com/2017/11/justina-valentine-drops-new-mixtape-feminem-stream/ |access-date=2025-05-20 |website=RESPECT. {{!}} The Photo Journal of Hip-Hop Culture |language=en-US}}</ref> On July 8, 2014, the singer released her second mixtape, ''Red Velvet''. In 2016, she released her studio album, ''Scarlet Letter''. 

In 2017, Valentine released a third mixtape, ''Feminem,'' described as a homage to the rapper [[Eminem]].<ref>{{Citation |title=Feminem by Justina Valentine |date=2017-11-08 |url=https://music.apple.com/us/album/feminem/1495404224 |language=en-US |access-date=2022-03-22}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Feminem by Justina Valentine |url=https://genius.com/albums/Justina-valentine/Feminem |access-date=2022-03-22 |website=Genius |language=en}}</ref> She released the album ''Favorite Vibe'' in 2019, which debuted in the top 30 hip hop charts and gained over a million streams in its first two weeks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jones |first=Jiggy |date=2020-12-03 |title=The Source {{!}}Wild 'N Out's Justina Valentine Drops Latest Project, 'INFRARED' |url=https://thesource.com/2020/12/03/wild-n-outs-justina-valentine-drop-latest-project-infrared/ |access-date=2022-03-22 |website=The Source |language=en-US}}</ref> ''Favorite Vibe'' was shortly followed by the album ''Infrared'' in 2020, which debuted in the top 5 on the iTunes charts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Justina Valentine – Indie Amplify |url=https://www.indieamplify.com/services/justina-valentine-vocal-feature/ |access-date=2022-03-22 |language=en-US}}</ref> ''Infrared'' is described as "an infusion of classic hip hop and R&B, with a pop sensibility."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Justina Valentine – "Infrared" (Album) – DJIceberg.com |date=December 11, 2020 |url=https://djiceberg.com/justina-valentine-infrared-album/ |access-date=2022-03-22 |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2016, Valentine was added to the cast of season 8 of ''[[Wild 'n Out]]'' on [[MTV]] (later [[VH1]]) and has been a member of the cast for every successive season since.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://comedyhype.com/mtv-to-bring-back-wild-n-for-season-8-on-august-4th-with-iggy-azalea-erykah-badu-omarion-and-more-watch-preview/|title=MTV To Bring Back Wild N' Out For Season 8 On August 4th With Iggy Azalea, Erykah Badu, Omarion And More; Watch Preview – ComedyHype.Com {{!}} Comedy ReFueled|date=June 9, 2016|access-date=September 8, 2016|archive-date=November 6, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181106054938/https://comedyhype.com/mtv-to-bring-back-wild-n-for-season-8-on-august-4th-with-iggy-azalea-erykah-badu-omarion-and-more-watch-preview/|url-status=dead}}</ref> As of season 17, she is the longest running female cast member to appear on the show.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-02-28 |title=Justina Valentine Talks Wild N' Out Season 17 |url=https://www.koin.com/everydaynorthwest/wild-n-out/ |access-date=2022-03-22 |website=KOIN.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

Valentine competed on season 1 of the reality series special for [[MTV]]'s ''[[The Challenge (TV series)|The Challenge]]'' titled ''[[The Challenge: Champs vs. Stars season 2|Champs vs. Stars]]'', which premiered on November 21, 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://people.com/tv/the-challenge-champs-vs-stars-cast-reveal/ |title=Cast Revealed! Josh Murray, Shawn Johnson and More Stars to Compete in MTV's The Challenge: Champs vs. Stars |last=Russian |first=Ale |date=October 11, 2017 |website=[[People (magazine)|People]]  |access-date=October 11, 2017}}</ref> Valentine made it to the finale, finishing as a runner-up alongside fellow "Stars" [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]] fighter [[Michelle Waterson]] and ''[[The Bachelorette (American season 10)|The Bachelorette Season 10]]'' winner Josh Murray. In 2019, Valentine hosted the two-part reunion of ''[[The Challenge: War of the Worlds 2]]''.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Longeretta |first1=Emily |title=Wes Bergmann Talks Returning to MTV's 'The Challenge,' Playing Cupid and Johnny Bananas: 'He's This Season's Layup' |url=https://www.usmagazine.com/entertainment/news/the-challenges-wes-says-johnny-bananas-is-this-seasons-layup/ |website=US Weekly |date=February 6, 2019 |access-date=5 February 2021}}</ref>

In November 2018, Valentine was selected to co-host a relaunched version of the MTV dating game show ''[[Singled Out]]'' alongside rapper and fellow ''Wild 'n Out'' cast member [[Conceited (rapper)|Conceited]] that aired exclusively on the network's YouTube channel.

In August 2019, Valentine and fellow ''Wild 'n Out'' cast member Chico Bean stated that [[Sebastian Maniscalco]] was Valentine's "second freaking cousin".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild 'N Out Awards Road To VMAs Hosted by Justina Valentine & Chico Bean |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=URbrC_0yKM4 |access-date=2019-08-18 |website=YouTube | date=August 18, 2019 |language=en}}</ref>

In 2021, Valentine began appearing weekly alongside [[Nick Cannon]] on his syndicated daytime talk show, ''Nick Cannon'', during "The Rap Up" and other segments.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Justina Valentine Weekly Rap Up |url=https://www.nickcannonshow.com/video/justina-valentine-weekly-rap-up/ |access-date=2022-03-22 |website=Nick Cannon |language=en}}</ref>

In February 2022, she became the third host of the [[iHeartRadio]] and MTV podcast series ''MTV's Women of Wild 'n Out,'' alongside co-hosts [[B. Simone]] and Pretty Vee.

Valentine has also gained prominence as a social media personality on [[TikTok]] where she actively posts content. As of September 2022, her account has amassed over 10 million followers and over 200 million likes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TikTok |url=https://www.tiktok.com/@justinavalentine |access-date=2022-09-09 |website=www.tiktok.com}}</ref>
