He later said in a 2024 podcast interview that the performance, delivered while his voice was breaking, was one of the most difficult experiences of his career, despite the strong placement.{{cite news |title=Dani Fernández: de su discreto paso por Eurovisión Junior a ser uno de los cantantes punteros del país |url=https://www.elespanol.com/corazon/bluper/20241116/dani-fernandez-discreto-paso-eurovision-junior-cantantes-punteros-pais/901160078_0.html |work=El Español |date=16 November 2024 |access-date=8 July 2026}} === 2009–2016: Auryn === In January 2009, Fernández became a founding member of the boy band [[Auryn]], together with Álvaro Gango, [[Blas Cantó]], Carlos Marco and David Lafuente. The band rose to prominence following its participation in ''[[Spain in the Eurovision Song Contest 2011#Destino Eurovisión|Destino Eurovisión]]'', the 2011 national selection process for the [[Eurovision Song Contest 2011]], in which it finished second.{{Cite web |last=RTVE.es |date=2011-02-18 |title=Minuto a minuto de la final de Destino Eurovisión |url=https://www.rtve.es/play/noticias/20110218/minuto-a-minuto-final-destino-eurovision/409337.shtml |access-date=2026-07-08 |website=RTVE.es |language=es}} Auryn went on to release four studio albums — ''Endless Road, 7058'' (2011), ''Anti-Heroes'' (2013), ''Circus Avenue'' (2014) and ''Ghost Town'' (2015) — the first three of which reached number one on the [[Productores de Música de España|Spanish Albums Chart]], before the band announced its breakup in 2016. === 2016–present: Solo career === Following Auryn's separation, Fernández began working on a solo project, releasing an acoustic cover of Andrés Suárez's "No saben de ti" on YouTube in December 2016 as an introduction to the musical style of his solo work.{{Cite web |last=Serena |first=Nuria |date=2016-12-15 |title=Un ex Auryn, Dani Fernández, versiona "No saben de tí" de Andrés Suárez |url=https://www.cadenadial.com/2016/un-ex-auryn-dani-fernandez-versiona-no-saben-de-ti-de-andres-suarez-90344.html |access-date=2026-07-08 |website=Cadena Dial |language=es}} His debut solo single, "Te esperaré toda la vida", was released on 18 May 2018 and later received a platinum certification; a follow-up EP, ''En llamas'', was released that November.{{Cite web |last=digital |first=Redacción |date=2018-11-26 |title=Dani Fernández, lanza su EP "En llamas" |url=https://www.cadena100.es/al-dia/noticias/dani-fernandez-lanza-llamas-20181126_323450 |access-date=2026-07-08 |website=CADENA 100 |language=es}} He released his debut solo studio album, ''Incendios'', on 24 May 2019 through [[Warner Music Spain]], produced by Tato Latorre; the album's singles "Bailemos" and "Disparos" were also certified platinum and gold respectively and reached the top ten of Spanish radio airplay charts.{{Cite web |title=Dani Fernández {{!}} EPDM |url=https://elportaldemusica.es/artist/dani-fernandez?language=en-US |access-date=2026-07-08 |website=elportaldemusica.es}} An acoustic reissue of the album, titled ''Incendios y Cenizas'', followed in 2020.{{cite web |title=El pop-rock de Dani Fernández se adueña este domingo del escenario de la Plaza del Castillo |url=https://www.pamplona.es/actualidad/noticias/el-pop-rock-de-dani-fernandez-se-aduena-este-domingo-del-escenario-de-la-plaza |work=Ayuntamiento de Pamplona |date=8 July 2023 |access-date=8 July 2026}} Fernández released his second solo studio album, ''Entre las dudas y el azar'', in 2022, featuring collaborations with Juancho de Sidecars and Nil Moliner.{{cite news |title=Dani Fernández, el manchego que conquistó el pop español: de ídolo juvenil a artista imprescindible |url=https://www.elplural.com/revista-bando/dani-fernandez-manchego-conquisto-pop-espanol-idolo-juvenil-artista-imprescindible_351788102 |work=El Plural |date=12 May 2025 |access-date=8 July 2026}} The album was recognized at the 2022 [[Premios Ondas]], where Fernández won the award for Musical Phenomenon of the Year, and at the 2022 [[LOS40 Music Awards]], where he was named Best Artist. He went on to sell out concerts at Madrid's [[WiZink Center]] and Barcelona's [[Palau Sant Jordi]]. In 2023, he received the Música category prize at the Premios Ídolo.{{cite news |title=Dani Fernández: "Si alguien que aprecio me dice que se quiere dedicar a la música le diría que lo deje directamente" |url=https://www.elespanol.com/corazon/famosos/20241011/dani-fernandez-alguien-aprecio-dice-quiere-dedicar-musica-diria-deje-directamente/892410915_0.html |work=El Español |date=11 October 2024 |access-date=8 July 2026}} His third solo studio album, ''La Jauría'', was released in 2024; in support of the release, Fernández was again nominated at the LOS40 Music Awards. In March 2025, the city council of his hometown, Alcázar de San Juan, announced it would name him a "Hijo Predilecto" (favourite son) of the city in recognition of his musical career.{{cite web |title=Quién es Dani Fernández, cantante e invitado de 'El Hormiguero' |url=https://www.esdiario.com/chismografo/tendencias/250311/154706/dani-fernandez.html |work=EsDiario |date=11 March 2025 |access-date=8 July 2026}} ==Personal life== Fernández married Spanish singer-songwriter Yarea Guillén in 2022; the couple's first daughter was born the following year. ==Discography== {{see also|Auryn#Discography}} ===Studio albums=== {| class="wikitable plainrowheaders" style="text-align:center;" |- ! '''Juliette Berthet''' (née '''Labous'''; born 4 November 1998) is a French [[bicycle racing|racing cyclist]], who rides for [[UCI Women's Team|UCI Women's WorldTeam]] {{UCI team code|FSF}}.<ref>{{Cite web |title=FDJ - Suez 2025 |url=https://www.procyclingstats.com/team/fdj-suez-2025 |access-date=1 February 2025 |website=ProCyclingStats}}</ref> Berthet won the [[French National Time Trial Championships|French National Time Trial Championship]] in 2020, and the [[French National Road Race Championships|French National Road Race Championship]] in 2024.

==Personal life==
In October 2025, she married fellow professional cyclist [[Clément Berthet]],<ref>{{cite news|first=Stéphane|last=Cléau|url=https://www.estrepublicain.fr/societe/2025/10/25/les-champions-cyclistes-juliette-labous-et-clement-berthet-se-sont-dit-oui-pour-la-vie|title=Les champions cyclistes Juliette Labous et Clément Berthet se sont dit oui pour la vie|language=French|trans-title=Cycling champions Juliette Labous and Clément Berthet said "I do" for life|work=[[L'Est Républicain]]|publisher=Groupe EBRA|date=25 October 2025|accessdate=25 March 2026}}</ref> and began competing under her married name from the start of the 2026 season.

'''Liniker de Barros Ferreira Campos''' ([[Araraquara]], July 3, 1995), widely known as '''Liniker''', is a Brazilian singer-songwriter and former bandleader for Brazilian [[Soul music|soul]] and [[Black music]] band [[:pt:Liniker e os Caramelows|Liniker e os Caramelows]]. Her voice has been described as 'powerful and low-pitched' with a 'slightly raspy, soul-singer' character<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://brasil.elpais.com/brasil/2015/11/12/cultura/1447331706_038108.html|title=Liniker: "Sou negro, pobre e gay e tenho potência também"|first=Camila|last=Moraes|date=November 13, 2015|website=[[El País]]|access-date=September 6, 2026|trans-title=Liniker: "I'm Black, poor, and gay, and I'm also powerful"|language=pt-BR}}</ref> as well as 'versatile' with a 'recurrent falsetto' and 'easily recognisable timbre', with occasional comparisons arising towards [[Tim Maia]].<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=http://enciclopedia.itaucultural.org.br/pessoa640291/liniker|title=Liniker|author=Instituto Itaú Cultural|website=[[Enciclopédia Itaú Cultural]]|isbn=978-85-7979-060-7|access-date=September 6, 2026}}</ref> Liniker is an openly [[trans woman]], and her music is an influence on young Brazilians facing [[Sexism|gender discrimination]], an audience which 'rarely finds itself represented in [[Music of Brazil|Brazilian music]]'.<ref name="auto1"/>

==Biography==
===Early life and adolescence===
Liniker was born in the city of [[Araraquara]] in rural [[São Paulo (state)|São Paulo state]]. Her mother Ângela raised her as a [[Single parent|single mother]].<ref name="Diaz-Hurtado2017">{{Cite web|url=https://www.npr.org/sections/altlatino/2017/01/31/512470018/alt-latino-extra-liniker-barros-a-woman-who-resists-by-existing|title=Alt.Latino Extra: Liniker Barros, A Woman Who Resists By Existing|website=[[NPR.org]]|date=January 31, 2017 |language=en|access-date=October 22, 2019|last1=Diaz-Hurtado |first1=Jessica }}</ref> Liniker reports how she always wanted to wear her mother's clothes: 'I was OK with myself, the city was the problem...when I came back to Araraquara, I thought I'd show them who I really was [by wearing a dress with lipstick and earrings on]. This is when my uncle confronted me, he wanted to know what was going on and gave me one of his clothes to wear so I would learn "how to dress like a man", to which I thanked but said I wasn't taking it. And then my mother said, "Let Liniker be, he's an artist."'<ref name="auto"/>

Having grown up in a musical family, Liniker was exposed to [[samba rock]], as well as [[jazz]], [[Soul music|soul]], and [[R&B]]. She started writing songs at age 16. At 18, she left Araraquara to pursue her passion for the arts, especially [[tap dance]] and [[drama]].<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.cartacapital.com.br/diversidade/liniker-201csou-dona-do-meu-corpo-e-das-coisas-que-escolho-para-mim201d/|title=Liniker: "Sou dona do meu corpo e das coisas que escolho para mim"|first=Infra|last=Carta|date=July 29, 2018|access-date=September 6, 2026|website=[[CartaCapital]]|trans-title=Liniker: "I own my body and the things I choose for myself"|language=pt-BR}}</ref> In 2014, she relocated to [[Santo André]] to pursue [[drama school]], where she was encouraged by rapper [[:pt:Linn da Quebrada|Linn da Quebrada]] to come out as trans and start wearing her signature skirts-lipstick-turban look on a regular basis.<ref name="auto1"/>

=== Musical career and activism ===
In 2015, Liniker formed the band [[:pt:Liniker e os Caramelows|Liniker e os Caramelows]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.papermag.com/liniker-brazil-2581560257.html|title=Liniker Is Changing the Way Trans People Are Seen in Brazil|date=June 26, 2018|website=[[Paper (magazine)|Paper]]|language=en|access-date=October 23, 2019|last=Camargo|first=Pedro}}</ref> (formerly Os Caramelows, a play on words with 'caramel' and 'mellow') with friends. Songs are entirely written by Liniker.<ref name="auto1"/> Their first concert took place when the band was one day old.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite magazine|url=https://rollingstone.uol.com.br/noticia/liniker-e-os-caramelows-anunciam-separacao-a-entrevista-rolling-stone/|title=Liniker e os Caramelows anunciam separação: Entrevista Rolling Stone|first=Pedro|last=Antunes|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|date=February 17, 2020|trans-title=Liniker e os Caramelows announce separation: Rolling Stone interview|language=pt-BR}}</ref>

The video for the single ''Zero'' from EP ''Cru'' (''Raw'') went viral on [[YouTube]], receiving 1.5 million views in the space of a week.<ref name="Rothman2018">{{Cite web|url=https://nowtoronto.com/api/content/5d8e1b84-8528-11e8-b464-12408cbff2b0/|title=Liniker is claiming space for queer Brazilian musicians|last=Rothman|first=Jonathan|date=July 11, 2018|website=[[Now (newspaper)|NOW Magazine]]|language=en-US|access-date=October 23, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190922215705/https://nowtoronto.com/api/content/5d8e1b84-8528-11e8-b464-12408cbff2b0/|archive-date=September 22, 2019}}</ref> In 2016, the band released ''Remonta'' (''Reassembling''). They began touring around Brazil as well as internationally,<ref name="Rothman2018" /> having performed in Europe, Latin America, Africa and the US. Audiences were able to enjoy the music even though failing to understand their [[Portuguese language|Portuguese]] lyrics.<ref name="auto1"/>

In 2019, the album ''Goela Abaixo'' (''Down My Throat'') was nominated for the [[Latin Grammy Award for Best Portuguese Language Rock or Alternative Album]] in [[20th Annual Latin Grammy Awards|2019]].<ref name="billboardLG19">{{cite magazine |last1=Cabo |first1=Leila |title=Latin Grammys 2019 Winners: Complete List |url=https://www.billboard.com/music/latin/latin-grammys-2019-winners-list-8543699/ |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |publisher=[[MRC (company)|MRC]] |access-date=9 September 2020 |date=14 November 2019}}</ref>

The band describe their music as new Brazilian Black music or "funzy" (a 'nearly indescribable fusion'),<ref name="Johnson2017">{{Cite web|url=https://remezcla.com/features/music/liniker-e-os-caramelows-interview/|title=Liniker e os Caramelows are at the Forefront of Brazil's Black Music Movement|date=August 4, 2017|website=[[Remezcla]]|language=en-US|access-date=October 23, 2019|last=Maria Johnson|first=Catalina}}</ref> highlighting [[Black music]]'s deep influence throughout Latin America. In ''Goela Abaixo'', elements of Caribbean and African music, as well as verses in English and Spanish are noticeable. In it, Liniker affirms her body as 'political' and exhibits global ambitions as a representative of the [[African diaspora]].<ref name="auto1"/>

In 2020, after 5 years active, the band have announced their separation with a [[farewell tour]] scheduled for the second semester of 2020. This however has not taken place yet due to the consequences of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. In the meantime, Liniker goes on with her solo career.<ref name="auto3"/>

Liniker uses her position as a well-known artist to promote social change and represent Black trans culture in a hostile social environment. She feels she has a responsibility to speak up about the violence against [[queer]] people in Brazil.<ref name="Johnson2017" /> However, she also expressed discontent that sometimes, especially during her [[Gender transitioning|transition]], too much time in interviews was spent discussing her gender, and comparatively little discussing her music.<ref name="auto3"/>

In November 2022, Liniker became the first trans woman to win a Latin Grammy.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 18, 2022 |title=Liniker se torna primeira artista transgênero brasileira a vencer um Grammy Latino: 'Histórico' |url=https://g1.globo.com/pop-arte/musica/noticia/2022/11/18/liniker-se-torna-primeira-artista-transgenero-brasileira-a-vencer-um-grammy-latino-historico.ghtml |access-date=January 8, 2024 |website=[[G1 (website)|G1]] |language=pt-BR|trans-title=Liniker becomes the first Brazilian transgender artist to win a Latin Grammy: 'Historic'}}</ref> She won the category Melhor Álbum de Música Popular Brasileira ([[Latin Grammy Award for Best MPB Album|Best MPB Album]]) for her first solo album [[:pt:Indigo Borboleta Anil|Indigo Borboleta Anil]], which mixes lyrics in English and Portuguese languages and incorporates elements of [[Música popular brasileira|MPB]], R&B, Soul, Jazz, Reggae, beyond Samba. In her speech, she got emotional and highlighted that something historical happened in her country that day.{{Citation needed|date=June 2026}}

===Partnership with Johnny Hooker and ''Flutua''===

In 2017, Liniker partnered up with Brazilian singer [[Johnny Hooker]] on single ''Flutua'' (''It Floats''). The single cover features both singers [[French kiss|French kissing]]. The song is a cry from the heart against [[homophobia]] in Brazil.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://blogs.opovo.com.br/foradaordem/2017/12/24/amar-sem-temer-johnny-hooker-e-liniker-lancam-clipe-de-flutua-em-apelo-contra-homofobia/|title=Amar sem temer: Johnny Hooker e Liniker lançam clipe de "Flutua" em apelo contra homofobia|date=December 24, 2017|website=Fora da Ordem|access-date=September 7, 2026|last=Rodrigues|first=Rubens|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210126034438/https://blogs.opovo.com.br/foradaordem/2017/12/24/amar-sem-temer-johnny-hooker-e-liniker-lancam-clipe-de-flutua-em-apelo-contra-homofobia/|archive-date=January 26, 2021|trans-title=Love without fear: Johnny Hooker and Liniker release the music video for "Flutua" in an appeal against homophobia|language=pt-BR}}</ref> As the lyrics go: 'No one will have the power / to want to tell us how to love.'{{Citation needed|date=June 2026}}

===Views on queer rights===

When asked if she had a message for conservative people who are against [[birth control]], [[abortion]] and [[Gay men|gay]] people, Liniker replied: 'It's my body. I am free to do what I want with it. If I have this entireness, how come you want to stick your nose in it? Who do you think you are to lay down the rules I am supposed to follow? To each their own, to each body its history.'<ref name="auto"/>

==Musical influences==

Liniker lists as her main musical influences [[:pt:Clube do Balanço|Clube do Balanço]], [[Cartola]], [[Elza Soares]], [[Etta James]], [[Nina Simone]], [[Caetano Veloso]], [[Gilberto Gil]], [[Gal Costa]], [[Tulipa Ruiz]], [[:pt:Tássia Reis|Tássia Reis]] as well as members of her own family.<ref name="auto"/><ref name="auto2"/>

Liniker was one of the featured performers in a televised musical tribute to [[Milton Nascimento]] on the Brazilian TV series [[Altas Horas]] in 2023.<ref>{{cite web | title=Famosos se emocionam com homenagens a Milton Nascimento em edição especial do Altas Horas | date=January 7, 2023 | url=https://gshow.globo.com/tv/altas-horas/noticia/famosos-se-emocionam-com-homenagens-a-milton-nascimento-em-edicao-especial-do-altas-horas.ghtml |access-date=September 7, 2026|website=gshow|trans-title=Celebrities get emotional during tributes to Milton Nascimento in a special edition of Altas Horas|language=pt-BR}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Altas Horas | Liniker canta 'Encontros e Despedidas' | url=https://globoplay.globo.com/v/11262453/ |access-date=September 6, 2026|website=[[Globoplay]]|trans-title=Altas Horas | Liniker sings 'Encontros e Despedidas'|language=pt-BR}}</ref>

''' Sara Waisglass''' (born July 3, 1998)<ref name="stars">{{cite web|title=Sara Waisglass |url=https://www.northernstars.ca/actor/sara-waisglass/|work=northernstars.ca| date=March 15, 2023}}{{Dead link|date=July 2026}}</ref><ref name="show">{{cite web|first=Sanjay|last=Kunwar|title=Sara Waisglass Parents And Sister Have Been Her Strength To Build Her Career|url=https://showbizcorner.com/sara-waisglass-parents|publisher=showbizcorner.com|date=March 10, 2023|access-date=March 15, 2023|archive-date=March 15, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230315102336/https://showbizcorner.com/sara-waisglass-parents|url-status=dead}}</ref> is a Canadian actress. 

Waisglass initially rose to notability as a child actress, playing the role of Jordy Cooper in the children's sitcom ''[[Overruled!]]'' from 2010 to 2011. As a teenager, she appeared as [[List of Degrassi: The Next Generation characters|Frankie Hollingsworth]] in ''[[Degrassi: The Next Generation]]'' and ''[[Degrassi: Next Class]]'' from 2013 to 2017. She also played Robyn in the 2017 drama film ''[[Mary Goes Round]]''. As an adult, she starred as Maxine Baker in the [[Netflix]] drama series ''[[Ginny & Georgia]]'' since 2021.

== Early life ==
Sara was born and raised in Toronto, Ontario<ref name="show"/> to parents Tessa and Jeff Waisglass, along with her sister Carly.<ref name="show"/> She attended [[Earl Haig Secondary School]] in Toronto.<ref name="show"/> She attended [[York University]] for four years,<ref name="tvo">{{cite web|first=Camille|last=Moore| title=10 Things You Didn't Know about Sara Waisglass |url= https://tvovermind.com/sara-waisglass/|publisher=tvovermind.com|date=2021}}</ref> graduating with a degree in screenwriting,<ref name="nuvo">{{cite web|first=Leah|last=Scott| title= Sara Waisglass on Acting in Canada, Progressive Characters, and Netflix's Ginny & Georgia |url=https://nuvomagazine.com/culture/sara-waisglass|publisher=nuvomagazine.com| date=May 21, 2021}}</ref> citing an interest in developing her writing skills.<ref name="nuvo"/><ref name="schon">{{cite web|first=Tessa|last=Swantek| title=Schön! interview - sara waisglass |url=https://schonmagazine.com/interview-sara-waisglass/|publisher=schonmagazine.com| date=February 28, 2023}}</ref> She likes to play the piano.<ref name="schon"/> She is [[Jewish]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-01-18 |title=Next class of Degrassi also features Jewish actors - The Canadian Jewish News |url=https://thecjn.ca/arts/next-class-of-degrassi-also-features-jewish-actors/ |access-date=2024-09-06 |website=thecjn.ca |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Career ==
In 2007, Waisglass made her television debut playing eight-year-old Jane in ''[[The Jane Show]]''.<ref name="Jane">{{cite web|title=The Jane Show (TV series 2004-2007) |url=https://www.rarefilmfinder.com/movie.php?id=19509&dl=off|publisher=rarefilmfinder.com | date=2007}}</ref> In 2008, Waisglass was cast in her first film role in the [[Gilles Bourdos]]-directed [[psychological thriller]] ''[[Afterwards (2008 film)|Afterwards]]'', alongside [[John Malkovich]] and [[Evangeline Lilly]].<ref name="holly">{{cite news|last=Besserglik|first=Bernard|date=January 14, 2009|title=Film Review: Afterwards|publisher=hollywoodreporter.com|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-reviews/film-review-afterwards-92748/}}</ref><ref name="after">{{cite web|date=|title=Afterwards (2008)|url=https://www.studiocanal.com/title/afterwards-2008/|publisher=studiocanal.com}}</ref><ref name="decider"/> In 2009, she continued her career on television, appearing in 29 episodes of ''[[Overruled!]]''.<ref name="stars"/><ref name="show"/> She also appeared in a commercial for [[KFC]].<ref name="tvo"/> Beginning in 2013, she played Frankie Hollingsworth in the television series ''[[Degrassi: The Next Generation]]''.

In 2015, Waisglass was cast in the [[Anton Corbijn]]-directed [[biographical drama]] film ''[[Life (2015 film)|Life]]'',<ref name="life">{{Cite web |url=https://www.thecoast.ca/halifax/life/Film?oid=5022749 |title=Life |website=thecoast.ca |access-date=May 14, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210514185853/https://www.thecoast.ca/halifax/life/Film?oid=5022749 |archive-date=14 May 2021 |url-status=dead}}</ref> alongside [[Robert Pattinson]] and [[Sir Ben Kingsley]].<ref name="affinity">{{Cite web|title=Life (2015)|url=https://www.filmaffinity.com/uk/film372907.html|website=filmaffinity.com}}</ref> The same year, Waisglass was nominated for "Best Recurring Young Actress 16-21" at the Young Entertainer Awards for her role as Frankie Hollingsworth in ''Degrassi: The Next Generation''.<ref name="nom"/>

In 2017, Waisglass played Mary's half-sister Robyn in the [[Molly McGlynn]] directed film ''[[Mary Goes Round]]'',<ref name="gate">{{Cite web|last=Powell|first=W. Andrew|date=2018-03-30|title=John Ralston & Sara Waisglass talk Mary Goes Round|url=https://www.thegate.ca/film/033017/john-ralston-sara-waisglass-mary-goes-round/|website=thegate.ca}}</ref> which featured at the [[2017 Toronto International Film Festival]].<ref name="close">{{Cite web|last=Prestridge|first=James|title=Close-up: An Interview with Sara Waisglass|url=https://closeupculture.com/2018/04/25/close-up-an-interview-with-sara-waisglass/|website=closeupculture.com|date=April 25, 2018}}</ref> In 2020, she starred as Madison St. Claire in eight episodes of the supernatural drama series ''[[October Faction (TV series)|October Faction]]''.<ref name="tvo"/>

In 2021, Waisglass starred as Maxine in the [[Netflix]] comedy series ''[[Ginny and Georgia]]'',<ref name="nuvo"/><ref name="pop">{{cite news|last=Sullivan|first=Corinne|date=February 24, 2021|title=Newly Obsessed With Ginny & Georgia's Sara Waisglass (aka Maxine)? Join the Club! |publisher=popsugar.co.uk|url=https://www.popsugar.co.uk/celebrity/who-is-sara-waisglass-facts-48183384}}</ref> in a cast that included [[Brianne Howey]], [[Antonia Gentry]], [[Chelsea Clark (actress)|Chelsea Clark]] and [[Katie Douglas (actress)|Katie Douglas]].<ref name="decider">{{Cite news|last=O'Keefe|first=Meghan|title='Ginny & Georgia' Stars Felix Mallard and Sara Waisglass Were Honored to Portray an ASL Family|url=https://decider.com/2021/03/01/ginny-georgia-felix-mallard-sara-waisglass-interview/|website=Decider|date=2021-03-01}}</ref> After the Season 2 release, Ginny & Georgia was the most-watched title from January to June 2023 on Netflix, with a combined 967.2M hours viewed between Seasons 1 and 2.<ref>{{Cite web |title='Ginny & Georgia' Dominated Netflix In First Half Of 2023 | url=https://deadline.com/2023/12/netflix-viewership-ginny-georgia-female-young-adult-interest-1235680015/ |website=Deadline | date=December 21, 2023 |language=en}}</ref> In May 2023, the series was renewed for a third and fourth season. The third season is slated to be released on June 5, 2025. It is one of the most anticipated new and returning TV shows of 2025.
<ref>{{Cite web |title='35 Of The Most Anticipated New & Returning TV Shows Of 2025 | url=https://deadline.com/lists/2025-tv-shows/ginny-georgia-season-3-netflix-june-5-2025/|website=Deadline |language=en}}</ref>

{{Short description|Japanese actor and singer (born 1997)}} {{Use dmy dates|date=March 2026}} {{Infobox person | image = Daigo_Nishihata_Naniwa_Danshi.jpg | caption = Nishihata in 2023 | name = Daigo Nishihata | native_name = 西畑 大吾 | native_name_lang = ja | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1997|1|9}} | birth_place = [[Osaka Prefecture]], Japan | occupation = {{hlist|Idol|actor|television personality}} | years_active = 2011–present | agent = [[Starto Entertainment]] | known_for = Member of [[Naniwa Danshi]] | module = {{Infobox musical artist|embed=yes | genre = [[J-pop]] | label = {{flatlist| * [[Storm Labels]]}} | current_member_of = {{flatlist| * [[Naniwa Danshi]]}} }} | website = [https://www.storm-labels.co.jp/s/js/artist/J0011/profile Naniwa Danshi (Storm Labels)]
[https://starto.jp/s/p/artist/56?lang=en&ima=1648 Naniwa Danshi (Starto Entertainment)] }} '''Daigo Nishihata''' (西畑 大吾, born January 9, 1997) is a Japanese idol and actor. He is a member of the Japanese boy band [[Naniwa Danshi]]. Nishihata joined [[Johnny & Associates]] in 2011 and later became a member of the Kansai Johnny's Jr. unit Naniwa Ōji.{{cite web |title=なにわ男子CDデビュー決定 過去のJr.内ユニット“なにわ皇子”が再び話題 |url=https://mdpr.jp/news/detail/2693440 |website=modelpress |access-date=2026-03-13 |language=ja |date=2021-07-28}} In 2018 he was selected as a member of Naniwa Danshi, which made its CD debut in 2021 with the single "[[Ubu Love]]".{{cite web |title=なにわ男子のデビューシングルは「初心LOVE」 |url=https://natalie.mu/music/news/445578 |website=Natalie |access-date=2026-03-11}} ==Early life and career== Nishihata was born on January 9, 1997, in [[Osaka Prefecture]], Japan.{{cite web |title=なにわ男子メンバー分析第1回：西畑大吾 |url=https://realsound.jp/2021/10/post-877685.html |website=Real Sound |access-date=2026-03-11}} Nishihata auditioned at [[Osaka-jō Hall]] during [[Tomohisa Yamashita]]'s Asia tour "TOMOHISA YAMASHITA ASIA TOUR 2011 SUPER GOOD SUPER BAD" and joined Johnny & Associates on April 3, 2011.{{cite web |title=西畑大吾プロフィール |url=https://mdpr.jp/model/detail/2197 |website=Modelpress |access-date=2026-03-13 |language=ja}} He later performed as a member of the Kansai Johnny's Jr. unit Aぇ少年. On the same day, [[Ren Nagase]] and [[Yoshinori Masakado]] also joined the agency. The three later became known as close contemporaries. In 2012 he became a member of the [[Kansai region|Kansai]] Johnny's Jr. unit Naniwa Ōji together with [[Ryūsei Ōnishi]] and [[Ren Nagase]].{{cite web |title=永瀬廉・西畑大吾・正門良規、“同期卍会”の絆 |url=https://realsound.jp/2024/02/post-1565506.html |website=Real Sound |access-date=2026-03-11}} Nishihata made his television drama debut in the [[NHK]] [[asadora]] ''[[Gochisōsan]]'' (2013–2014). He later appeared in another NHK asadora, ''[[Asa ga Kita]]'' (2015–2016).{{cite web |title=西畑大吾プロフィール |url=https://www.oricon.co.jp/prof/681276/ |website=Oricon |access-date=2026-03-11}} In 2018 he was selected as a member of the Kansai-based idol group [[Naniwa Danshi]]. The group officially debuted on November 12, 2021, with the single ''"Ubu Love"''.{{cite web |title=なにわ男子のデビューシングル「初心LOVE」初日50万枚 |url=https://www.oricon.co.jp/news/2213690/full/ |website=Oricon |access-date=2026-03-11}} ==Acting career== Nishihata has cited actor and singer [[Kazunari Ninomiya]] as one of his major influences. He became interested in Ninomiya after watching the television dramas ''[[Yamada Tarō Monogatari]]'' and ''[[Ryūsei no Kizuna]]''.{{cite web |url=https://thetv.jp/news/detail/1057878/ |title=西畑大吾、憧れの二宮和也への思いを語る |website=The Television |language=ja |access-date=2026-03-13}}{{cite web |url=https://realsound.jp/2021/08/post-844129.html |title=西畑大吾が語る二宮和也への憧れ |website=Real Sound |language=ja |access-date=2026-03-13}} He later appeared with Ninomiya in the film ''Last Recipe'' (2017) and co-starred with him in a commercial for the Nisshin Oillio Group "Fresh Oil Series".{{cite web |url=https://www.oricon.co.jp/news/2090543/full/ |title=二宮和也＆西畑大吾がCM初共演 |website=Oricon |language=ja |access-date=2026-03-13}} In addition to his music activities, Nishihata has appeared in numerous television dramas and films. '''Daniel Forcén Esteban''' is a Spanish [[chess]] grandmaster.

==Chess career==
He achieved the Grandmaster title in 2016, after earning his norms at the:<ref name="FIDE"/>
*IV Open International St Casablanca in December 2010
*Winterchess Mallorca Masters Marzo in March 2013
*XXXV Open International Villa de Benasque in July 2015

In May 2018, he finished in second place in the Villa de Estadilla International Chess Open, half a point behind winner Sergio Garza.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://rondasomontano.com/campeon-aragon-sergio-garza-vence-xxxii-open-internacional-villa-estadilla/|title=El Campeón de Aragón Sergio Garza vence en XXXII Open Internacional Villa de Estadilla|date=May 22, 2018}}</ref>

In July 2025, he finished with 7.5/10 in the Open Internacional "Villa de Benasque", during which he held a draw against the higher-rated [[Daniele Vocaturo]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://s2.chess-results.com/tnr1113047.aspx?lan=1&art=4&turdet=YES&flag=30&SNode=S0|title=XLIV Open Internacional "Villa de Benasque"}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chessbase.in/news/Loic-Travadon-wins-44th-Villa-de-Benasque-Open-2025-Pranav-Anand-third|title=Loic Travadon wins 44th Villa de Benasque Open 2025, Pranav Anand third|date=August 10, 2025|first=Shahid|last=Ahmed}}</ref>

'''Anna Punsoda i Ricart''' (born in 1985) is a [[Catalans|Catalan]] [[journalist]], [[novelist]], [[essayist]], [[Translation|translator]] and [[politician]].

She is the author of several books and is the translator of seven German-language works published in Catalan.

In 2024, she was a founding member of the new pro-independence political party [[Alhora]], and was presented as a candidate for the party at the [[2024 Catalan regional election|elections of the same year]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last=Pere |first=Millan |date=2024-03-13 |title=La precipitació electoral, un entrebanc per a les candidatures de l'ANC i Alhora. Vilaweb (in Catalan). |url=https://www.vilaweb.cat/noticies/alhora-nova-direccio-onze-membres-graupera-punsoda-ojeda/ |journal=Vilaweb |language=ca |access-date=2025-11-26}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=2024-04-10 |title=Tots els noms de la llista de Ponsatí i Graupera per al 12-M |url=https://elmon.cat/politica/eleccions/tots-noms-alhora-llista-ponsati-graupera-12-m-829453/ |access-date=2025-11-26 |website=El Món - Notícies i actualitat d'última hora en Català |language=ca}}</ref>

== Early life and literary career ==
Punsoda was born in [[Els Plans de Sió]], on the plain of [[Segarra]] in central Catalonia, before moving to Lleida where she grew up.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Aquesta dura, seca, oblidada terra |url=https://www.nuvol.com/llibres/aquesta-dura-seca-oblidada-terra-350207 |access-date=2025-11-26 |website=Núvol |language=ca}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite web|title=Anna Punsoda Ricart - LA MIRA - Periodisme a foc lent|url=https://www.lamira.cat/autor/anna-punsoda-ricart|website=LA MIRA|access-date=2025-12-01|language=Catalan}}</ref> She received a degree in Journalism from [[University Ramon Llull|Ramon Llull University]] and Philosophy from the [[University of Barcelona]] (UB).<ref name=":6">{{Cite web|title=Anna Punsoda|url=https://bibliotecavirtual.diba.cat/ca/club-del-llibre/anna-punsoda|website=Biblioteca Virtual. Xarxa de Biblioteques Municipals|access-date=2025-12-01|language=ca}}</ref> As part of a Master's degree in Contemporary Thought and Classical Tradition at UB, she produced a thesis on the social and political thought of [[Joan Maragall i Gorina|Joan Maragall]], eventually resulting in a published anthology of Maragall's texts.<ref name=":6" /><ref name=":0">{{cite web|access-date=2023-08-01 |language=Catalan |publisher=La Mira |title=Anna Punsoda Ricart |url=https://www.lamira.cat/autor/anna-punsoda-ricart}}<!-- auto-translated from Catalan by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> She later moved to Germany, living in the cities of Dresden, Leibzig and Hamburg, where she worked as a translator.<ref name=":5" />

Her journalistic work has focused on cultural topics, and she has contributed to a range of media outlets including newspapers ''[[El País]]'',<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2023-08-01 |date=2015-05-16 |language=es |publisher=El País |title=Artículos escritos por Anna Punsoda |url=https://elpais.com/autor/anna-punsoda/}}<!-- auto-translated from Catalan by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> ''[[Ara (newspaper)|Ara]]'',<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2023-08-01 |publisher=Ara Balears |title=Anna Punsoda |url=https://www.arabalears.cat/firmes/anna-punsoda/}}<!-- auto-translated from Catalan by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> ''[[Nació Digital]]'',<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2023-08-01 |language=ca |publisher=NacióDigital |title=Articles d'opinió de Anna Punsoda |url=https://www.naciodigital.cat/opinio/autor/1795/anna-punsoda}}<!-- auto-translated from Catalan by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> ''El Núvol,''<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2023-08-01 |language=ca |publisher=El Núvol |title=Anna Punsoda |url=https://www.nuvol.com/firmes/anna-punsoda}}<!-- auto-translated from Catalan by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> ''La Mira''<ref name=":0" /> and ''El Temps'',<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2023-08-01 |date=2023-10-05 |language=ca |publisher=El Temps |title=Anna Punsoda - Articles |url=https://www.eltemps.cat/autor/anna-punsoda?gclid=Cj0KCQjw2qKmBhCfARIsAFy8buL3UvjIGShAMqVBijGPvvLhQlTgDncQdAkfWLDrurP6QIqA7MXt2qQaApShEALw_wcB}}<!-- auto-translated from Catalan by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> as well as appearing on radio stations [[Catalunya Ràdio]] and [[RAC1]].<ref name=":7" /> In 2017 she was involved in the creation of ''La Llança'', the cultural supplement of ''[[El Nacional (Catalonia)|El Nacional]]'', and she has been the editor of ''Diagonal'' magazine since 2020.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |title=Anna Punsoda|url=https://www.fumdestampa.com/writers/anna-punsoda|access-date=2025-11-26|website=Fum d'Estampa Press|language=en-GB}}</ref>

Her 2018 debut novel, ''Els llits dels altres'', won the [[Premi Roc Boronat|Roc Boronat prize]] for that year.<ref name=":1">{{cite journal|title=Anna Punsoda, premi Roc Boronat amb 'Els llits dels altres'|url=https://www.nuvol.com/noticies/anna-punsoda-guanya-el-premi-roc-boronat/|work=Núvol}}<!-- auto-translated from Catalan by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Plantada |first=Esteve |date=2018-03-22 |title=Anna Punsoda guanya el Premi Roc Boronat amb un relat «que deixa parlar la memòria» |url=https://naciodigital.cat/opinio/anna-punsoda-guanya-el-premi-roc-boronat-amb-un-relat-que-deixa-parlar-la-memoria.html |journal=Nació Digital |access-date=2025-11-26}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|access-date=2018-10-24 |archive-date=2018-10-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181024073800/http://llengua.gencat.cat/ca/detalls/noticia/La-periodista-Anna-Punsoda-guanya-el-XX-premi-Roc-Boronat-amb-lobra-Els-llits-dels-altres |title=La periodista Anna Punsoda guanya el XX premi Roc Boronat amb l'obra 'Els llits dels altres' |url=http://llengua.gencat.cat/ca/detalls/noticia/La-periodista-Anna-Punsoda-guanya-el-XX-premi-Roc-Boronat-amb-lobra-Els-llits-dels-altres}}<!-- auto-translated from Catalan by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> The novel was translated into English by Mara Faye Lethem and published in 2022.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web|title=Other People's Beds|url=https://www.hatchards.co.uk/book/other-peoples-beds/anna-punsoda/9781913744076|website=Hatchard's|access-date=2025-12-01|language=en}}</ref> ''La luxúria'' (2020) was an extended essay on lust, while ''La terra dura'' (2023) explored her relationship to the rural Catalan environment of her youth.<ref name=":4" />

== Political career ==
In 2024, Punsoda became a founding member of [[Big tent|big-tent]], [[Catalan independence movement|pro-independence]] Catalan political party [[Alhora]], and was placed second-in-command on the 14-member national council charged with directing the party's activities.<ref name=":2" />

Punsoda was put forward as the 3rd placed candidate on the party's list for the [[2024 Catalan regional election|2024 Catalan elections]], after [[Clara Ponsatí]] and [[Jordi Graupera]], although she was not elected as the party failed to gain a single seat.<ref name=":3" />

'''Robin Rivaton''' (born July 17, 1987) is a [[French people|French]] [[entrepreneur]], investor, and essayist. He is known for his work on real estate, housing policy, [[Artificial intelligence|AI]], and the impact of new technologies on urban development.

== Biography ==
=== Early life ===
Rivaton grew up in [[Firminy]], a former steelmaking town in the suburbs of [[Saint-Étienne]], and has described his background as working-class. He completed his secondary education at the Albert Camus public high school in Firminy. He then pursued higher education at [[Sciences Po]], where he earned a master's degree in economic law in 2011, followed by a degree in management from [[ESCP Business School|ESCP Europe]] in 2012.

=== Career ===
In 2012, Rivaton joined the [[Boston Consulting Group]] (BCG) as an associate. In April 2016, he joined the office of [[Valérie Pécresse]] at the Île-de-France Regional Council as an advisor in charge of economic attractiveness and development.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cohen-Hadad |first=Bernard |date=2016-02-15 |title=Valérie Pécresse enrôle Robin Rivaton |url=https://www.lopinion.fr/politique/valerie-pecresse-enrole-robin-rivaton |access-date=2026-01-21 |website=l'Opinion |language=fr}}</ref> In September 2016, he was appointed to the executive management of Paris Region Enterprises (PRE), the agency responsible for promoting the Île-de-France region, later renamed Choose Paris Region.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Paquier |first=Jacques |date=2016-09-02 |title=Robin Rivaton officiellement nommé à la tête de PRE |url=https://www.lejournaldugrandparis.fr/robin-rivaton-officiellement-nomme-a-tete-de-pre/ |access-date=2026-01-21 |website=Le journal du Grand Paris |language=fr}}</ref> He left the organization in 2018, following initiatives aimed at attracting companies relocating from London after [[Brexit]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-12-04 |title=HSBC is moving jobs from London to Paris |url=https://www.scmp.com/business/banking-finance/article/2122643/hsbc-moving-jobs-london-paris-asian-banks-stay-put-even |access-date=2026-01-21 |website=South China Morning Post |language=en}}</ref>

After working as a [[venture capital]]ist, he became a partner and president of Stonal <ref>{{Cite web |title=Stonal – La plateforme SaaS qui transforme la gestion immobilière |url=https://stonal.com/ |access-date=2026-02-04 |website=stonal.com |language=fr}}</ref> in 2022. Stonal raised {{currency|20 million|EUR|passthrough=yes}} in 2022 and {{currency|100 million|EUR|passthrough=yes}} in 2024 to expand its AI-powered real estate SaaS platform.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-09 |title=Stonal raises $22M, appoints Robin Rivaton as CEO |url=https://www.cretech.com/news/stonal-a-top-real-estate-saas-platform-raises-22m-appoints-robin-rivaton-as-ceo-for-european-expansion/ |access-date=2026-01-21 |website=CREtech |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-06 |title=Stonal secures near €100M investment from Aareon |url=https://tech.eu/2024/05/06/stonal-secures-near-eur100-million-investment-from-aareon-for-real-estate-data-management/ |access-date=2026-01-21 |website=Tech.eu |language=en}}</ref> He is also a co-founder of Vibiscus, a deep tech company specializing in acoustics.{{Citation needed|date=February 2026}}

=== Real estate and urban policy ===
In March 2019, [[Julien Denormandie]], then Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs, tasked Rivaton with examining the digital transformation of the construction and real estate sectors.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Batiactu |date=2019-03-04 |title=Une nouvelle mission pour accompagner la transformation numérique du logement |url=https://www.batiactu.com/edito/nouvelle-mission-accompagner-transformation-numerique-55672.php |access-date=2026-01-21 |website=Batiactu |language=fr}}</ref> He was later appointed to the board of directors of Sogeprom, a subsidiary of [[Société Générale]], and joined the supervisory board of CDC Habitat in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bellemare |first=Carole |date=2019-04-17 |title=Les nominations du jour |url=https://www.lefigaro.fr/decideurs/carnet/decideurs-les-nominations-du-jour-20190417 |access-date=2026-01-21 |website=Le Figaro |language=fr}}</ref> Rivaton has published eight essays on economy and real estate. He appears regularly as a commentator on [[BFM Business]] and has contributed to major newspapers including ''[[Le Monde]]'' and ''[[Le Figaro]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-12-04 |title=Les chroniques de Robin Rivaton |url=https://www.lexpress.fr/economie/les-chroniques-de-robin-rivaton_2139999.html |access-date=2026-01-21 |website=L'Express |language=fr}}</ref>

'''Takuro Yamada''' (山田 拓朗, Yamada Takuro; born 12 April 1991) is a Japanese former Paralympic swimmer who competed mainly in freestyle and individual medley events. He represented Japan at five consecutive Paralympic Games from 2004 to 2020 and won a bronze medal in the men's 50 metre freestyle S9 at the [[2016 Summer Paralympics]].<ref name="parasapo">{{cite web |url=https://www.parasapo.tokyo/featured-athletes/yamada-takuro |title=Takuro Yamada |publisher=Nippon Foundation Paralympic Support Center |date=21 May 2019 |access-date=11 August 2019 |language=ja}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Takuro Yamada - Swimming |url=https://www.paralympic.org/takuro-yamada |website=International Paralympic Committee |access-date=26 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=[INTERVIEW 02] Takuro YAMADA {{!}} ISSUE 02 |url=https://www.parasapo.tokyo/gojournal/en/issue02/interview02/ |access-date=2026-02-26 |website=GO Journal |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life and education==

Yamada was born in Sanda, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan, and later resided in Tokyo. He graduated from Hokusetu Sanda High School and the University of Tsukuba.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.city.sanda.lg.jp/bunka_sports/rio2016para.html |title=Rio 2016 Paralympics (Athletes connected to Sanda City) |publisher=Sanda City |date=12 October 2016 |access-date=11 August 2019 |language=ja}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=Hirano Sugako |url=http://www.komei.or.jp/km/hirano-sugako/2016/12/05/障害者フェスティバル２０１６に出席/ |title=Attendance at Disability Festival 2016 |publisher=Sanda City Assembly |date=5 December 2016 |access-date=11 August 2019 |language=ja}}</ref>

He was born with a congenital absence of his left forearm and began swimming at the age of three.<ref name="docomo">{{cite web |url=https://www.nttdocomo.co.jp/special_contents/beyond2020/tokyo2020/athlete03/ |title=Introducing Young Athletes: Takuro Yamada |publisher=NTT Docomo Style'20 |access-date=11 August 2019 |language=ja}}</ref>

==Career==

Yamada made his Paralympic debut at the [[2004 Summer Paralympics]] at the age of 13.<ref name="docomo" />

At the [[2016 Summer Paralympics]] in Rio de Janeiro, he competed in the 100 metre freestyle and 50 metre freestyle events.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://paraswim.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/6f87af379e069765875a1f70a5d886bf.pdf |title=Rio de Janeiro Paralympics Japanese Team Recommendation Athletes |publisher=Japan Para-Swimming Federation |date=6 March 2016 |format=PDF |access-date=24 June 2016 |language=ja |archive-date=16 April 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160416023747/http://paraswim.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/6f87af379e069765875a1f70a5d886bf.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> He won the bronze medal in the men's 50 metre freestyle S9.

He also won a bronze medal in the 100 metre freestyle S9 at the [[2006 IPC Swimming World Championships]] in Durban.<ref>{{cite web |title=2006 IPC Swimming World Championships Durban/RSA Results |url=https://oepc.at/downloads/Ergebnislisten_Weltmeisterschaften/WM-Schwimmen_2006_Durban_RSA.pdf |access-date=26 February 2026}}</ref>

Yamada continued competing through the [[2020 Summer Paralympics]] in Tokyo. Persistent shoulder and lower back pain led him to announce his retirement in 2023. His final race took place on 18 September 2023 at the Japan Para Swimming Championships held at Yokohama International Pool.<ref>{{cite news |title=Takuro Yamada retires after changing the environment of para swimming |newspaper=Tokyo Shimbun |date=2 October 2023 |author=Yūki Kanemura |url=https://www.tokyo-np.co.jp/article/280987 |access-date=9 February 2024 |language=ja}}</ref>

'''Mikel Huerga Leache''' is a Spanish [[chess]] grandmaster. He is the first grandmaster from [[Navarre]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://adsj-dke.com/mikel-huerga-unico-navarro-gran-maestro-de-ajedrez/|title=Mikel Huerga, único navarro Gran Maestro de Ajedrez|date=March 2, 2022}}</ref>

==Chess career==
He began playing chess at the age of 6, and won the U18 Spanish Junior Championship in 2007. He is coached by [[Jesús de la Villa]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.noticiasdenavarra.com/mas-deportes/2009/12/18/primer-gran-maestro-navarro-3533916.html|title=El primer Gran Maestro navarro|date=December 18, 2009|first=Tomas|last=de la Ossa}}</ref>

He achieved the Grandmaster title in 2022 after surpassing the rating requirement in late 2021, after earning his norms at the:<ref name="FIDE"/>
*XXXIV Open Intl Ciudad de Sevilla in January 2009
*III Open Intl Ajedrez San Juan in August 2009
*Torneo Magistral Intl Elgoibar in December 2009
*LXXX CE Individual Absoluto in August 2015
*VII Cto. Iberoamericano Individual in August 2019

In August 2024, he tied for second place at the Ciudad de Oviedo Open with seven other players, prevailing over the field on tiebreak scores.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chessbase.in/news/Himal-Gusain-convincingly-clinches-10th-Ciudad-de-Oviedo-Open-2024|title=Himal Gusain clear first at Ciudad de Oviedo Open for the second consecutive year|first=Shahid|last=Ahmed|date=September 3, 2024}}</ref>

'''Katharina Stark''' (born 26 September 1998) is a German actress. In 2024 she was awarded the [[European Shooting Star Award]].

== Biography ==
Stark was born on 26 September 1998<ref>{{cite web |title=Katharina Stark |url=https://www.csfd.cz/en-gb/creator/253814-katharina-stark |website=csfd.cz |access-date=22 May 2026}}</ref> in [[Illertissen]]. She has said that she has always wanted to be an actress. When she was eight years old, she began taking acting classes in [[Munich]], roughly 90 minutes from Illertissen. Show got her first acting role at 15, in a film called ''King Laurin''.<ref name="Roxborough-2024">{{cite news |last1=Roxborough |first1=Scott |title=Berlin Shooting Star Katharina Stark Always Knew She Wanted to Be an Actress |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/berlin-rising-star-katharina-stark-german-actress-1235824492/ |access-date=21 May 2026 |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=15 February 2024}}</ref> Stark struggled to balance acting with school during this time, sometimes needing to the film shoot on the same day as completing her ''[[Abitur]]'' exams.<ref name="Kaulfersch-2016">{{cite news |last1=Kaulfersch |first1=Verena |title=Die Fellheimerin Katharina Stark spielt im Film König Laurin: Am Samstag Premierenvorstellung in Memmingen |url=https://www.all-in.de/allgaeu/die-fellheimerin-katharina-stark-spielt-im-film-koenig-laurin-am-samstag-premierenvorstellung-in-me-104303421 |access-date=21 May 2026 |work=all-in.de |date=27 August 2016 |language=German |trans-title=The Fellheimer Katharina Stark plays in the film King Laurin: On Saturday premiere performance in Memmingen}}</ref>

Following positive reception of the film, Stark took a number of one-off jobs in episodes of popular German television programs. After high school, Stark studied at the [[Otto Falckenberg School of the Performing Arts]]. While studying, she got her first lead role in a series, playing Eva Bruhns in ''[[The Interpreter of Silence]]'', a historical drama about the [[Auschwitz trial]].<ref name="Roxborough-2024" /> Stark later starred in ''Nuremberg 45'', which follows Seweryna Szmaglewska, an [[Auchwitz]] survivor and witness at the [[Nuremberg trials]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Riedner |first1=Fabian |title=‚Erinnerung ist keine Pflicht, sondern Verantwortung‘ – Katharina Stark über «Nürnberg 45» |url=https://www.quotenmeter.de/n/166023/erinnerung-ist-keine-pflicht-sondern-verantwortung-katharina-stark-ueber-nuernberg-45 |access-date=21 May 2026 |work=Quotenmeter |date=8 November 2025 |language=German |trans-title="Remembrance is not a duty, but responsibility" – Katharina Stark on "Nuremberg 45"}}</ref> Stark said that "it's important to consider the social impact of the stories you tell".<ref name="Roxborough-2024" />

In 2024, Stark was awarded the European Shooting Star Award, a film award for up-and-coming young actors, for her performance in ''The Interpreter of Silence''. The judges of the award said that she played "an emotionally charged and demanding role with ease".<ref>{{cite news |title=Katharina Stark als «Shooting Star» ausgezeichnet |url=https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/unterhaltung/boulevard/katharina-stark-reiht-sich-in-die-liste-beruehmter-schauspielerinnen-und/64812432 |access-date=21 May 2026 |work=Ad Hoc News |date=19 February 2024 |language=German |trans-title=Katharina Stark named "Shooting Star"}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Schuster |first1=Barbara |title=Katharina Stark ist deutscher Shooting Star 2024 |url=https://the-spot-mediafilm.com/kino/european-shooting-stars-katharina-stark-ist-deutscher-shooting-star-2024-497a2f9a18b4468eda39812ce6bde8bb |access-date=21 May 2026 |work=The Spot |date=14 December 2023 |language=German |trans-title=Katharina Stark is German Shooting Star 2024}}</ref>

Stark has said that she would like to act in English-language productions, having only played parts in German films and series so far. She has also written scripts for several [[Short film|short films]], and is planning to write a feature-length film.<ref name="Roxborough-2024" /> Outside of acting, Stark studies [[health sciences]],<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kaulfersch |first1=Verena |title=Unterallgäuer Schauspielerin (18) startet durch |url=https://www.allgaeuer-zeitung.de/bayern/unterallgC3A4uer-schauspielerin-18-startet-durch-103404838 |access-date=21 May 2026 |work=Allgäeuer Zeitung |date=8 January 2017 |language=German |trans-title=Unterallgäuer actress (18) starts through}}</ref> and enjoys playing music and doing sports such as skiing and horse riding.<ref name="Kaulfersch-2016" />

'''Arianna Turturro''' (born July 25, 1990) is an American former actress, editor, and comic book writer known for her work on the [[DC Comics]] titles such as ''[[Poison Ivy (2022 comic book)|Poison Ivy]]'', ''[[Harley Quinn (comic book)|Harley Quinn]]'', ''[[Catwoman]]'', and ''[[Detective Comics]]''.<ref name="dup-0-48">{{Cite web |url=https://www.heroescomiccon.be/en/arianna-turturro/ |title=Arianna Turturro (DC) is heading to Heroes Comic Con 2024! |website=Heroes Comic Con |language=en |access-date=September 12, 2024 |date=August 27, 2024 |archive-date=September 13, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250913141017/https://www.heroescomiccon.be/en/arianna-turturro/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Early life ==
Turturro was born on July 25, 1990, in [[Los Angeles, California]].<ref name="dup-1-38">{{Cite web |url=https://www.comics.org/creator/24143/ |title=Arianna Turturro (n. 1990) |website=Grand Comics Database |language=en |access-date=September 12, 2025 |archive-date=January 11, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260111145047/https://www.comics.org/creator/24143/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Between 2008 and 2012, she studied at the [[School of Visual Arts]],<ref name="dup-1-38" /> graduating in [[cartooning]] and illustration.<ref name="dup-0-48" />

== Career ==
In 2012, Turturro founded the ''SVA INK Magazine'', a semi-monthly comics magazine run by students,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://inksva.com/new-page |title=About INK |website=INK Magazine |language=en |access-date=September 12, 2025 |archive-date=December 10, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251210200024/https://inksva.com/new-page |url-status=live }}</ref> and prior to 2014, she worked as a radio presenter, producer, and DJ at WFMU, an American radio station.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://theorg.com/org/dc-comics/org-chart/arianna-turturro |title=Arianna Turturro – Editor at DC Comics |website=The Org |language=en |access-date=September 12, 2025}}</ref>

She began working as an assistant editor for [[DC Comics]] in 2014, initially working within the [[Vertigo Comics|Vertigo]] and [[DC Black Label|Black Label]] imprints. In 2017, she was promoted to senior editor and in 2022, to associate senior editor.<ref name="dup-1-38" /> Beyond her work as an editor, she has also worked sporadically as a writer, publishing in titles such as ''Tis the Season to Be Freezin''',<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://batman-news.com/2021/12/14/tis-the-season-to-be-freezin-2021-1-review/ |title=Tis the Season to Be Freezin' (2021) #1 review |website=Batman News |language=en |access-date=September 12, 2025 |date=December 14, 2021 |archive-date=September 27, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230927222351/https://batman-news.com/2021/12/14/tis-the-season-to-be-freezin-2021-1-review/ |url-status=live }}</ref> as well as a [[Swamp Thing]] story published in the anthology ''DC: The Doomed and the Damned''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.cbr.com/swamp-thing-clayface-gotham-fight/ |title=Swamp Thing: Batman Villain Clayface Just Ripped the DC TV Hero Into Shreds |website=Comic Book Resources |language=en |access-date=September 12, 2025 |date=October 15, 2020 |archive-date=January 7, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260107114825/https://www.cbr.com/swamp-thing-clayface-gotham-fight/ |url-status=live }}</ref> She also wrote for the one-shot ''Gotham City Sirens: Uncovered'', published by DC Comics and focused on the [[Gotham City Sirens]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://freshcomics.us/creator/arianna-turturro |title=Ariana Turturro |website=Fresh Comics |language=en |access-date=September 12, 2025 |archive-date=September 13, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250913134508/https://freshcomics.us/creator/arianna-turturro |url-status=live }}</ref> in addition to the comic ''Catwoman: Uncovered'', published on August 29, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://comic-watch.com/news/the-sneak-peek-for-catwoman-uncovered-1-is-looking-good-feline-great |title=The Sneak Peek for CATWOMAN: UNCOVERED #1 is Looking Good, Feline Great |website=Comic Watch |access-date=September 13, 2024 |date=August 27, 2023 |archive-date=June 17, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250617194944/https://comic-watch.com/news/the-sneak-peek-for-catwoman-uncovered-1-is-looking-good-feline-great |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2025, she began editing the new [[Red Hood]] comic book series, written by [[Gretchen Felker-Martin]] and illustrated by Jeff Spokes, and aimed at readers over 17 years old.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.comicsbeat.com/red-hood-dc-all-in-ongoing-series/ |title=RED HOOD leaves Gotham in a new, Ages 17+ DC All In ongoing series |website=Comics Beat |language=en |access-date=September 13, 2025 |date=June 17, 2025 |archive-date=September 12, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250912184342/https://www.comicsbeat.com/red-hood-dc-all-in-ongoing-series/ |url-status=live }}</ref> However, the series was canceled by the publisher after the first issue was released due to Felker-Martin's statements about the [[assassination of Charlie Kirk]] via the [[Bluesky]] platform.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/dc-cancels-red-hood-comic-book-series-charlie-kirk-1236368576/ |title=DC Cancels 'Red Hood' Comic Book Series After Writer Shares Inflammatory Post Following Charlie Kirk Shooting |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en |access-date=September 13, 2025 |date=September 11, 2025 |archive-date=September 13, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250913133817/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/dc-cancels-red-hood-comic-book-series-charlie-kirk-1236368576/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Awards and recognition ==
Some of the works Turturro has worked on throughout her career have received various awards in the comic book industry. The ''[[Poison Ivy (2022 comic book)|Poison Ivy]]'' series by [[G. Willow Wilson]] and [[Marcio Takara]], published in Spanish as {{lang|es|Hiedra Venenosa}} and edited by Turturro, won a [[GLAAD Media Award]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ifema.es/madrid-comic-pop-up/autores |title=Autores Madrid Comic Pop Up {{!}} MADRID COMIC POP UP |access-date=September 13, 2025 |website=ifema.es |language=es}}</ref> Furthermore, the story ''Finding Batman'', also edited by Turturro and written by [[Kevin Conroy]], the renowned voice actor for [[Batman]], who narrated his struggles as a [[closeted]] [[gay man]] in the story, won an [[Eisner Award]] for Best Short Story.<ref name="dup-0-48" />

On March 8, 2024, Panini Comics Spain, part of the [[Panini Group]], highlighted her as one of the various influential women in the world of comics.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.facebook.com/story.php?story_fbid=1027775802720477&id=100064642001430 |title=La cuarta #8MWonders que destacamos es Arianna Turturro, actualmente editora en DC Comics. |website=Facebook |access-date=September 13, 2025 |date=August 3, 2024}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Arianna Turturro is a [[trans woman]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.lgbtqnation.com/2025/09/dc-comics-fires-trans-writer-cancels-red-hood-series-after-charlie-kirk-posts/ |title=DC Comics fires trans writer & cancels 'Red Hood' series after Charlie Kirk posts |website=LGBTQ Nation |access-date=June 7, 2026 |date=September 16, 2025}}</ref>

'''Alice Pignagnoli''' (born 14 March 1988) is an Italian professional footballer and manager who plays as a goalkeeper for Padova Woman.

==Club career==
Born in [[Reggio Emilia]],<ref name=":0" /> Pignagnoli approached football from an early age, first as an outfield player and, only around the age of 15, due to an injury to the starting goalkeeper of the Primavera team, she wore the number 1 shirt.

After her first experiences in mixed teams, Pignagnoli grew up as a footballer in the youth sector of Reggiana,<ref name=":0" /> with whose first team (which would then finish fourth in the [[Serie A Women|Serie A]] championship, gaining access to the [[UEFA Women's Champions League|UEFA Women's Cup]]) she would be aggregated for the first time in the 2004-2005 season, collecting two benches in the top division.

The following year she was included in the first team squad as a permanent third goalkeeper and played in the National Primavera championship as the starting goalkeeper.

In the 2006-2007 season, Pignagnoli was loaned to Galileo Giovolley in [[Serie B (women's football)|Serie B]], a team with which she played 21 matches out of 22 as a starter, finishing in third place, just a hair's breadth from promotion to Serie A2. From this moment on, Alice went on several loans around Italy, until her debut in Serie A with [[ACF Milan|Milan]] and her arrival at [[ASD Women Torres Calcio|Torres]],<ref name=":0" /> a team with which she also played in the Champions League and won an Italian Supercup (in 2011) and a Scudetto in 2012.<ref name=":0" />

In July 2019, after a year at Genoa Women and the consequent relegation to Serie B, Pignagnoli moved to Cesena, in the same category. However, at the beginning of December she suspended her football career, as she was pregnant.<ref name=":1" /> In agreement with the club, her employment contract was terminated (as indicated by the federation at the time), but with the guarantee of being able to benefit from a reimbursement for expenses.<ref name=":1" /> In the summer of 2020, while she was in the seventh month of pregnancy, Cesena renewed her contract, the first known case in Italian women's football.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> On 19 November of the same year, just 100 days after giving birth to her daughter Eva, she returned to the field in the [[2020–21 Coppa Italia (women)|Coppa Italia]] match against [[AC Milan Women|Milan]], losing 2-0.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> From that day onwards, she was always available, making 17 appearances as a starter in the rest of the championship.

In the summer of 2022, after being released for a short period, Pignagnoli reached an agreement with Lucchese, a Serie C club. The following October, she suspended her career again, after discovering her second pregnancy.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympics.com/en/news/italian-footballer-alice-pignagnoli-pregnant-inspiration-interview|title=Italian footballer Alice Pignagnoli on having her contract ended due to pregnancy and becoming a voice for change|first=Evelyn|last=Watta|publisher=Olympics.com|date=27 March 2024}}</ref> However, despite the support of the coach and her teammates,<ref name=":2" /> the club refused to pay the player the remaining monthly wages, going as far as to exclude her from the squad: after a few weeks, Pignagnoli decided to publicly denounce the incident.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> Lucchese, although finally agreeing to pay the goalkeeper's outstanding wages, denied her version of events.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lacasadic.com/news-serie-c/lucchese-pignaroli-caso-comunicato-22-dicembre-2022/|title=Lucchese, caso Pignagnoli: il comunicato del club sulla vicenda|website=La Casa di C|date=2022-12-22|access-date=2023-01-11}}</ref> In the meantime, among others, the MP [[Laura Boldrini]] intervenes in the case, presenting together with other colleagues an official parliamentary question to the [[Meloni government]],<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://aic.camera.it/aic/scheda.html?core=aic&numero=5/00183&ramo=CAMERA&leg=19|title=5/00183 : CAMERA - ITER ATTO|website=aic.camera.it|date=23 December 2022|access-date=11 January 2023}}</ref> and the management of Ternana, who offers to hire the player and cover her expenses.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ternanacalcio.com/stefano-bandecchi-alice-pignagnoli-siamo-disposti-a-prenderla/|title=Stefano Bandecchi: “Alice Pignagnoli? Siamo disposti a prenderla”|website=Ternana Calcio|date=23 December 2022|access-date=11 January 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://ternanacalcio.com/alice-pignagnoli-grazie-di-cuore-per-la-vicinanza-ternana-e-presidente-bandecchi-come-raggi-di-sole/|title=Alice Pignagnoli: “Grazie di cuore per la vicinanza, Ternana e presidente Bandecchi come raggi di sole”|website=Ternana Calcio|date=23 December 2022|access-date=11 January 2023}}</ref> In the meantime, Pignagnoli confirms her desire to leave the club in the following summer, taking advantage of a federal solidarity fund for maternity from February 2023 until the end of the season.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" />

On 30 December of the same year, Pignagnoli was officially signed by Ravenna, in Serie B.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bepitv.it/il-ravenna-women-si-prepara-al-riscatto-nel-nuovo-anno-e-ricerca-lesperienza-dal-mercato-ecco-i-tre-nuovi-acquisti/|title=Il Ravenna Women si prepara al riscatto nel nuovo anno e ricerca l’esperienza dal mercato: ecco i tre nuovi acquisti|author=Asia Di Palma|website=Be.Pi TV|date=30 December 2023|access-date=1 January 2024}}</ref>

On 22 September 2024, the newly formed club Pro Palazzolo Women officially presented Pignagnoli, participating in the Eccellenza Lombardia championship.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bepitv.it/pro-palazzolo-women-colpo-da-serie-a-ufficiale-lex-milan-e-torres-alice-pignagnoli/|title=Pro Palazzolo Women, colpo da Serie A: ufficiale l’ex Milan e Torres Alice Pignagnoli|website=Bet IPTV}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.calciofemminileitaliano.it/extra-time/pro-palazzolo-una-nuova-realta-che-saffaccia-nel-panorama-del-calcio-femminile-italiano/|title=Pro Palazzolo, una nuova realtà che s’affaccia nel panorama del calcio femminile italiano}}</ref>

==Managerial career==
In June 2023, Pignagnoli was hired as the new team manager of Beach Soccer Terracina, a team in the top division of the Italian beach soccer championship.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tuttocalciofemminile.com/alice-pignagnoli-nuova-team-manager-del-terracina-beach-soccer-sto-lavorando-per-creare-la-squadra-piu-competitiva-possibile/|title=Alice Pignagnoli nuova Team Manager del Terracina Beach Soccer: "Sto lavorando per creare la squadra più competitiva possibile"|author=Pierfrancesco Modica|website=Tutto Calcio Femminile|date=17 June 2023|access-date=17 June 2023|archive-date=17 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230617152733/https://tuttocalciofemminile.com/alice-pignagnoli-nuova-team-manager-del-terracina-beach-soccer-sto-lavorando-per-creare-la-squadra-piu-competitiva-possibile/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In 2010, Pignagnoli graduated in Communication Sciences at [[IULM University of Milan|IULM]] in Milan, with a thesis on the representation of women in the media, obtaining a grade of 110/110.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.minervaedizioni.com/autori/alice-pignagnoli.html|title=Alice Pignagnoli|website=www.minervaedizioni.com|access-date=2024-11-21}}</ref>

She is the mother of two children, born in 2020 and 2023 respectively.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.gazzetta.it/calcio/calcio-femminile/21-12-2022/alice-pignagnoli-portiere-lucchese-sono-incinta-club-non-mi-paga-piu-4501632635527.shtml|title=Alice Pignagnoli, portiere della Lucchese, denuncia: "Sono incinta, il club non mi paga più"|website=[[La Gazzetta dello Sport]]|date=21 December 2022|access-date=11 January 2023|language=it}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{cite web|url=https://www.raiplaysound.it/audio/2021/03/Alice-Pignagnoli-incinta-di-sette-mesi-e-contratto-da-calciatrice-rinnovato-de2e39a2-c38c-4166-a3b5-0be6a432ba53.html|title=Alice Pignagnoli, incinta di sette mesi e contratto da calciatrice rinnovato {{!}} Non è un Paese per Giovani|website=[[RaiPlay]] Sound|date=29 March 2021|access-date=11 January 2023|language=it}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{cite web|url=https://sport.sky.it/calcio/2022/12/24/alice-pignagnoli-lucchese-intervista|title=Alice Pignagnoli: 'Noi senza tutele, sogno un mondo diverso per i miei figli'|author=Fabrizio Moretto|website=[[Sky Sport]]|date=24 December 2022|access-date=11 January 2023|language=it}}</ref>

In February 2023, Pignagnoli published her autobiography, entitled ''I Just Wanted to Be a Footballer'', where she recounts her journey of struggle and emancipation both in life and in her football career. The volume features a preface by Laura Giuliani.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.minervaedizioni.com/volevo-solo-fare-la-calciatrice.html|title=Volevo solo fare la calciatrice|website=www.minervaedizioni.com|language=it|access-date=2024-11-20}}</ref>

'''Clara Alvarado Bermudo''' (born 2 July 1990) is a Spanish actress, singer and nurse. She became known for playing Ariadna Cascales in the first two parts of the crime series ''[[Money Heist]]'' (''La casa de papel''), returned to work as a nurse in March 2020 during the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]], and in 2023 played the singer [[Rocío Dúrcal]] in the biographical series ''[[Untameable]]'' (''Cristo y Rey''). She was a founder of the pop duo Biuti Bambú.<ref>{{cite web |title=¿Quién es Clara Alvarado? Conoce a la actriz que interpreta a Rocío Dúrcal en 'Cristo y Rey' |trans-title=Who is Clara Alvarado? Meet the actress who plays Rocío Dúrcal in 'Cristo y Rey' |url=https://www.europafm.com/noticias/tv-cine/quien-clara-alvarado-conoce-actriz-que-interpreta-rocio-durcal-cristo-rey_2023011663c596a73c81f20001d8975b.html |website=Europa FM |language=es |date=16 January 2023 |access-date=20 August 2026}}</ref>

== Early life ==

Clara Alvarado Bermudo was born on 2 July 1990<ref>{{cite web |title=Clara Alvarado |url=https://www.sensacine.com/actores/actor-805226/biografia/ |website=SensaCine |language=es |access-date=20 August 2026}}</ref> in [[Navalmoral de la Mata]], in the [[Province of Cáceres]]. Both her parents worked in healthcare, and from the age of eight she attended the local music school, where she studied clarinet and sang in the choir.<ref>{{cite web |last=Marcos |first=Miguel Ángel |title=Una morala en 'Cuéntame' |trans-title=A Navalmoral girl in 'Cuéntame' |url=https://www.hoy.es/v/20111109/sociedad/morala-cuentame-20111109.html |website=Hoy |language=es |date=9 November 2011 |access-date=20 August 2026}}</ref> She moved to Madrid to study nursing, and during the degree an offer to appear in a short film led her to acting. She made her film debut in the 2012 short ''Almohada''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Clara Alvarado, Premio Woman Extremadura Actriz: cuando el éxito empieza en la autenticidad |trans-title=Clara Alvarado, Woman Extremadura Actress Award: when success begins with authenticity |url=https://woman.elperiodico.com/lifestyle/clara-alvarado-premio-woman-extremadura-actriz-124140989 |website=Woman |language=es |access-date=20 August 2026}}</ref>

== Career ==

=== Stage ===

After finishing a degree in dramatic art in 2013, Alvarado appeared in the musical ''Jekyll y Hyde''. In August 2015 she played Íole in ''Hércules, el musical'', directed by Ricard Reguant and staged at the [[Roman Theatre (Mérida)|Roman Theatre of Mérida]] during the city's classical theatre festival.<ref>{{cite web |last=Marcos |first=Miguel Ángel |title=Clara Alvarado triunfa en el Festival de Teatro de Mérida con 'Hércules' |trans-title=Clara Alvarado triumphs at the Mérida Theatre Festival with 'Hércules' |url=https://www.hoy.es/prov-caceres/201508/21/clara-alvarado-triunfa-festival-20150821000200-v.html |website=Hoy |language=es |date=21 August 2015 |access-date=20 August 2026}}</ref>

=== Television and film ===

Alvarado's early television work included a small role in ''[[Cuéntame cómo pasó]]'' and the part of Raquel, a new student, in the second season of the youth series ''Yo quisiera''.<ref>{{cite web |last=García |first=María |title=Comienza el rodaje de la segunda temporada de 'Yo quisiera', la serie juvenil de Divinity |trans-title=Filming begins on the second season of 'Yo quisiera', the Divinity youth series |url=https://www.formulatv.com/noticias/60990/estreno-yo-quisiera-divinity/ |website=FormulaTV |language=es |date=3 November 2016 |access-date=20 August 2026}}</ref> She played Ariadna Cascales, one of the hostages, in the first two parts of ''[[Money Heist]]'' (''La casa de papel''), which reached a global audience through [[Netflix]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Biuti Bambú, dos voces femeninas para tiempos de resiliencia |trans-title=Biuti Bambú, two female voices for times of resilience |url=https://elpais.com/espana/madrid/2021-08-16/biuti-bambu-dos-voces-femeninas-para-tiempos-de-resiliencia.html |website=El País |language=es |date=16 August 2021 |access-date=20 August 2026}}</ref>

In 2023 she played the singer [[Rocío Dúrcal]] in ''[[Untameable]]'' (''Cristo y Rey''), the [[Atresplayer]] biographical series about Ángel Cristo and [[Bárbara Rey]]. Her episodes recreated the 1977 film ''Me siento extraña'', in which Dúrcal and Rey played two women who fall in love, with [[Belén Cuesta]] as Rey.<ref>{{cite web |title=Clara Alvarado: 'Meterme en la piel de Rocío Dúrcal fue un reto. Su historia con Bárbara Rey fue arriesgada' |trans-title=Clara Alvarado: 'Getting into Rocío Dúrcal's skin was a challenge. Her story with Bárbara Rey was risky' |url=https://www.elespanol.com/corazon/famosos/20230321/clara-alvarado-meterme-rocio-durcal-barbara-rey/750175035_0.html |website=El Español |language=es |date=21 March 2023 |access-date=20 August 2026}}</ref>

In 2024 she joined the cast of ''[[La Moderna]]'', the daily afternoon drama of [[La 1 (Spanish TV channel)|La 1]], as Mercedes Morel, the sister of César Morel, played by [[Miguel Ángel Muñoz]].<ref>{{cite web |title='La Moderna' recibe a nuevos personajes |trans-title='La Moderna' welcomes new characters |url=https://www.rtve.es/rtve/20240829/moderna-recibe-a-nuevos-personajes/16230413.shtml |website=RTVE |language=es |date=29 August 2024 |access-date=20 August 2026}}</ref>

== Nursing ==

Both of Alvarado's parents are nurses; she graduated in nursing from the [[Complutense University of Madrid]] in 2012 but never practised, and when the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain|COVID-19 pandemic reached Spain]] she joined a small centre caring for elderly people in the [[Community of Madrid]], where her work included palliative care.<ref>{{cite web |last=Guerra |first=Andrés |title=Clara Alvarado, del mono de 'La casa de papel' a la bata de enfermera |trans-title=Clara Alvarado, from the 'Money Heist' jumpsuit to the nurse's gown |url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/gente/20200326/48103205974/clara-alvarado-mono-casa-papel-bata-enfermera.html |website=La Vanguardia |language=es |date=26 March 2020 |access-date=20 August 2026}}</ref>

She started on 25 March 2020, during the state of alarm declared over the coronavirus, and said she felt an ethical and moral duty to help at a time when protective equipment was scarce.<ref>{{cite web |last=García |first=Silvia |title=Clara Alvarado, de 'La casa de papel', se quita la careta de Dalí para ponerse el traje de enfermera |trans-title=Clara Alvarado, from 'Money Heist', takes off the Dalí mask to put on the nurse's uniform |url=https://www.abc.es/play/series/noticias/abci-clara-alvarado-casa-papel-quita-careta-dali-para-ponerse-traje-enfermera-202003271144_noticia.html |website=ABC |language=es |date=27 March 2020 |access-date=20 August 2026}}</ref> She announced the decision on Instagram with a message to her father, a nurse who had just retired: "Tú te jubilas y yo me incorporo" ("You retire and I sign up"), and explained that nursing had always been her "plan B" but had become her "plan A".<ref>{{cite web |title=Actriz de 'La casa de papel' retoma su carrera de enfermera para ayudar en la pandemia de coronavirus |trans-title='Money Heist' actress resumes her nursing career to help in the coronavirus pandemic |url=https://www.univision.com/famosos/actriz-de-la-casa-de-papel-retoma-su-carrera-de-enfermera-para-ayudar-en-la-pandemia-de-coronavirus-fotos |website=Univision |language=es |date=2 April 2020 |access-date=20 August 2026}}</ref> The job was the first time she had practised nursing; she said the aim of every shift was to go home feeling she had done all she could to improve her patients' health.<ref>{{cite web |title=La finalidad de cada jornada era volver a casa con la sensación de que habías hecho todo lo que podías por mejorar la salud de los pacientes |trans-title=The aim of every day was to go home feeling you had done everything you could to improve the patients' health |url=https://www.enfermeria21.com/diario-dicen/la-finalidad-de-cada-jornada-era-volver-a-casa-con-la-sensacion-de-que-habias-hecho-todo-lo-que-podias-por-mejorar-la-salud-de-los-pacientes/ |website=Diario Enfermero |language=es |date=13 July 2020 |access-date=20 August 2026}}</ref>

Days into the job she admitted she was afraid of infection: staff received one mask per day and she had bought her own surgical caps online. Her father, who had asthma, was proud of her decision.<ref>{{cite web |last=Taibó |first=Marieta |title=Clara Alvarado ('La casa de papel') y su lucha como enfermera contra el coronavirus: 'Tengo miedo al contagio' |trans-title=Clara Alvarado ('Money Heist') and her fight as a nurse against the coronavirus: 'I'm afraid of contagion' |url=https://www.cosmopolitan.com/es/famosos/peliculas-series/a31951351/clara-alvarado-la-casa-de-papel-enfermera-entrevista/ |website=Cosmopolitan |language=es |date=27 March 2020 |access-date=20 August 2026}}</ref> Alvarado remained in nursing for two and a half years, until September 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Clara Alvarado: 'Cuando se empezó a emitir 'La Casa de Papel' subía 20.000 seguidores al día' |trans-title=Clara Alvarado: 'When Money Heist started airing I was gaining 20,000 followers a day' |url=https://www.elespanol.com/treintayseis/economia/talento-rebelde/20231209/clara-alvarado-empezo-emitir-casa-papel-subia-seguidores-dia/815918557_0.html |website=El Español |language=es |date=9 December 2023 |access-date=20 August 2026}}</ref>

== Music ==

Alvarado and Iciar Segovia formed the pop duo Biuti Bambú, a project they said was born on the rooftop of a concert among friends. They presented the group in February 2020 at the Café Comercial in Madrid, where the room was full, and they recorded their first single separately at home during the coronavirus lockdown; a second single followed in July 2020. At the time Alvarado was working eight-hour hospital shifts and gave her afternoons to the band.<ref>{{cite web |last=Rivera |first=Miguel |title=Biuti Bambú |url=https://www.rocktotal.com/entrevista-grupo-biuti-bambu-con-clara-alvarado-iciar-segovia/ |website=RockTotal |language=es |date=24 July 2020 |access-date=20 August 2026}}</ref> The duo, whose members described their sound as "pop fronterizo", released its first album in the winter of 2022–23 and presented it in Cáceres in April 2023.<ref>{{cite web |title=Biuti Bambú, el grupo musical de la actriz cacereña Clara Alvarado, en Boogaloo Club |trans-title=Biuti Bambú, the musical group of Cáceres actress Clara Alvarado, at the Boogaloo Club |url=https://www.regiondigital.com/noticias/cultura/378455-biuti-bambu-el-grupo-musical-de-la-actriz-cacerena-clara-alvarado-en-boogaloo-club.html |website=Región Digital |language=es |date=27 April 2023 |access-date=20 August 2026}}</ref>
